items.title: Últimas noticias de la Asamblea General de la ONU, en directo | Trump amenaza con “aniquilar” Irán si no hay pacto, pero augura un acuerdo tras las elecciones de noviembre
items.description: El presidente de EE UU, Donald Trump , ha amenazado una vez más con “aniquilar” Irán si no logra un acuerdo con el régimen de los ayatolás que incluya su renuncia al arma nuclear y la apertura del estrecho de Ormuz . Pese a la amenaza, ha augurado que ese acuerdo llegará después de las elecciones de medio mandato, que se celebran el próximo 3 de noviembre y que pintan mal para Trump y su partido republicano. “Tengo que tomar una gran decisión. Pactar con Irán un acuerdo que les permita reconstruir y hacer un mejor país o aniquilar a la República islámica. ¿Les mando al infierno sin posibilidad de supervivencia y sin esperanza de grandeza o generaciones futuras? Creo que lograremos un pacto después de las elecciones”, ha dicho en un discurso triunfalista con su legado y en el que ha atacado también al Tribunal Penal Internacional. También ha augurado que Cuba “caerá” y ha defendido el desarrollo sin restricciones de la IA (superinteligencia, la ha llamado). Antes, el secretario general de la ONU, António Guterres , ha abogado por que la inteligencia artificial sea “moldeada por la humanidad, con la humanidad y para toda la humanidad”, así como un “desarrollo responsable” del fenómeno para que ningún país quede atrás. “Los robots asesinos no tienen lugar en nuestro futuro”, ha alertado en su último discurso como líder de Naciones Unidas. También ha pintado un sombrío retrato del presente, con “grietas” que “se han convertido en abismos”, “derechos humanos pisoteados” y “derecho internacional ignorado”. Por su parte, el presidente brasileño, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva , ha afirmado que la ONU está fallando en su misión de proteger a los más vulnerables de las guerras. “Este es sin duda el momento mas crítico para las Naciones Unidas”, ha dicho. items.title: Security forces thwart terrorists' attempt to infiltrate Pak-Afghan border in Kurram: security sources
items.description: Security forces foiled an attempt by terrorists to cross into Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Kurram from Afghanistan and also effectively responded to firing by the Afghan Taliban, security sources said on Tuesday. According to the sources, the terrorists tried to infiltrate the border from Nangarhar and Paktia in Afghanistan. They identified the terrorists as those belonging to Fitna-al-Khawarij — a term that the state uses for the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan. When the attempt was thwarted, the Afghan Taliban began firing on Pakistani checkposts on the border, the sources said, adding that the firing was unprovoked. In retaliation, Pakistani troops targeted multiple checkposts of the Afghan Taliban and their defensive positions, the sources said. They added that several Afghan Taliban operatives fled the posts as a result of the retaliation. According to the sources, security forces were constantly monitoring the border situation and remained prepared to respond to any aggression. More to follow

items.title: Reports of petroleum levy being 'central point' in IMF programme are 'misleading': finance ministry
items.description: The finance ministry issued a rebuttal on Tuesday, saying that reports of the petrol development levy (PDL) being a “central point” of Pakistan’s ongoing programme with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) were “misleading”. The programme includes a $7 billion Extended Fund Facility (EFF) and a $1.1bn Resilience and Sustainability Facility (RSF). On Tuesday, an Express Tribune report said the “finance ministry had made petroleum levy the central point of the programme, although there is no explicit condition in the IMF document about the rate of the levy. As a result, the government has managed to improve fiscal numbers but it fueled inflation, unemployment, poverty and low economic growth”. The finance ministry, referring to the report in a statement, termed the assertions “misleading” and said the programme’s fiscal strategy was “substantially broader and revolves around FBR revenue mobilisation, expansion of tax base, provincial taxation, expenditure rationalisation etc”. For FY27, the ministry said, the programme specifically emphasised additional revenue mobilisation and strengthening FBR performance rather than relying solely on petroleum taxation. “PDL is one of the revenue instruments and describing it as center piece of program materially overstates its role,” the ministry said. It also argued that the assertion of there being “no IMF conditionality relating to petroleum levy pricing” was “technically narrow and potentially misleading”. “While the programme does not prescribe a single permanent headline PDL rate in the manner suggested, published programme documents contain explicit details concerning petroleum pricing and levies. These include alignment of domestic fuel prices with international prices through regular adjustments. The RSF also included a specific reform measure introducing a supplementary carbon levy through the PDL framework. “Thus, petroleum pricing policy forms part of the agreed programme framework, rather than being a unilateral fiscal strategy developed solely by the Finance Division,” it said. The ministry also took exception to the linking of inflation, unemployment, poverty and low economic growth to the levy and said the assertion was “analytically incorrect and attributes broad macroeconomic outcomes to a single fiscal instrument”. “Pakistan’s inflation and growth outcomes reflect multiple factors, importantly prevailing geo-political situation along with domestic and international commodity prices, exchange-rate movements, monetary conditions, fiscal imbalances, external financing constraints and global shocks,” it added. Moreover, the ministry said, the report mentioned that it had kept “tight control” over the IMF programme’s design and negotiations, “which caused problems such as commitments about the agriculture sector and focusing too much on fiscal stabilisation”. The inference was made in connection with a statement by Planning Minister Ahsan Iqbal, who was quoted as saying that he had “recommended to the prime minister that a representative of the Planning Commission should also be included in the team that will negotiate with the IMF”. But, the programme was a “whole-of-government programme, not a Finance Division programme”, it said in its rebuttal. The assertion did “not accurately reflect the institutional arrangements underlying Pakistan’s IMF programme. IMF’s EFF and RSF facilities encompass reforms and commitments falling within the mandates of multiple federal and provincial institutions, including Finance Division, Planning Commission/ Ministry of Planning, Ministry of Energy, provincial governments, Federal Board of Revenue, State Bank of Pakistan and other relevant stakeholders”. The relevant ministries and institutions participated and led technical discussions, including benchmarks setting relating to their respective mandate, the ministry said. Seemingly referring to the conclusion derived in The Express Tribune ’s report that there had been “criticism from government circles and independent experts about viewing the financing facility only in relation to fiscal numbers”, the ministry said the programme was “demonstrably not confined to numbers or fiscal targets”. “The Finance Division fully recognised that macroeconomic stabilisation was a means towards sustainable and inclusive economic growth. Even, the published IMF programme explicitly encompasses growth-enhancing structural reforms, social protection, governance, energy sector efficiency, climate resilience and reduction of distortions in economy. “The latest IMF staff report specifically states that policy discussions focused on accelerating reforms to support stronger growth, while protecting vulnerable households,” it argued. The ministry also contended that fiscal stabilisation could not be separated from growth. “Pakistan entered the programme with limited fiscal and external buffers and significant financing requirements. Restoring fiscal sustainability, rebuilding reserves and reducing refinancing risks are necessary conditions for durable private investment and growth. “The IMF’s third-review documents record that fiscal consolidation contributed to reducing macroeconomic imbalances and demand pressures, supported disinflation, and external-sector stabilisation through reserve build-up and recovery in overall growth numbers,” it said. The ministry also asserted that it has not pursued fiscal consolidation without social safeguards, and supported the programme to incorporate explicit floors and commitments for social protection. Giving multiple examples in this connection, the ministry further stated that the latest targeted fuel-subsidy programme is another initiative to “protect vulnerable households through targeted, temporary and fiscally sustainable interventions, rather than untargeted subsidies that create large fiscal liabilities”. “Sovereign debt is contingent on fiscal imbalance, and in last financial year, debt growth has been limited to lowest levels in two decades,” it said. The ministry also said that agriculture-related commitments were not exclusively with the Finance Division. “Agricultural income taxation, for instance, is constitutionally and administratively a provincial responsibility, and implementation necessarily involves provincial governments. Any assessment of these reforms should therefore distinguish between programme coordination by the Finance Division and constitutional/ administrative responsibilities of the relevant governments and institutions.” It concluded its statement saying that a “clear distinction needs to be maintained between the Finance Division’s responsibility for overall programme coordination, and agreement on benchmarks with the IMF leading to policymaking, legislative and implementation responsibilities of respective federal ministries and provincial governments”. “The appropriate policy debate is therefore not ‘stabilisation versus growth’, but how to transition from stabilisation towards sustainable growth without any fiscal and external imbalances that necessitated reverting to IMF stabilisation programmes, as witnessed in the past,” it said.

items.title: Journée internationale de la paix : Le gouvernement invite chaque citoyen à être un artisan de la paix
items.description: Lomé, 22 sept. (ATOP) – Le gouvernement a invité, dans un communiqué publié, le lundi 21 septembre à Lomé, chaque citoyen à être un artisan de la paix dans son environnement à l’occasion de la journée internationale de la paix. Cette journée instituée par la communauté internationale vise à sensibiliser et mener des actions en faveur de la préservation de la paix et de la prévention des conflits. Le communiqué a rappelé la conception du Président du Conseil, Faure Gnassingbé sur la paix lors du Forum de Lomé sur la sécurité. « La paix ne signifie pas l’absence de guerre… La paix durable se construit dans le dialogue, la paix ne se décrète pas, elle se construit par l’inclusion et par la cohésion sociale ». Cette déclaration du Président du Conseil indique que la paix est une construction permanente qui exige de chaque citoyen un engagement individuel et collectif où qu’il se trouve. Les Togolaises et togolais sont invités à semer la paix en famille, sur les lieux de travail, sur les espaces publics, dans les écoles et centre de formation par la recherche du dialogue au sein des communautés, par la pratique de la justice sociale et par la réconciliation là où subsistent des tensions communautaires. Au nom de la politique d’inclusion et de cohésion sociale que prône le Président du Conseil, le gouvernement s’attelle à favoriser, pour tous, un accès équitable aux services publics, à l’éducation, à la santé et à l’emploi pour un mieux-vivre partagé. « La construction de la paix trouve également sa place dans nos écoles et sur nos lieux de travail. Elle exige le savoir vivre, l’écoute des autres, le respect de nos différences et la recherche de solutions pacifiques lorsque la concorde vient à être menacée », souligne le message du gouvernement. Le gouvernement invite les parents, les éducateurs, les chefs de communauté, chacune et chacun, à transmettre aux jeunes et aux enfants la culture de la paix. Selon les termes du communiqué, nos différences de langues, de pratiques religieuses ou d’opinions ne doivent jamais constituer une menace pour la paix. Nous devons nous attacher à promouvoir une éducation citoyenne à la démocratie et à la paix par un choix judicieux des mots. « Dans l’espace public comme sur les réseaux sociaux, refusons les discours de haine, les rumeurs et les provocations qui blessent, divisent et fragilisent la confiance », conseille le gouvernement. Le communiqué demande aux Togolais de préserver les acquis du Président du Conseil en matière de recherche de la paix et de la sécurité dans la sous-région. ATOP/HKM/AJA

items.title: Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway to be closed for all types of traffic from 11pm on Wednesday
items.description: Islamabad police on Tuesday issued an advisory stating that the Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway (M-1) will be closed to all types of traffic from 11pm on September 23 (Wednesday). “Those travelling from the twin cities of Islamabad and Rawalpindi, and from other areas, should avoid using the M-1 and postpone non-essential travel,” the advisory, posted on the social media platform X, said. The advisory noted that the M-2 Motorway between Lahore and Islamabad will remain open to all types of traffic, and urged motorists to take this information into consideration when planning their journeys. The development came amid a planned long march to Islamabad by the PTI for the release of party founder Imran Khan, which is scheduled to take place on Sept 27 (Sunday). Police have already set up around 2,000 containers around the federal capital and at Attock Bridge, an entry point from Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and northern parts of the country. On Monday, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had warned the PTI against its Sept 27 long march, urging the party to refrain from proceeding with the protest. “We have clearly told them (PTI) that they can never achieve anything through such drama, and I will say again that there is still time; they should not go into this situation,” Naqvi said during a press briefing, advising the party to “not enter a dead-end street”. The interior minister vowed the government will not “leave any loopholes” in its response if the party went ahead with the protest. It should be mentioned that the Jamaat-i-Islami, which had also announced a long march to Islamabad against the petroleum levy, said on Tuesday it was postponing it at the request of Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, pending a meeting with him.

items.title: Kpélé : Le personnel soignant du CHP d’Adeta bénéficie de nouvelles tenues professionnelles
items.description: Adéta, 22 sept. (ATOP)- Les différents corps soignants du Centre hospitalier préfectoral (CHP) d’Adéta ont bénéficié, le lundi 21 septembre, de nouvelles tenues professionnelles. Ces uniformes ont été offerts par le ministère en charge de la Santé. Cette dotation vise à faciliter l’identification des différentes catégories professionnelles par les patients et les usagers de l’hôpital. Les tenues ont été conçues selon un code vestimentaire permettant de distinguer les différentes spécialités. Elles contribuent également à renforcer la visibilité et l’image professionnelle des différents corps qui concourent à la prise en charge des usagers. Les infirmières et infirmiers portent une tenue blanche à rayures bleues, tandis que les sages-femmes sont reconnaissables à leur tenue rose rayée. Les médecins portent une tenue blanche, alors que les agents d’entretien sont vêtus de rouge bordeaux. Le directeur préfectoral de la santé de Kpélé, Dr Messanvi Amblasso, a déclaré que ces uniformes constituent non seulement un outil pratique d’identification, mais également un signe de reconnaissance des différentes fonctions exercées au sein de l’hôpital. « La dotation de cet habit n’est pas seulement un simple vêtement. C’est plutôt notre protection, notre sécurité et le symbole de notre engagement pour la santé de la population », a-t-il indiqué. Le préfet de Kpélé, Mme Blewoussi Ablavi Metsokewo, a souligné que la force du travail réside également dans la tenue ou l’uniforme, qui constitue un socle de visibilité du personnel soignant. Elle a félicité le corps sanitaire pour les efforts consentis en faveur du bien-être de la population. ATOP/SKD/MD

items.title: With Tinubu, Shettima abroad, who is running Nigeria – ADC asks
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike The African Democratic Congress, ADC, on Tuesday questioned who is exercising Nigeria’s presidential powers as President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Vice-President Kashim Shettima remain outside the country. The opposition party said Tinubu’s absence had crossed the 21-day period referenced in Section 145 of the Constitution, raising questions over whether the constitutional procedure for transferring presidential functions had been followed. In a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Mallam Bolaji Abdullahi, the ADC asked whether Tinubu had transmitted the required written declaration to the President of the Senate and Speaker of the House of Representatives. “President Tinubu left Nigeria on 30 August and has now been away for more than 21 days. We therefore demand to know whether the required declaration was transmitted by the President. If he did not, we would like to know why the National Assembly has ignored Section 145 of the Constitution,” the ADC said. The party also rejected the Presidency’s description of Tinubu’s trip as a ‘working vacation’, saying the Secretary to the Government of the Federation, Senator George Akume, could not assume presidential powers by representing the President at official engagements. “Representing the President at events and ceremonies does not confer constitutional powers. The Secretary to the Government of the Federation is a mere appointee of the President. He may attend events or deliver speeches on the President’s behalf, but he cannot exercise the constitutional powers of the President or Acting President,” it said. The ADC said the President’s absence could not be addressed through official representation or remote communication. “Representation is not governance. Attendance at official functions is not presidential authority. Nigeria cannot be governed through ceremonial proxies, telephone calls and press statements issued from foreign capitals,” the party said. It further argued that calling the trip a ‘working vacation’ did not remove Tinubu’s constitutional obligations. “There is no constitutional category known as a ‘working vacation’. Presidential authority cannot be transferred by convenience, protocol or press statement. Nigeria is a constitutional democracy, not a private enterprise to be managed remotely from a holiday destination,” the ADC said. The party said the simultaneous absence of Tinubu and Shettima was particularly troubling as Nigerians grappled with insecurity, unemployment and rising living costs. Turning to the President’s stay in France, the ADC also criticised Tinubu for remaining in Paris while French President Emmanuel Macron was in New York attending the United Nations General Assembly. “The irony would be amusing if it were not a national disgrace. At a time when world leaders are advancing their countries’ interests at the United Nations General Assembly, Nigeria’s President is holed up in the French capital while his host has left to pursue his own country’s national interest,” the party said. The ADC said the situation was ‘not merely poor optics’ but ‘a national embarrassment’, arguing that Tinubu could not remain in Paris after Macron had left for New York to represent France at the UN. The party ultimately challenged the Presidency and National Assembly to clarify who currently exercises the powers of the Nigerian President. “Who presently exercises the constitutional powers of the President of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, and under what provision of the Constitution?” the ADC asked. The post With Tinubu, Shettima abroad, who is running Nigeria – ADC asks appeared first on Vanguard News .

ONU: les grands enjeux mondiaux au cœur de la 81e Assemblée générale à New York
items.description: La 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies s'est ouverte, ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 à New York. Près de 130 chefs d’État et de gouvernement sont attendus pour le débat général, prévu jusqu’au 28 septembre, sur fond de conflits internationaux, de crise climatique, de gouvernance de l’intelligence artificielle et de défis pour le multilatéralisme. La diplomatie mondiale a les yeux tournés vers New York. Le débat général de la 81e session de l’Assemblée générale des Nations Unies s’est ouvert, ce mardi 22 septembre 2026, avec la présence annoncée de près de 130 dirigeants mondiaux. Cette séquence de haut niveau se poursuivra jusqu’au 28 septembre, donnant lieu à une succession d’allocutions, de réunions et d’entretiens bilatéraux. Placée sous la présidence du Bangladais Khalilur Rahman, la session est articulée autour du thème: «Restaurer la confiance, gérer la transformation: Des Nations Unies qui apportent des résultats pour tous». L’agenda de la présidence met, notamment, l’accent sur la paix et la sécurité, le développement durable, l’action climatique, les droits humains, l’innovation et la réforme du système multilatéral. Guerres, climat et intelligence artificielle au menu Les conflits internationaux figurent parmi les principales préoccupations des dirigeants réunis dans la capitale américaine. Les crises au Moyen-Orient ainsi que la guerre russo-ukrainienne occupent une place importante dans les discussions, alors que l’ONU cherche à promouvoir le dialogue et les solutions politiques. Le changement climatique et la transition écologique constituent également un autre axe majeur. Une réunion de haut niveau consacrée à l’action climatique et à la transition juste est prévue le 23 septembre, avec la participation des pays développés, de grandes économies, des pays vulnérables ainsi que des principaux producteurs et consommateurs d’énergie. La gouvernance de l’intelligence artificielle et, plus largement, des technologies numériques figure également parmi les dossiers suivis durant cette semaine diplomatique. La présidence de l’Assemblée générale entend notamment promouvoir une gouvernance de l’IA fondée sur les données scientifiques, inclusive et attentive aux risques liés aux inégalités, à la surveillance et aux usages abusifs des technologies. Lula, Trump et Macron donnent le ton Les premières interventions de cette journée ont déjà placé les débats sur le terrain des rapports de force internationaux. Le secrétaire général de l’ONU, António Guterres, a donné le coup d’envoi des allocutions de haut niveau. Le président brésilien Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva a ensuite défendu la coopération internationale tout en rejetant l’idée d’«interventions» extérieures pour répondre aux défis auxquels sont confrontés les États. Le président américain Donald Trump a, pour sa part, livré un discours centré notamment sur les menaces qu’il associe aux intérêts américains dans l’hémisphère occidental. Il a affirmé que les États-Unis étaient prêts à recourir à leur «puissance militaire» pour défendre leurs intérêts face à des menaces liées à des implantations étrangères dans cette région. Arrivé à New York dès le 21 septembre, Emmanuel Macron s’est également entretenu avec Donald Trump dans le cadre de cette séquence diplomatique. Selon les éléments communiqués, les échanges entre les deux dirigeants ont été qualifiés de «très constructifs». La France défend parallèlement au Conseil de sécurité une résolution visant à garantir la liberté de navigation dans le détroit d’Ormuz. Une semaine de diplomatie intense Après l’ouverture du débat général ce 22 septembre, le programme prévoit, le 23 septembre, une réunion de haut niveau consacrée à l’action climatique et à la transition juste. Les séances plénières se poursuivront ensuite jusqu’au 28 septembre, parallèlement à de nombreuses rencontres bilatérales et discussions diplomatiques. Au-delà des discours officiels, cette semaine constitue ainsi un important moment de concertation entre dirigeants, dans un contexte international marqué par les conflits, les urgences climatiques et les transformations technologiques. L’enjeu affiché par la présidence de l’Assemblée générale sera de «restaurer la confiance» et de renforcer la capacité de l’ONU à produire des réponses collectives aux crises mondiales. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article ONU: les grands enjeux mondiaux au cœur de la 81e Assemblée générale à New York est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

items.title: Government must answer how 80 bags of cocaine passed through Ghana’s ports – Miracles Aboagye
items.description: The Director of Communications aspirant of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Dennis Miracles Aboagye, has challenged the government to explain how large quantities of cocaine were able to pass through Ghana’s ports without detection. He said the issue should be treated as a national security concern rather than reduced to a political blame game. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, Mr Aboagye said the reported drug seizures linked to Ghana over the past 18 months raise serious questions about the effectiveness of security checks at the country’s ports and airports. “We are talking about twelve major drug busts in 18 months under this government. The question that remains unanswered is how did anybody move such a quantity of cocaine, which is almost like about 80 bags of cement in a container, through our port without anybody seeing, sighting, or noticing this?” he asked. His comments follow the reported seizure of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine at the Port of Dunkirk in France in September 2026. The drugs, estimated to be worth €225 million, were reportedly concealed in a container carrying plastic waste shipped from Ghana. The Narcotics Control Commission subsequently announced the arrest of three people in connection with the consignment. The incident followed the seizure of 866 parcels of substances suspected to be cocaine at a warehouse within the Tema Harbour enclave on August 5, 2026. The consignment, reportedly valued at $6.9 million, was allegedly concealed in sacks of gari. According to him, several of the major consignments were intercepted outside Ghana after passing through the country’s ports. “Most of these busts, those with major, the huge sums, were arrested outside the country after the cocaine had gone through the ports,” he said. Mr Aboagye said the government must provide answers instead of pointing to similar incidents under previous administrations. “If you don’t have an answer to that question and your response is that a certain government that has gone and has left, has been voted out, also did same, so what should we do with that information?” he asked. He warned that Ghana’s reputation and the treatment of Ghanaian travellers could be affected if the country is increasingly associated with international drug trafficking. “If we don’t deal with this matter… you will get to Heathrow Airport, you will get to an airport in Paris, and you will spend three, four hours simply because you have a Ghanaian passport,” Mr Aboagye stated.

items.title: Ghana Women’s Movement announces protest over alleged intimidation of women
items.description: The Ghana Women’s Movement has announced plans to stage a demonstration in Accra on Tuesday, September 29, 2026, to demand greater protection for women’s rights, freedom of expression and political participation. Dubbed the “Women’s Voices Matter Demonstration”, the protest will bring together women from political parties, markets, salons, dressmaking shops, offices and households. Male sympathisers have also been invited to participate. In a statement issued on Tuesday, September 22 and signed by its convener, Janet Asana Nabla, the movement expressed concern about what it described as the increasing intimidation, arrest, remand and imprisonment of Ghanaian women over the exercise of their right to free expression. “Women cannot remain silent while other women are arrested, detained and imprisoned for speaking their minds,” the group said. It maintained that women had the constitutional right to express their opinions, participate in politics, criticise the government and demand accountability without fear of intimidation or arrest. “We will not accept a situation where women are made to feel that speaking their minds comes at the price of intimidation, arrest or imprisonment,” the statement added. As part of the demonstration, the movement said it would present a petition to Vice President Professor Naana Jane Opoku-Agyemang, outlining its concerns and demands concerning dignity, equality, freedom of expression, women’s empowerment and equal treatment. The group is also demanding the full implementation of the Affirmative Action (Gender Equity) Act, 2024, particularly provisions intended to increase women’s representation and participation in decision-making. “We do not want promises. We want implementation,” it declared. The movement further called for enhanced economic opportunities for Ghanaian women, including improved access to capital, employment and support for businesses. The demonstration is scheduled to begin at 6 am at Opera Square in Accra. The conveners include Janet Asana Nabla, Chairperson of the People’s National Party; Betty Akuffo Amoabeng, Chairperson and Leader of the National Democratic Party; Elizabeth Sam, running mate of the Liberal Party of Ghana; and Akosua Asaa Manu, Advisor on Gender and Social Protection to the New Patriotic Party’s flagbearer. Others include Grace Akosua Amoabeng, spokesperson for the Gender and Social Protection Committee, as well as representatives of market women, hairdressers and dressmakers. GHANA WOMEN Download

items.title: ‘I was waiting for the list to believe my Black Stars call-up was real’- Ronald Donkor
items.description: Ronald Donkor says he had to wait for the official announcement before believing he had earned his first Black Stars call-up. The young m was midfielder was named in Carlos Queiroz’s squad for Ghana’s upcoming 2027 Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, marking his first invitation to the senior national team. Donkor revealed that he spoke to Alex before the squad was officially announced but remained unsure until he saw his name on the list. “When I finished speaking to Alex, I was still waiting for the list to be published so I could believe it was true,” Donkor said. The call-up fulfils a childhood ambition for the youngster, who says representing Ghana has always been one of his biggest dreams. “It’s been my dream to play for the National team [Black Stars]. Every Ghanaian player wants to play for the national team and wear the national colours.” Donkor said his first reaction after receiving the call-up was to share the moment with his mother, who was delighted by the news. “When I received the call-up, I called my mother, and she was happy.” The opportunity will also allow Donkor to reunite with two players he knows from his time at JMG Academy. He is particularly looking forward to meeting Alidu Seidu and Augustine Boakye, who were his seniors during their time at the academy. “I want to meet my fellow Black Stars teammates, Alidu Seidu and Augustine Boakye, because they were my seniors back in JMG Academy.” With his first senior international opportunity now secured, Donkor is aware of the expectations that come with playing for Ghana. The youngster says he understands the passion of Ghanaian football fans and is determined to use the opportunity to continue developing his game. “I know Ghanaians love their football. My friends used to call me Agogo, but right now, I want to play and improve.” Donkor will now look to make the most of his first experience with the Black Stars as Ghana prepare for their 2027 AFCON qualifying campaign.

items.title: The ICE Officer in Austin Wasn’t Wearing a Body Cam
items.description: T he ICE officer who shot a Venezuelan man last weekend in Austin, Texas, was a recent hire who was not wearing his body camera, three officials at the Department of Homeland Security with knowledge of the incident told me. The officer, who has not been publicly identified, was hired last year, according to two of the officials, but he previously worked for another federal law-enforcement agency, one of the officials said. The officials were not authorized to discuss the investigation into the shooting, which left Wilber Rafael Garcés Pérez with a bullet lodged in his upper torso, according to his attorney. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officials have rushed to distribute body-worn cameras to officers since the fatal shootings in July of a Mexican construction contractor in Texas and a Colombian delivery driver in Maine. Officers making arrests are required to have the cameras at all times. The agency has directed officers to activate the devices prior to engaging in enforcement activity, the three officials said, and ICE instructs them to stop recording only when the incident has safely concluded. Officers who do not follow these instructions are required to submit a written statement to their supervisors and could face possible disciplinary action, the three officials said. DHS and ICE public-affairs officials did not immediately respond to questions about the incident in Austin and whether the officer will face consequences. On Sunday, the officer was working with a partner who was driving in a separate vehicle. That second officer had a body-worn camera that was turned on, two officials told me. The officers were checking license plates using a system that helps them find targets for arrest using commercial databases and federal immigration files. When they ran the plates from the blue Toyota Corolla driven by Garcés Pérez, the officers saw he had an outstanding deportation order from an immigration judge. The ICE officers, who were driving unmarked vehicles, attempted to pull Garcés Pérez over, but he drove away, nearly striking one of the officers, according to one of the DHS officials. The official said the incident was recorded by the body camera of the ICE officer’s partner. The officers followed Garcés Pérez in their vehicles. The officer without the body camera found Garcés Pérez, and attempted to detain him. When Garcés Pérez attempted to drive away again, that officer pulled his gun and fired, striking Garcés Pérez in the back, both of the officials told me. A bystander video recorded just after the shooting shows an officer wearing a cap and a face covering standing next to the Corolla speaking with Garcés Pérez, who clutches at the wound on his back and winces in pain. [ Read: ICE has quietly changed its deadly-force rule ] G arcés Pérez, 28, briefly received medical treatment for the gunshot wound, then was taken to an ICE detention center southwest of Austin. As his attorney, Kate Lincoln-Goldfinch, gathered with supporters and journalists at a news conference yesterday, Garcés Pérez addressed the crowd by phone and with the help of a translator. “I have not received the medical attention that I require,” Garcés Pérez said. Lincoln-Goldfinch said that Garcés Pérez was taken out of the hospital after just four hours and then had to sleep on the floor of the detention center. She said he was moved to a hospital after reporting “left-side paralysis” and severe pain. “He should have stayed in the hospital all of this time,” she told CNN. Representative Joaquin Castro of Texas, a Democrat, said this morning that Garcés Pérez had been transferred back to the ICE detention center. Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client has a valid driver’s license and was making deliveries for DoorDash when ICE attempted to stop him and rammed his car. She said Garcés Pérez entered the United States legally in 2024 through the CBP One program, which allowed asylum seekers to enter the country and pursue asylum claims through a “parole” program offered by the Biden administration. President Trump canceled that program, so if Garcés Pérez did not obtain another form of legal-immigration status, he would be potentially subject to ICE arrest. Lincoln-Goldfinch said her client was issued a deportation order because his court documents were sent to the wrong address. “I see this all the time in my practice and it’s a mistake we can easily correct. It does not justify shooting people in the street,” Lincoln-Goldfinch wrote in a social-media post. The Trump administration launched a hiring spree at ICE last year to add 10,000 deportation officers and more than double the number of personnel deployed on U.S. streets. The officer who fatally shot the Colombian immigrant Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Maine was also a new hire. Veteran officers at ICE have repeatedly shared their concerns with me about the qualifications and competence of new recruits, especially those sent through a fast-track training course in which classroom hours were cut by more than half. ICE has ended the fast-track program for new hires, but one senior ICE official told me that a large number of the officers the agency recruited have since been disqualified or let go. [ Read: The education of Markwayne Mullin ] ICE arrests increased this summer to 50,000 a month, the highest levels ever recorded by the agency, which remains under intense White House pressure to carry out 1 million deportations a year. After Durán Guerrero’s killing, DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin ordered a pause on most vehicle stops by ICE officers, citing the need to finish distributing body cameras and improve officer training. But Trump reversed that order a day later, after immigration-enforcement hard-liners protested. ICE training instructs officers that the use of deadly force against a fleeing suspect is not permissible unless there is an imminent risk of harm to law-enforcement personnel or the public. DHS’s inspector general is investigating the fatal shooting of Durán Guerrero in Maine as well as the killing of 52-year-old Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston on July 7. The findings from those investigations have not been released.

items.title: 'Terrific man' Shehbaz gets special mention during Trump's UNGA speech
items.description: United States President Donald Trump on Tuesday called Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif a “terrific man” during his address to the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) as he once again mentioned his role in ending the Pakistan-India conflict in May 2025 . During a speech that covered the conflict in Iran, artificial intelligence and criticism of the UN, Trump once again listed conflicts that he had played a role in ending. “Since I took office, it has been my honour to help settle eight wars, and in so doing, become friendly with the leaders of many of those countries,” Trump said. “It was a great honour to do it,” he added. He highlighted that he had been able to settle these conflicts via his “great relations”, as well as the use of tariffs. Listing off the countries, he noted “Pakistan and India” as a conflict he settled, alongside Thailand and Cambodia, Armenia and Azerbaijan, and the Gaza conflict, among others. He noted that almost all of these countries had written him letters of thanks for his role. “The prime minister of Pakistan — terrific man — said that Donald Trump was responsible for saving 30 million lives and probably many more than that,” he added. Tensions between India and Pakistan had flared in April 2025 when a deadly terror attack on tourists in occupied Kashmir was, without evidence, blamed on Islamabad, which strongly refuted the allegations. The two sides traded a series of tit-for-tat blows that ended in May with the declaration of a ceasefire by Trump, who has since repeatedly talked about his role in ending the military escalation between the two countries. He has also praised Chief of the Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir on several occasions, calling him a “ highly respected general ”, a “ great fighter ” and “ my favourite ”. Trump warns he could ‘annihilate’ Iran without peace deal Trump also used his speech to argue that the war with Iran prevented Tehran from obtaining a nuclear weapon and warn that he could “annihilate the Islamic Republic” if no deal is reached to end the conflict. While predicting his administration would strike a peace deal with Iran following the November 3 US midterm elections, Trump called on other nations to join America in isolating Iran economically to force it to the negotiating table. “I have a big decision to make. Will a deal be made with Iran that lets them rebuild and create a far greater country than it ever was before?” Trump said. “Or do I annihilate the Islamic Republic and do it quickly, never giving them a chance to kill and destroy people and countries again?” Trump added: “Do I drive them into hell with no chance of survival and no hope of future greatness or generations? But I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election.” The remarks marked the latest justification Trump has offered for the war with Iran. He has previously cited a range of reasons for the February US-Israeli strikes, including Tehran’s nuclear programme, its support for regional proxy groups and the prospect of regime change. Iran has consistently denied seeking to develop nuclear weapons. “I believe we’ll make a deal right after the election because it doesn’t make sense for them not to. They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election,” Trump said in his speech. “I call on all nations to help to enforce the complete economic isolation of Iran,” he said. Calls for all nations to quit ‘rogue institution’ ICC During his address, the US president also called for all nations that are part of the International Criminal Court to quit the body, calling it “out of control”. “The United States is equally opposed to the out-of-control institution known as the International Criminal Court,” he said. “I call on all nations that are members of the ICC to officially resign from this rogue institution immediately,” he added. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has vowed to dismantle the ICC “brick by brick”, describing the court as an “intolerable threat to US sovereignty”. The body tries individuals for the world’s worst crimes. Washington has imposed a series of sanctions on ICC officials, furious at the court’s issuance of an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu — a close US ally. Trump said Washington would “never allow US service members or anyone else to be investigated or given show-trials by an anti-American tribunal with no jurisdiction over us”. The United States is not an ICC member and has never ratified the Rome Statute that established the court. Israel, Russia and China are also not members. Rejects international regulation of AI Addressing the General Assembly, Trump firmly rejected calls for international supervision of artificial intelligence, calling them a “globalist scheme” to control the new technology. He also announced that the US government would henceforth use the term “super intelligence” rather than “artificial intelligence” in its communications, hoping that the world would follow suit. “It sounds much better” and “it’s much more accurate”, he added, musing on whether the rest of the world would adopt the term. Trump also dismissed warnings from AI safety advocates, comparing them to warnings about climate change , whose human causes are affirmed by the overwhelming consensus of the scientific community. “Every major new technology brings challenges, and super intelligence is no exception,” he said. “The very same people who said we’ll all be dead in 12 years because of global warming… are now saying that AI is going to kill us all, that robots are going to attack us, and that everything is going to be a total disaster.” Ahead of the week of meetings and speeches in New York, leaders of more than 20 countries urged binding safety measures for advanced artificial intelligence, warning that the technology’s development could outpace the ability to control it. AI superpowers China and the US are not signatories. Trump told the UN that the “United States totally rejects any attempt to construct a globalist scheme to control… artificial intelligence”. UN chief Antonio Guterres, meanwhile, called for the US and China to start a dialogue on the technology’s future akin to US-Soviet engagement at the height of the Cold War. “Governments with the greatest AI capabilities have the greatest responsibilities to humanity, to establish channels for dialogue, transparency, trust and cooperation,” Guterres said in his address to the assembly. “At a pivotal moment during the Cold War, strategic rivals came to recognise the need to manage shared existential risks.” China and the US are currently discussing creating a communication channel for AI concerns in anticipation of a Washington summit meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. Both powers confront rising fears that increasingly capable artificial intelligence systems could eventually escape human control, even as they race for technological supremacy. Trump has come out strongly against AI safety measures, vowing on Saturday not to allow the “destruction” of the AI industry, a major driver of the US economy, over what he calls unjustified fears. China’s President Xi Jinping in July said artificial intelligence should not be dominated by a single country and urged international cooperation on its development.

items.title: Mahama has ordered NACOC back into port container inspections – Tanko-Computer
items.description: The Deputy Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko-Computer, says President John Mahama has ordered the Narcotics Control Commission (NACOC) to return to the inspection of containers and other goods at the ports. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse , he said the directive forms part of the government’s measures to strengthen Ghana’s fight against drug trafficking. Mr Tanko-Computer said NACOC had previously been removed from the inspection of containers and other goods under the former New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration. “The President has ordered that NACOC should immediately be part of that inspection division…You remember 2018, this group of people, NPP government, sat down and decided that NACOC should not be part of inspecting this in containers and other goods which were exiting the country,” he said. He questioned the rationale behind the decision and said the current administration had moved to restore NACOC’s role in the inspection process. According to him, NACOC’s renewed involvement has contributed to arrests linked to narcotics trafficking. “NACOC is doing fantastic. Based on NACOC, a lot have been arrested,” he added. He said the government had prioritised national security to prevent Ghana from being used as a transit point for illicit drugs.

items.title: Photos: Vice President joins ECOWAS Parliament, calls for stronger regional cooperation
items.description: Vice President Jane Naana Opoku-Agyemang has called for stronger regional cooperation and increased investment in communities to help West African countries respond to the growing effects of climate change. She made the call in Accra today, September 22, when she joined the ECOWAS Parliament for the joint opening of its Second Extraordinary Session and Second Parliamentary Seminar of 2026. The session was held under the theme, “Climate Change as a Driver of Environmental Degradation, Population Displacement and Growing Insecurity in the ECOWAS Region.” The Vice President noted that the impact of climate change is increasingly being felt across West Africa through disrupted livelihoods, population displacement and growing insecurity. She said the challenges cut across national boundaries and therefore require a coordinated regional response. According to her, greater cooperation among ECOWAS member states, coupled with investment in vulnerable communities, is necessary to help populations withstand and recover from the effects of climate-related pressures. She stressed that protecting livelihoods and strengthening food security should not only be viewed as development priorities but also as essential measures for promoting peace and stability across the region. The Vice President further highlighted the role of the ECOWAS Parliament in ensuring that regional integration translates into tangible benefits for citizens. She said the success of regional integration should be reflected in how easily citizens can move, trade, work and pursue opportunities across West Africa. Vice President Opoku-Agyemang also linked Ghana’s commitment to regional integration to the country’s historical Pan-African vision, citing the contribution of Osagyefo Dr Kwame Nkrumah and successive governments to the integration agenda. She reaffirmed Ghana’s commitment to efforts aimed at building a more united, integrated and prosperous West Africa. See more photos below:

items.title: Osun Assembly passes resolution on state police
items.description: By Shina Abubakar, Osogbo The Osun State House of Assembly on Tuesday passed the resolution in support of the creation of State Police. Recall that the National Assembly passed a State Police Creation amendment bill on June 24, 2026, before passing it to the States Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval. The House, in its plenary on Tuesday, after a motion for the consideration of the bill was moved by the Majority Leader, Mr Babajide Kofoworola and seconded by Mr Tajudeen Adeyemi, approved the proposed bill. The Speaker of the Assembly, Adewale Egbedun, in his remarks, said the approved amendment of the House should be forwarded to the National Assembly for consideration. The State Police Creation Amendment Bill is before the 36 State Houses of Assembly for consideration and approval before the bill is returned to the National Assembly for final approval. The approved bill will then be passed to the President to be assented and pave the way for the creation of State Police in line with the directives of President Bola Tinubu. The post Osun Assembly passes resolution on state police appeared first on Vanguard News .
