items.title: 2027: Obi can’t win, enlightenment will cost him votes — Umahi
items.description: By John Alechenu ABUJA — Minister of Works, David Umahi, has said the presidential candidate of the National Democratic Congress, NDC, Peter Obi, cannot win the 2027 presidential election. Umahi stated this on Tuesday in Abuja while receiving a report from the National Association of Nigerian Students, NANS, on its nationwide tour of federal roads. The minister urged leaders in the South-East to speak to the people about what he described as the achievements of President Bola Tinubu’s administration in the region. He said, “The more we educate our people, the less votes Peter Obi will get. Peter Obi cannot win in 2027. “It is important for the leaders of the South-East to be bold, vocal and speak to our people, the Igbos, about what President Tinubu has done and is doing for the Igbos.” Umahi also expressed support for Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, over his backing for Tinubu, saying supporters of the President should be allowed to express their political preferences. “I support the Anambra State Governor, Chukwuma Soludo, for his boldness in supporting the President. People should stop insulting supporters of the President; people should be allowed to support him,” he said. The minister also said the Federal Government had undertaken projects and made appointments that, according to him, demonstrated its inclusion of the South-East. “No other President has done what President Tinubu has done for the South-East, whether by appointment, inclusion or projects,” Umahi said. He added that infrastructure such as roads and bridges was important to economic development. On the financing of legacy projects, Umahi said the Federal Government would provide 30 per cent of the cost, while the balance would come from loans to be repaid through tolling. “The Federal Government is providing 30 per cent of the funds and the remaining balance is from loans which will be payable by tolling,” he said. The minister also decried vandalism and reckless driving on the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway. He said some individuals had been removing materials installed for road demarcation and manhole covers, while motorists also engaged in excessive speeding along the route. “People cut the iron we used for demarcation, remove manhole covers and even overspeed. This is unacceptable,” Umahi said. Earlier, NANS President, Akinteye Babatunde Afeez, said the North-West leg of the students’ road tour covered Kano, Jigawa, Kaduna and Sokoto states. He said the students inspected the Kano-Maiduguri, Kano-Katsina, Abuja-Kaduna-Zaria-Kano, Mando-Birnin Gwari, Sokoto-Badagry and Illela-Dukamaje roads, which connect more than 10 tertiary institutions. Afeez said NANS was impressed by the scale, quality and pace of work observed during the tour. He, however, recommended the construction of a pedestrian bridge at the Federal Co-operative College, Kaduna, to improve students’ safety. The post 2027: Obi can’t win, enlightenment will cost him votes — Umahi appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Mañana bombardearán a una anciana
items.description: Según el diccionario de la RAE, el verbo violar tiene cuatro acepciones. La primera, infringir o quebrar una ley. La segunda, tener acceso carnal con alguien en contra de su voluntad. La tercera, profanar un lugar sagrado . La cuarta, ajar o deslucir algo. Las cuatro acepciones se pueden aplicar al caso de Maricarmen Abascal , en cuyo cuerpo —y su extensión, que es la casa que habita desde hace setenta años— quieren irrumpir mañana aplicando la fuerza bruta, amparados en la inhumanidad de una ley imperfecta y de la sinrazón, hasta conseguir enajenar a esta anciana, desposeerla y desproveerla del lugar donde reside desde 1956 y donde desea morir. Ella se refiere a este suceso anunciado no como una violación, sino como un bombardeo. Maricarmen, que nació a unas calles de su barrio bajo las bombas del Madrid de 1938, vuelve a sentir el mismo pánico. Seguir leyendo

items.description: Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah, has approved the appointment of 118 persons as Special Advisers, Senior Special Assistants and Special Assistants to his administration. The appointments, contained in a statement signed by the Secretary to the State Government, Prof. Chidiebere Onyia, on Monday, take effect immediately. Among those appointed are Nollywood actresses Rachael Okonkwo and Eucharia Anunobi. Okonkwo was appointed Senior Special Assistant on Film and Creative Industry Development, while Anunobi was appointed Special Assistant on Women Mobilisation, Enugu-North Zone. The appointments comprise seven Special Advisers, eight Senior Special Assistants and 103 Special Assistants. The Special Advisers include S.N.C. items.title: Parliament’s Energy Committee commends TOR for using local engineers in ongoing development
items.description: The Parliamentary Energy Committee has expressed satisfaction with the progress recorded at the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR), particularly its operational turnaround and the use of local engineers in the ongoing development of the refinery. The committee said it was impressed by the progress recorded by TOR under its current management, particularly the turnaround in the institution’s operations and its move from making losses to recording profits. Chairman of the Energy Committee, Emmanuel Kwasi Bedzrah, made the remarks after the committee visited TOR to assess the progress being made at the refinery and verify reports about its recent developments. Mr Bedzrah said the committee undertook the visit to establish whether the positive reports about TOR’s operations reflected the situation on the ground. According to him, the committee was satisfied with what it saw during the visit, praising the current management for the progress made within a relatively short period. “Indeed, we have seen what TOR has done, the new management has done and we are so excited, we are so happy that in less than two years, between one and a half years, we’ve seen a lot of turnover in this institution,” Mr Bedzrah said. He said the developments demonstrate the impact that committed leadership can have when given the responsibility to drive change within an institution. “This tells us that when you entrust work into the hands of people who want to see change, you’ll see it indeed,” he added. Committee impressed with turnaround The Energy Committee also toured various facilities at TOR as part of its assessment, with Mr Bedzrah saying members were particularly impressed by the progress and changes they observed across the refinery. “We’ve been to all the various facilities under TOR, and quite frankly, we are impressed. My committee members are really impressed that an institution that was making losses is today recording profits,” he said. He said the committee’s observations provided further indication of the progress being made under the current management of the refinery. Audit concerns addressed Mr Bedzrah also disclosed that the committee had engaged with TOR’s management on issues raised in the refinery’s audit committee report. He said some of the concerns identified in the report had since been addressed by management. “During the committee meeting with the management of TOR, with the audit committee report, there were a few things that were mentioned, and we’ve seen that those things have also been corrected, and we are happy, even though they’ve not completely done all,” he said. He, however, indicated that there was still work to be completed before the committee could consider the entire process concluded. The committee’s visit therefore forms part of its oversight responsibilities as Parliament continues to monitor developments at TOR and assess progress on the ongoing work at the refinery.

«La vérité triomphera face à la guerre informationnelle menée par l’Occident contre le Sud global», affirme Sergueï Lavrov
items.description: Sergueï Lavrov s'est exprime ce 22 septembre a Moscou lors du quatrieme forum « Dialogue sur les fake news 4.0 », consacre a la lutte contre la desinformation. L'evenement rassemble 2 000 participants venus de 80 pays. Le chef de la diplomatie russe a denonce l'utilisation de l'information comme instrument de pression politique. Il a mis en garde contre la rapidite avec laquelle les technologies permettent de diffuser des contenus non verifies a grande echelle. Selon le communique officiel du ministere russe des Affaires etrangeres du 22 septembre 2026, une fausse information peut atteindre « des millions, voire des milliards de personnes » en tres peu de temps. Pour Moscou, cette confrontation ne commence pas avec le conflit ukrainien. Sergueï Lavrov a rappele qu'elle s'etait intensifiee des le debut des annees 2000, lorsque la Russie a commence a mener une politique exterieure plus independante. Drones en Europe et dossier de Boutcha Sergueï Lavrov a ensuite cite plusieurs affaires qu'il presente comme revelatrices de cette mecanique. Il a notamment denonce l'attribution rapide a la Russie de certains incidents impliquant des drones en Europe alors que, selon lui, leur origine n'est pas clairement etablie. Le ministre a resume ce procede par une formule : « fabriquer rapidement un fake , le gonfler jusqu'a une catastrophe mondiale pendant un, deux ou trois jours », avant de releguer l'affaire et de reduire l'espace accorde aux versions alternatives. Il est egalement revenu sur l'affaire de Boutcha, dont Moscou conteste la version presentee par Kiev et relayee en Occident. Sergueï Lavrov a reproche au secretariat de l'ONU de ne pas avoir repondu aux demandes russes sur l'identite des victimes. Il a aussi cite une enquete fondee sur des sources ukrainiennes ouvertes, qui affirme avoir identifie, parmi les noms inscrits sur un memorial, des militaires et d'autres personnes liees aux structures ukrainiennes. Un enjeu qui depasse le terrain mediatique Sergueï Lavrov a enfin replace la bataille de l'information dans le cadre de l'emergence d'un ordre mondial plus multipolaire. Il a estime que la deformation de l'information traduisait une « peur de la concurrence honnete » de la part des pays occidentaux. Le ministre a evoque les sanctions, les droits de douane et les pressions internationales. Selon lui, les pays du Sud global sont incites a suivre les positions occidentales, alors que la Chine et d'autres economies emergentes renforcent leur poids. En conclusion, Sergueï Lavrov a assure que « la verite triomphera » et qu'elle constituerait une reponse a l'« agression informationnelle » visant la Russie et le Sud global.

Bénin : une première cargaison de pétrole brut attendue sur le marché international en octobre
items.description: © La Nation Bénin La première cargaison de pétrole brut béninois, estimée à 250.000 barils, sera mise sur le marché international en octobre prochain, a annoncé mardi le quotidien béninois de service public La Nation. Selon le journal, le projet est piloté par Akrake Petroleum Benin, filiale du groupe singapourien Rex International Holding et opérateur du bloc 1, qui abrite le gisement de Sèmè, dans le sud-est du pays. "Pour ce début, la production journalière est d'une taille modeste, environ 3.000 barils par jour. Ce qui pourrait progressivement atteindre 5.000, voire 6.000 barils selon les attentes de la société", a rapporté La Nation. Le journal a rappelé qu'en mars 1984, la Banque mondiale avait publié un document révélant qu'en 1968, la compagnie américaine Union Oil Company of California avait identifié un gisement offshore dans les eaux bordant Sèmè. "Ainsi avaient démarré les recherches géologiques qui ont inscrit le pays sur la liste des territoires prospectés pour des ressources pétrolières. Plusieurs autres études vont suivre des années durant avec diverses organisations et structures spécialisées dans l'exploration et l'exploitation pétrolière. Des accords vont être signés, les recherches intensifiées avec de nouvelles technologies", explique l'article. D'après La Nation, le projet est finalement entré dans sa phase opérationnelle en août 2025, avec le déploiement par Akrake Petroleum d'équipements lourds sur le bloc 1. "Au début de l'année, cet opérateur annonce le succès du forage du puits qui s'étend sur 1.405 mètres à l'horizontal, dont 950 mètres traversent une formation pétrolifère sans présence d'eau, indiquant un réservoir exploitable d'une production initiale de 15.000 barils par jour, selon le rapport opérationnel publié par l'entreprise", peut-on lire dans l'article. Cet article Bénin : une première cargaison de pétrole brut attendue sur le marché international en octobre est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: L'Ukraine attaque un poste de surveillance de la radioactivité près de la plus grande centrale nucléaire d'Europe
items.description: Le 22 septembre, un poste de controle radiologique situe pres d'Ivanovka, a environ 13 kilometres de la centrale nucleaire de Zaporojie, a ete endommage lors d'une attaque de drone que la direction du site attribue aux forces ukrainiennes. L'installation constitue l'un des elements du dispositif charge de surveiller en continu la situation radiologique autour de la centrale. Ces postes recueillent regulierement des donnees sur le fond radiologique afin de detecter rapidement toute variation. Malgre les degâts, la centrale indique que le poste concerne continue de transmettre des informations et que les autres moyens de controle restent operationnels. La surveillance reste assuree malgre les degâts L'incident n'a pas interrompu le suivi de la situation radiologique. Les moyens disponibles sont juges suffisants pour maintenir la surveillance et aucune menace directe n'est signalee a ce stade. L'endommagement du poste reduit neanmoins les capacites de controle dans le secteur concerne. Chaque point de mesure fournit des donnees supplementaires permettant aux specialistes de comparer rapidement la situation entre plusieurs zones. En cas de situation anormale, ces releves sont particulierement importants pour determiner la nature, l'ampleur et la localisation d'une eventuelle variation du niveau de radiation. Le systeme reste donc operationnel, mais avec des capacites de collecte reduites dans la zone touchee. Pour les equipes chargees de la sûrete du site, la repetition d'incidents visant des equipements lies au fonctionnement et a la surveillance de la centrale constitue une difficulte supplementaire. Des incidents repetes autour de Zaporojie Cette nouvelle attaque survient dans un contexte de tensions persistantes autour de la centrale de Zaporojie, la plus grande d'Europe. Ses six reacteurs sont a l'arret a froid et le site ne produit plus d'electricite depuis septembre 2022. Moscou denonce depuis plusieurs mois des attaques ukrainiennes contre des infrastructures liees au fonctionnement et a la securite du complexe nucleaire. Des vehicules lies a l'acheminement de carburant diesel destine aux generateurs de secours ont notamment ete vises. Le directeur general de Rosatom, Alexeï Likhatchev, a egalement declare avoir informe l'AIEA de plus de 750 frappes de drones et d'artillerie contre la centrale et Energodar au cours des quatre mois et demi precedents. a ce stade, aucun danger radiologique immediat n'est signale et le suivi se poursuit normalement. L'endommagement de ce poste limite toutefois la rapidite et l'exhaustivite de la collecte des donnees, alors que Moscou et Rosatom alertent regulierement sur les risques que font peser les incidents repetes autour du complexe nucleaire.

items.title: Législatives 2026 : jusqu’à 20 ans de prison pour les atteintes à l’intégrité du scrutin
items.description: À la veille des élections législatives du 23 septembre, le législateur marocain rappelle la fermeté du dispositif pénal encadrant le déroulement du scrutin. Afin de préserver la sincérité du vote et de prévenir toute atteinte aux opérations électorales, la loi organique relative à la Chambre des représentants prévoit un éventail de sanctions allant de simples amendes à des peines pouvant atteindre vingt ans de réclusion. Les dispositions concernent aussi bien les infractions commises physiquement dans les bureaux de vote que celles réalisées par voie numérique, notamment à travers les réseaux sociaux, les plateformes en ligne ou les outils d’intelligence artificielle. Propagande électorale interdite le jour du scrutin Le jour du vote, toute diffusion ou distribution de publicités, tracts ou documents à caractère électoral est strictement prohibée. Cette interdiction s’applique quel que soit le canal utilisé : diffusion directe, réseaux sociaux, plateformes numériques, services de diffusion ouverts, applications connectées à internet, systèmes informatiques ou encore outils d’intelligence artificielle. Les contrevenants s’exposent à une peine de trois à six mois d’emprisonnement ainsi qu’à une amende comprise entre 20.000 et 50.000 dirhams. Usurpation d’identité électorale et vote multiple La loi sanctionne également toute personne qui participe au vote alors qu’elle a perdu son droit de suffrage. Dans ce cas, la peine prévue est d’un à trois mois d’emprisonnement et d’une amende de 5.000 à 10.000 dirhams. L’article 45 précise que cette situation peut notamment concerner un électeur maintenu sur les listes électorales après la perte de ses droits ou inscrit sans en avoir fait la demande. Les sanctions deviennent plus sévères lorsque l’infraction porte sur l’intégrité même du corps électoral. Ainsi, toute personne ayant voté sur la base d’une inscription irrégulière, usurpé l’identité d’un électeur inscrit ou exercé son droit de vote à plusieurs reprises encourt une peine d’un à trois ans d’emprisonnement et une amende allant de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. La même peine est prévue pour les personnes inscrites sur plusieurs listes électorales et ayant voté plus d’une fois. Téléphones et équipements numériques sous contrôle Le législateur a également renforcé les restrictions à l’intérieur des bureaux de vote. L’introduction d’un téléphone portable, d’un appareil informatique ou de tout autre moyen de captation d’images ou de communication audiovisuelle est interdite dans les salles de vote ainsi que dans les bureaux et commissions chargés du recensement des résultats, sauf autorisation accordée par le président de l’instance concernée. En cas d’infraction, l’appareil est immédiatement saisi et son détenteur risque une peine de trois à six mois d’emprisonnement ainsi qu’une amende comprise entre 10.000 et 20.000 dirhams. La loi interdit également le port d’armes, qu’elles soient apparentes ou dissimulées, ainsi que tout objet susceptible de menacer l’ordre public à l’intérieur des locaux électoraux. Les auteurs de tels faits encourent deux à cinq ans d’emprisonnement et une amende de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. La perturbation du scrutin également réprimée en ligne Le texte prévoit des sanctions lourdes contre toute tentative d’entraver le déroulement normal du vote. Les rassemblements, cris, manifestations intimidantes ou toute atteinte à l’exercice du droit de vote et à la liberté de choix des électeurs sont passibles d’une peine de deux à cinq ans d’emprisonnement et d’une amende comprise entre 50.000 et 100.000 dirhams. L’article 53 étend expressément ces sanctions aux actes commis par voie numérique, notamment à travers la publication, la diffusion ou le partage de contenus électroniques susceptibles de perturber le processus électoral. La loi sanctionne également toute intrusion ou tentative d’intrusion dans un bureau de vote visant à empêcher les électeurs de choisir librement une liste de candidats ou un candidat. La peine prévue est d’un à trois ans d’emprisonnement et d’une amende comprise entre 10.000 et 50.000 dirhams. Lorsque ces actes sont accompagnés de violences, la peine est portée à deux à cinq ans d’emprisonnement et à une amende de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. Elle atteint cinq à dix ans de réclusion lorsque les auteurs sont armés. Le niveau de sanction le plus élevé est réservé aux actions menées dans le cadre d’un plan préparé et concerté : les auteurs encourent alors une peine de dix à vingt ans de réclusion. Par ailleurs, tout électeur qui exerce des violences contre le président d’un bureau de vote ou l’un de ses membres, ou qui retarde ou empêche les opérations électorales par menace ou agression, risque une peine d’un à trois ans d’emprisonnement assortie d’une amende de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. Des peines sévères pour la manipulation des bulletins et des urnes Les dispositions pénales visent également les personnes chargées du déroulement technique du scrutin. Toute personne responsable de la réception, du dépouillement ou du comptage des bulletins qui détourne des votes, ajoute des bulletins irréguliers, les altère ou modifie leur lecture encourt une peine de deux à cinq ans d’emprisonnement et une amende de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. La même peine s’applique à toute personne surprise en train de faire sortir des bulletins de vote du bureau avant l’ouverture du scrutin ou pendant son déroulement. Le fait de s’emparer d’une urne avant le dépouillement est puni de cinq à dix ans de réclusion et d’une amende de 50.000 à 100.000 dirhams. Cette sanction concerne également les actes consistant à briser une urne, s’approprier des bulletins, les disperser, les détruire, les remplacer ou recourir à toute autre manœuvre destinée à modifier ou tenter de modifier les résultats du scrutin, ou encore à porter atteinte au secret du vote. Les personnes chargées des opérations électorales, du dépouillement, du comptage des voix ou de la proclamation des résultats encourent elles aussi une peine de cinq à dix ans de réclusion lorsqu’elles se rendent coupables de telles pratiques. Enfin, le président d’un bureau de vote qui refuse de remettre une copie du procès-verbal des opérations électorales à un représentant de liste ou à un candidat présent lors de son établissement encourt une peine de six mois à un an d’emprisonnement ainsi qu’une amende comprise entre 10.000 et 50.000 dirhams. L’ensemble de ces dispositions figure dans la loi organique n° 27.11 relative à la Chambre des représentants, telle que modifiée et complétée par la loi organique n° 53.25, qui encadre les élections législatives de 2026. The post Législatives 2026 : jusqu’à 20 ans de prison pour les atteintes à l’intégrité du scrutin appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: ‘Don’t manipulate 2027 elections’ — Obidient Movement warns Wike
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The Obidient Movement has warned the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, and other political actors against attempting to manipulate the outcome of the 2027 general elections. The movement issued the warning in a statement on Tuesday in reaction to Wike’s recent comments on the 2023 presidential election, particularly his disclosure that the former Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, G5 governors deliberately stopped Labour Party candidate, Peter Obi, from winning Rivers State. The statement, signed by the Media and Communications Directorate of the Obidient Movement and released on its X handle, was titled: “Wike’s Open Confession to Election Manipulation and Rigging on TVC: Write Your Will Now If You Are Planning to Manipulate 2027 Results.” “The Obidient Movement has watched with grave concern the video of the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike, speaking publicly about how he and other evil conspirators carried out a treasonable offence against the Nigerian people in 2023 by manipulating election results to favour Bola Tinubu and the APC,” the statement said. The movement said the comments had reinforced what it described as its longstanding position on the outcome of the 2023 presidential election. “Even though this reconfirms what we have always known about the outcome of the 2023 elections, it is jarring to hear it once again in a braggadocio manner from a perpetual nuisance, Wike, on the now-disgraced TVC,” it said. The group then issued its strongest warning ahead of the 2027 elections, saying any attempt to manipulate the people’s votes would be resisted. “In view of the foregoing, the Obidient Movement hereby invites Wike and his co-conspirators to make sure they write their will before the 2027 elections, as Nigerians are determined to enforce the rig-and-die mantra from the polling units to the collation centres,” it said. “Any manipulation or attempted manipulation of the people’s will would be met with forceful resistance, including the possible infliction of terminal wounds on such people.” The movement also called on the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to return to what it described as its constitutional responsibility of conducting credible elections. “We therefore call on the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) to go back to its constitutional responsibility of organising credible elections, instead of the charade it has been organising since 2019 in the name of elections,” it said. The group accused INEC of being loyal to the ruling APC, demanding an end to what it described as the commission’s alleged bias. “INEC’s loyalty to the APC must therefore come to an end, as Nigerians will strongly resist any attempt to keep them in perpetual bondage under Tinubu’s sadistic and wasteful government,” the statement said. It added: “INEC’s responsibility is to the Nigerian people and to the integrity of the electoral process.” The Obidient Movement also warned security agencies against interfering with the electoral process, saying their responsibility was to protect voters, electoral officials and democracy. “The same applies to the security agencies. Their duty is to protect voters, electoral officials and the democratic process, not to intimidate citizens, suppress opposition or facilitate electoral manipulation,” it said. The movement further warned that Nigerians would resist any attempt to use security agencies to manipulate the 2027 elections. “They are security agents because Nigerians have chosen to recognise them as such. But if they continue to see themselves as primarily loyal to criminals, and not to the Nigerian people, Nigerians will also treat them as enemies, the same way an armed robber breaking into any house at night is regarded as an enemy.” On the 2027 election, the group said Nigerians would not accept results that were allegedly predetermined by political actors. “In 2027, Nigerians are not going to court, and will not accept results written by Tinubu, Wike, and a compromised INEC,” it said. The movement also addressed political thugs, urging them not to allow themselves to be used to disrupt elections. “Tinubu, Wike and other politicians might use you to scatter polling units because they believe you have nuisance value. But when the election is over, they no longer need you, and they turn to their families when they need to travel on vacation or enter government house,” it said. “You must get to the point where you refuse to be used by these criminals. Even you deserve a good life.” The group insisted that the 2027 election must be determined by voters at polling units. “The 2027 election must be decided by voters at the polling units, not by politicians in private rooms, electoral officials behind closed doors or security agencies acting outside their constitutional mandate,” it added. “We will insist that the results announced must reflect the votes actually cast by Nigerians.” The Obidient Movement added that Nigerians’ peaceful disposition should not be interpreted as weakness. “Nobody should mistake the peaceful nature of Nigerians for weakness. The ballot belongs to the people. “Nobody has the right to steal it. Nobody has the right to manipulate it. And nobody who abuses public office to subvert the democratic process should expect to escape accountability.” The movement concluded by calling for a free, fair and credible 2027 election, saying: “The 2027 elections must be free, fair, transparent and credible. “Nigeria must be OK.” Wike’s 2023 election claim The statement followed comments by Wike during an interview on TVC News’ Journalists’ Hangout on Monday, where he explained the strategy adopted by the G5 governors during the 2023 presidential election. Wike said the group allowed Peter Obi to win in Edo and Cross River because the PDP’s strength in the South-South posed a threat to the presidential ambition of its candidate at the time, Atiku Abubakar. He said Rivers State was treated differently because the group did not want Obi to win there. “It was only Rivers that said, ‘No, we have a problem here in Rivers. Obi will not win here because if he wins, he sends a signal somewhere, people may not understand it.’ And we stopped…we stopped it,” Wike said. Wike also argued that the political circumstances that favoured Obi in 2023 had changed ahead of 2027, saying the Labour Party candidate could no longer win the South-South and advised him to prepare for the 2031 election. The post ‘Don’t manipulate 2027 elections’ — Obidient Movement warns Wike appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Share intelligence you have with authorities to deal with drug trafficking – NDC to NPP
items.description: The Deputy Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko-Computer, says persons behind allegations of clandestine laboratories processing illicit drugs in Ghana should be invited to answer questions and provide further information to security agencies. His comments follow allegations by the National Organiser of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Henry Nana Boakye, that drug traffickers have established laboratories in Ghana to process narcotics for export. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, September 22, 2026, Mr Tanko-Computer said the claims made by Mr Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, suggest that he has intelligence on the alleged operations. “I listened to the press conference, and I’m sure the National Security Secretariat and other allied security agencies listened to the press conference, because it appeared this group of people, they have a lot of information about these drugs. “People should be called to come and answer questions and give more information. The presenter, Nana B, mentioned that he believes these things were aided by government officials and all that. It means he has information,” Mr Tanko-Computer stated. He urged Mr Boakye and the NPP to share any credible intelligence they have with the relevant authorities. “If you have clear information about these dealings, we are open to information as a government. Come and give us more information,” he added. Mr Tanko-Computer also urged citizens not to conceal information that could threaten the country’s security, adding that “It is enjoined by the Constitution, the 1992 Constitution, not to conceal information.” “When you know that certain things are going to disturb the peace and tranquility of this nation, you don’t conceal it just because of political expediency.”

items.title: Floods take over homes, business premises in Warri, Udu, Uvwie
items.description: By Jimitota Onoyume Heavy flooding triggered by torrential rains on Monday and yesterday has taken over several homes and business premises in Warri South, Uvwie and Udu Local government areas of Delta state. Along Okere road in Warri, residential apartments and business premises were heavily flooded. Residents and business owners were seen bailing out water from their apartments and stores . A salon operator in the area said she lost hair weavons worth about N2 million belonging to customers who had brought them for revamping. She also said her generator was destroyed after floodwater entered her shop. Residents blamed the flooding along the Okere Road axis on a blocked canal, saying the waterway meant to evacuate rainwater had been filled with debris, preventing the free flow of water. Youths in the area were seen yesterday struggling to clear the canal beneath the bridge along Okere road, close to the Warri Correction Centre, apparently to ease the situation pending intervention by the local government authorities. Motorists and commercial tricycle operators also struggled to navigate flooded portions of Ogunu, Airport and Jakpa roads, with some commuters forced to make their way through deep pools of water. The rising floodwater also disrupted learning in some public schools in Udu local government area, as some parents kept their children and wards at home for fear of the dangers posed by the flood. “Flood has turned into something else. Houses have been taken over and there have been stories of the flood sweeping away children and even adults across the state, so I kept my children at home until the water level goes down,” a resident, Madam Oghenewhede, said. The affected residents appealed to the relevant local government authorities to take urgent and lasting measures to address the recurring flooding and improve drainage infrastructure in the affected areas. Meantime the Nigerian Hydrological Services Agency (NIHSA ) has said that about 15 states, including communities along the coastal fringes of the Niger Delta, could experience severe flooding between September 19 and 25, 2026. items.title: Trump says he thinks US will make deal with Iran after election
items.description: UNITED NATIONS, Sept 22 (Reuters) - President Donald Trump on Tuesday said that he thought the US would make a deal with Iran after mid-term elections are held on November 3. "I believe we'll make a deal right after the election because it doesn't make sense for them not to. They're waiting to see how I do in the midterm election," Trump said during a speech to the United Nations General Assembly. (Reporting by Doina Chiacu, Michelle Nichols, Katharine Jackson;Editing by David Ljunggren)

items.title: Trump calls on all ICC members to resign immediately
items.description: UNITED NATIONS, Sept 22 (Reuters) - U.S. President Donald Trump on Tuesday urged members of the International Criminal Court to resign and condemned what he called an "out of control institution" and "an evil group of people." Trump told the United Nations General Assembly that the US would not allow military servicemembers to be subject to what he called show trials by an anti-American tribunal. "I call on all nations that are members of the ICC to officially resign from this rogue institution immediately," he said.

Plateau killings: Northern CAN demands urgent action to halt bloodshed
items.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo The Christian Association of Nigeria, CAN, Northern States and Federal Capital Territory, FCT, has condemned the continued killings and destruction of property in Plateau State, urging the Federal and state governments to take immediate steps to restore peace and protect vulnerable communities. Chairman of Northern CAN, Rev. Dr. Yakubu Pam, in a statement on Tuesday, expressed “deep sadness and grave concern” over the persistent violence and loss of innocent lives across affected communities. The Christian body strongly condemned the attacks and called for an immediate end to what it described as “senseless bloodshed and destruction.” Northern CAN urged President Bola Tinubu and the Plateau State Government to take firm and immediate measures to end the violence, protect residents and restore lasting peace and security in the affected areas. According to the association, the repeated attacks and destruction of property underscore the need for a comprehensive review and strengthening of Nigeria’s security architecture. “The persistent destruction of lives and property points to the urgent need for a comprehensive review and strengthening of the nation’s security architecture,” it said. Northern CAN said Nigerians should be able to live, work, worship and raise their families without fear of attacks in their communities. The association also expressed solidarity with families who lost loved ones and residents whose homes, livelihoods and communities had been affected by the violence. “We extend our heartfelt condolences and solidarity to the families who have lost loved ones and to all those whose homes, livelihoods, and communities have been affected by the violence,” the statement said. It called on the Federal Government to make the restoration of peace and security in troubled communities a priority, stressing that the safety and protection of citizens must remain central to governance. “The safety and protection of citizens must remain at the centre of governance and national attention,” Northern CAN said. The association also appealed to residents of Plateau State to remain united and avoid actions capable of escalating tensions, urging them to pursue peace, justice and the protection of their communities. “We equally call on the good people of Plateau State to remain united, reject actions capable of further escalating tensions, and work together in the pursuit of peace, justice, and the protection of their communities,” it said. Reaffirming its commitment to peace, justice and reconciliation, Northern CAN urged relevant authorities to act swiftly to prevent further loss of lives. “Northern CAN remains committed to peace, justice, reconciliation, and the protection of innocent lives. We urge all relevant authorities to act swiftly and decisively before more lives are lost,” Pam said. The post Plateau killings: Northern CAN demands urgent action to halt bloodshed appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: N’Zérékoré : l’ONCQ tape du poing sur la table et menace de sévir contre le mixage du café-cacao
items.description: À quelques jours du lancement officiel de la campagne de production du café et du cacao, l’Office national du contrôle qualité (ONCQ) de N’Zérékoré met en garde les opérateurs de la filière contre certaines pratiques jugées contraires aux exigences de qualité. Le chef du service du contrôle qualité de l’ONCQ de N’Zérékoré, Moussa Sacko, a notamment dénoncé le mélange de produits de qualités différentes, ainsi que des opérations de transfert et d’embarquement effectuées sans la présence préalable des agents de contrôle. Il s’exprimait ce mardi 22 septembre 2026, à la direction préfectorale de la Chambre de commerce, d’industrie et d’artisanat de N’Zérékoré, à l’occasion d’une rencontre d’échanges avec les opérateurs économiques de la filière café-cacao. « Le mixage n’est pas normal » Parmi les pratiques dénoncées par le responsable de l’ONCQ figure le mixage de produits de qualité différente. Une pratique qui consisterait, selon lui, à mélanger du café ou du cacao de bonne qualité avec des produits jugés de qualité inférieure afin d’en masquer les défauts. « Souvent, quand les gens ont une mauvaise qualité, soit du cacao ou du café, ils font du mixage. Ils cherchent une bonne qualité et la mélangent avec une mauvaise. Ce n’est pas normal », a-t-il dénoncé. Moussa Sacko a également insisté sur la nécessité pour les opérateurs de prévenir le service de contrôle qualité avant toute opération de transfert ou d’embarquement des produits. Selon lui, la présence des agents est indispensable pour vérifier la marchandise, contrôler les quantités et procéder aux prélèvements nécessaires. Des contrôles exigés avant tout transfert Le responsable de l’ONCQ a particulièrement mis l’accent sur les produits en provenance de la Côte d’Ivoire. Il estime que tout transfert d’un camion à un autre doit se faire en présence des agents de contrôle, afin de vérifier la conformité de la marchandise. Moussa Sacko a, par ailleurs, dénoncé la délivrance de bulletins d’inspection sans vérification effective du contenu des camions. « Si le bulletin d’inspection doit être délivré et que tu ne sais même pas ce qu’il y a à l’intérieur du camion, ni la qualité du produit, tu viens délivrer un bulletin d’inspection. Vous pensez que c’est du bon travail ? Ce n’est pas du bon travail », a-t-il martelé. « Je ne vais plus accepter de mettre ma signature » Autre pratique dans le viseur du chef du service contrôle qualité : l’acheminement vers Conakry de produits qui ne répondraient pas aux normes requises, avec l’idée qu’ils pourraient y être traités ou améliorés. Moussa Sacko rappelle que les produits quittant N’Zérékoré doivent satisfaire aux exigences de qualité et être accompagnés des documents requis avant leur expédition. « Je ne vais plus accepter de mettre ma signature, mon cachet sur un produit qui n’est pas de qualité », a-t-il averti. Le responsable de l’ONCQ a également défendu les opérations de prélèvement et de contrôle effectuées par ses agents dans les zones de production. Selon lui, ces opérations s’inscrivent dans le cadre des procédures prévues par l’État. Pour finir, Moussa Sacko a invité les opérateurs économiques à faciliter l’accès des agents de contrôle aux magasins et aux produits à inspecter. Il estime qu’une meilleure collaboration entre les services de contrôle et les acteurs de la filière est indispensable pour renforcer la qualité du café et du cacao produits dans la région de N’Zérékoré.

items.title: ‘You promised 24-Hour economy not 24-hour cocaine trafficking’ – Nana B to Mahama
items.description: The National Organiser of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Henry Nana Boakye, popularly known as Nana B, has criticised President John Dramani Mahama over what he describes as growing concerns about cocaine trafficking and Ghana’s international image. Speaking at an NPP press conference on drug trafficking, Nana B directly addressed the President, saying: “Mr. President, you promised Ghanaians a 24-hour economy. You did not promise 24-hour cocaine trafficking.” Nana B said the reported cases of drug trafficking linked to Ghana are having consequences beyond the individuals involved, particularly for ordinary Ghanaians travelling and doing business internationally. “Remember, Ghanaians, if you can, how a government elected on the promise of jobs and prosperity has instead delivered a country whose name now triggers extra searches, extra suspicion and extra humiliation for every innocent Ghanaian traveller.” He further alleged that Ghanaian travellers and exporters are increasingly facing heightened scrutiny at international airports because of concerns surrounding narcotics trafficking. “At every airport in the world, Ghanaian exporters are now treated with suspicion. Ghanaian travellers now carry a stigma they did not create,” he said. According to Nana B, the situation requires Parliament to exercise its oversight responsibilities and establish the facts surrounding the reported drug interceptions and shipments allegedly linked to Ghana. “In the light of this, the New Patriotic Party demands an immediate parliamentary inquiry, as already stated,” Nana B said. He called on Parliament to examine relevant shipping documents, inspection records, production records and other documentation connected to the reported cases. Nana B’s comments come against the backdrop of a major narcotics interception involving a large consignment of suspected cocaine believed to have passed through Ghana’s port security and customs processes before being intercepted by French authorities. The development has further intensified calls for scrutiny of Ghana’s systems for detecting and preventing the trafficking of illicit drugs through the country’s ports.

items.title: Nana Konadu dedicated her life to community transformation — Yaa Asantewaa Agyeman-Rawlings
items.description: The Executive Director of the J.J. Rawlings Foundation, Ms Yaa Asantewaa Agyeman-Rawlings, has paid tribute to her late mother, former First Lady Nana Konadu Agyeman-Rawlings, describing her as a fierce campaigner who spent her life driving the political, social, and economic development of Ghanaian communities. Speaking at the launch of the Sheroes of Africa Coffee Table Book at The Palms by Eagles in Accra, Ms Agyeman-Rawlings noted that her mother possessed a fighting spirit that went far beyond basic gender advocacy. True national progress, she explained, only happens when local communities are given the tools and confidence to take control of their own futures. Grassroots leadership and community work Reflecting on her mother’s approach to public life, Ms Agyeman-Rawlings highlighted her refusal to lead from behind a desk or stay inside the capital. “This was my mother: boots on the ground. She did not believe in championing an idea from a distance. She went where the people were. She listened, she mobilized, she organized and she acted. She always said that there was not a single community in Ghana that she had not been to,” she said. She stressed that the impact of her mother’s life work extends far beyond her immediate family. “Her Legacy, therefore, belongs not only to her children or to her family. It belongs to the women whose confidence she awakened; to the communities whose horizons she expanded; to the young people who saw in her an example of courage and resilience; and to every Ghanaian whose life was touched, directly or indirectly, by her work.” Advancing local governance and women’s political involvement Looking back at the political history of the mid-1980s, the second daughter of the former First Lady recalled how her mother used the 31st December Women’s Movement to back the Provisional National Defence Council’s (PNDC) decentralisation policy, travelling across the country to explain the benefits of local administration to grassroots communities. “She also recognized the opportunity presented by district-level elections and encouraged many women – including some of her own organisers – to put themselves forward for election and public service,” Ms Agyeman-Rawlings added. Honoured among 100 African women leaders The Sheroes of Africa Coffee Table Book , authored by Princess Flossy Tachie-Menson, profiles 100 prominent African women whose leadership and vision have influenced the continent. The event was chaired by former Malawian President Dr Joyce Banda, who serves as Chairperson of the Sheroes Foundation. Commending the author and publishers, Ms Agyeman-Rawlings noted that the project plays an essential role in preserving vital history for future generations. “We are deeply moved that Nana Konadu Agyeman-Rawlings, has been featured among these remarkable African women and that a commemorative copy is being presented in her honour. May these pages remind them that the flame she carried was never hers alone. It was a flame meant to be passed on,” she remarked. Ahead of the first anniversary of her mother’s passing on October 23, 2026, Ms Agyeman-Rawlings observed that a meaningful life continues through the people and places it touched. “Yet today reminds us that a life of purpose does not end with physical departure. It continues in the people we inspire, the communities we strengthen, the courage we awaken and the legacy we leave behind,” she said.

Younes Ebnoutalib : « Quand Klopp vous appelle, vous devez aller vers lui »
items.description: Courtisé par le Maroc, Younes Ebnoutalib a finalement choisi de représenter l’Allemagne. L’attaquant de l’Eintracht Francfort explique que Jürgen Klopp a joué un rôle déterminant dans sa décision. Younes Ebnoutalib a choisi l’Allemagne plutôt que le Maroc. À 23 ans, l’attaquant de l’Eintracht Francfort affirme que l’arrivée de Jürgen Klopp à la tête de la Mannschaft a pesé lourd dans son choix. Le joueur avait pourtant échangé avec Mohamed Ouahbi, sélectionneur des Lions de l’Atlas. Mais la possibilité de travailler avec Klopp l’a convaincu. « Quand Klopp vous appelle, vous devez aller vers lui » , a déclaré Ebnoutalib, qui assure toutefois rester attaché aux deux pays. « J’aime les deux pays, les deux représentent ma patrie d’origine, et je souhaiterai toujours le meilleur au Maroc » , a-t-il ajouté. Ebnoutalib a été retenu par Klopp dans le premier groupe de la sélection allemande, qui affrontera les Pays-Bas jeudi en Ligue des nations, avant de jouer contre la Grèce dimanche. Avec Kai Havertz, il fait partie des rares véritables avant-centres de ce groupe. Une situation qui pourrait lui permettre de connaître rapidement ses premières minutes avec la Mannschaft. « Je ne sais encore rien à ce sujet. J’essaie simplement de donner le meilleur de moi-même et j’espère avoir beaucoup de temps de jeu » , a expliqué le joueur. Ebnoutalib réalise par ailleurs un début de saison remarqué avec l’Eintracht Francfort. Il a inscrit quatre buts en quatre journées de Bundesliga, avant de rejoindre le rassemblement allemand. Arrivé à la tête de la Mannschaft après Julian Nagelsmann, Jürgen Klopp entend désormais reconstruire une sélection allemande éliminée dès les seizièmes de finale de la dernière Coupe du Monde. The post Younes Ebnoutalib : « Quand Klopp vous appelle, vous devez aller vers lui » appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: N170,000 ‘Protecrion Fee’ Saga: Ogun monarch denies stopping PDP campaign
items.description: By James Ogunnaike, Abeokuta The Dagburewe-in-Council has denied allegations that the Dagburewe of Idowa, Oba Sikiru Kayode Okuribido, stalled the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, campaign rally in the community after the party paid N170,000 “protection fee”. Also, the Council said the monarch did not aid the alleged destruction of property during the party’s campaign activities on September 16. The council, at a press conference on Tuesday, said the traditional ruler neither instructed anyone to stop the PDP campaign train from entering Idowa nor participated in any alleged act of violence or destruction associated with the incident. The briefing was attended by members of the Oloritun-in-Council of Idowa, religious leaders and security operatives. Speaking on behalf of the council, the Sobaloju of Idowa, Chief Yusuf Olatunji Olusanya, urged the Police and other relevant security agencies to conduct an impartial investigation into the incident, and establish what transpired through eyewitness accounts, police records, bank transactions, photographs, videos and other available evidence. The genesis The controversy followed the PDP’s campaign activities in Odogbolu Local Government Area, during which the party alleged that it had planned to hold its campaign flag-off in Idowa, but was prevented from using the venue. Vanguard had reported the PDP’s claim that it paid N170,000 for the venue but was later prevented from holding its campaign in Idowa township. Olusanya, however, said the monarch neither stalled the rally nor frustrated the campaign. He said: “Oba Okuribido did not stall the rally, frustrate the campaign, nor aid the destruction of anybody’s property. “Nobody, and no government or government agency, instructed anybody or His Royal Highness to stop or disallow the PDP campaign train from entering Idowa.” According to him, there was also no formal notification letter, to its knowledge, sent to either the community or the palace informing them of the proposed campaign visit. Olusanya challenged anyone alleging that the monarch deliberately frustrated the rally to produce verifiable evidence rather than rely on reports circulating on social media. Shootings allegation He described the allegations of gunshots, looting and destruction of vehicles as serious matters that should be subjected to investigation rather than treated as political exchanges. He called on the security agencies to establish whether the PDP campaign train actually entered Idowa on September 16 and, if so, determine its approved itinerary and security arrangements. The council also sought clarification over conflicting accounts concerning the movement of the campaign train. Chief Olusanya further urged the police to investigate allegations surrounding the reported shooting of the son of one Sakiru Bello, popularly known as Omoh. He asked the authorities to establish whether the alleged shooting occurred, where and when it happened, who was responsible and the circumstances surrounding the incident. Other issues raised included an allegation that Bello was arrested over the pasting of PDP posters and claims of an alleged N50,000 payment linked to his release. The council said police records and banking evidence should be used to establish whether the arrest and payment occurred. Olusanya also questioned the circumstances surrounding the reported payment of N170,000 into community coffers for the use of a venue allegedly sought by the PDP. According to the council, the agreed payment for the venue was N30,000, while N170,000 was subsequently paid. He alleged that N140,000 was later approved for refund through a signed cheque bearing the name of Oyinlola Odufuwa, whom the council said had requested the refund, saying that the cheque was reportedly not collected because Odufuwa claimed to have travelled to Abuja. He maintained that the circumstances surrounding the payment and proposed refund should be established through documentary evidence. The PDP had earlier said it paid N170,000 into a community account after obtaining approval to use the venue, but alleged that it was prevented from using the facility only hours before the scheduled event. Olusanya appealed to political actors and residents not to drag the traditional institution into partisan politics. “Oba Okuribido occupies a traditional position that transcends party politics,” he said. “If anyone alleges that His Royal Highness stalled a political rally or aided the destruction of property, the proper thing is to present the evidence to the appropriate authorities.” The council said anyone found to have committed an offence should face the law, irrespective of political affiliation. “We are not asking for favour. We are not asking for protection for anybody. We are asking for the truth,” the council said. It urged the security agencies to conduct a “thorough, impartial and transparent investigation” into the September 16 incident. “Let nobody attempt to rewrite history through social media. “Let the eyewitness accounts, police records, bank records, photographs, videos and other available evidence speak for themselves,” the council said. items.title: Décentralisation : l’ANAFIC et ses partenaires dressent le bilan du PANAFIC
items.description: Le gouvernement guinéen, l’Agence nationale de financement des collectivités locales (ANAFIC) et l’Agence française de développement (AFD) ont procédé à la capitalisation des acquis du Projet d’appui à l’ANAFIC (PANAFIC). La rencontre a permis aux différents acteurs d’évaluer les résultats obtenus, d’identifier les difficultés rencontrées et de réfléchir à la pérennisation des mécanismes de financement du développement local. Dans son intervention, le directeur général de l’ANAFIC, Sékou M’Mawa Touré, a expliqué que le PANAFIC s’inscrit dans une politique de renforcement des capacités des collectivités décentralisées et d’amélioration des mécanismes de financement local. « Le PANAFIC s’inscrit dans la volonté de renforcer les capacités des collectivités décentralisées, d’améliorer les mécanismes de financement du développement local et de rapprocher davantage l’action publique des populations », a-t-il déclaré. 0-3840×2160-0-0-{}-0-24# Selon lui, l’objectif de l’atelier ne se limite pas à dresser un bilan des activités réalisées. Il s’agit également d’identifier les pratiques qui ont produit des résultats, de comprendre les contraintes et de proposer des améliorations pour les futurs programmes. « Capitaliser, ce n’est pas simplement faire le bilan. C’est identifier ce qui a fonctionné, comprendre les difficultés rencontrées, valoriser les bonnes pratiques et dégager les améliorations nécessaires pour l’avenir », a-t-il ajouté. Le directeur général de l’ANAFIC a notamment insisté sur la nécessité d’évaluer l’efficacité des mécanismes mis en place, la qualité des investissements réalisés, le renforcement des capacités des collectivités et la durabilité des acquis. Il estime que l’expérience du PANAFIC pourrait servir de référence aux futures interventions en faveur de la décentralisation et du développement local. Dans le contexte du programme Simandou 2040, Sékou M’Mawa Touré considère que des collectivités mieux organisées et capables de planifier leurs investissements seront indispensables pour accompagner les transformations économiques et sociales du pays. 0-3840×2160-0-0-{}-0-24# Une expérience issue de plusieurs décennies d’accompagnement Revenant sur l’historique de l’ANAFIC, Moussa Doumbouya, représentant de l’Agence française de développement à cette rencontre, a rappelé que l’institution était initialement un projet d’appui aux collectivités villageoises. Selon lui, ce dispositif avait été mis en place dans le prolongement des premières politiques de décentralisation engagées en Guinée dans les années 1990. Après plusieurs années d’accompagnement par les partenaires techniques et financiers, le gouvernement avait décidé, entre 2017 et 2019, de l’institutionnaliser. Cette évolution a conduit à la création de l’Agence nationale de financement des collectivités locales, chargée notamment d’accompagner les communes et de faciliter l’allocation directe de financements en leur faveur. « Globalement, je voudrais dire que le projet PANAFIC a été une réussite. Il s’agit d’une réussite globale, qui a permis d’atteindre les territoires les plus éloignés de la Guinée », a indiqué Moussa Doumbouya. Il a affirmé que le projet avait permis de renforcer les capacités de l’ANAFIC et des collectivités, mais aussi de développer des outils de gestion, de planification, d’exécution et de suivi des financements. Le représentant de l’AFD a également évoqué l’élaboration des plans de développement local, des programmes annuels d’investissement et l’intégration des enjeux climatiques dans les interventions des collectivités. Il a réaffirmé la volonté de l’Agence française de développement de poursuivre son accompagnement en faveur de la décentralisation et du développement local. Dix millions d’euros mobilisés Présidant la cérémonie, la ministre de l’Administration du territoire et de la Décentralisation, Djenabou Touré, a affirmé que le PANAFIC avait atteint la plupart des objectifs fixés. « Le PANAFIC a tenu parole. Sur les dix millions d’euros engagés, la totalité a été utilisée. La plupart des objectifs que nous nous étions fixés ont été atteints », a-t-elle déclaré. D’après la ministre, plus de cinq millions de personnes, dont une majorité de femmes, auraient bénéficié directement ou indirectement des actions du projet. Elle a notamment cité la réalisation d’une centaine de microprojets, parmi lesquels des écoles, des postes et centres de santé clôturés et électrifiés, des points d’eau, des unités de fabrication de savon gérées par des groupements féminins, ainsi que des actions de protection de forêts et de têtes de source. Les collectivités décentralisées ont également été équipées en matériel informatique afin d’améliorer la gestion et la présentation de leurs comptes. Trois communes de Conakry ont, par ailleurs, engagé une démarche commune pour faire face aux problèmes de salubrité publique. Des insuffisances à corriger Malgré les résultats enregistrés, Djenabou Touré a reconnu que plusieurs défis restent à relever. Elle a notamment évoqué la faible participation des femmes dans les instances de décision, la progression jugée insuffisante du recouvrement des ressources propres des collectivités et les difficultés liées à la chaîne comptable communale. « Nous ne sommes pas ici pour célébrer. Nous sommes ici pour apprendre. Capitaliser, c’est regarder ce qui a réussi et comprendre pourquoi. C’est aussi regarder ce qui a résisté et en tirer les conséquences », a-t-elle souligné. La ministre a également appelé à l’abondement régulier des budgets d’affectation spéciale du Fonds national de développement local (FNDL) et du Fonds de développement économique local (FODEL). Elle a plaidé pour la généralisation de la digitalisation comptable, l’assermentation des receveurs communaux et l’opérationnalisation de la fonction publique locale. Selon elle, la pérennisation des acquis dépendra désormais de l’engagement du gouvernement, de l’administration centrale et déconcentrée, des collectivités locales, des élus et des partenaires. L’atelier a aussi été marqué par la remise de kits informatiques, de terminaux de paiement électronique et de motos, ainsi que par des présentations consacrées aux objectifs, aux composantes, au taux d’exécution et aux investissements réalisés dans le cadre du PANAFIC. Des échanges en plénière ont permis aux participants d’analyser les résultats obtenus, les écarts constatés et les perspectives du projet.

items.title: Minna: NAS demands arrest of owners of illegal mining sites
items.description: Wants public release of investigative report The National Association of Seadogs (Pyrates Confraternity) has demanded the arrest of owners of the illegal mining sites at Lt Gen Mohammed Inuwa Wushishi Estate and Lukoto Village in Minna, Niger State, where the 37 teenagers who died in the custody of the Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps NSCDC) were arrested. The NAS Cap’n, Dr Charles Meribole, in a statement entitled: ‘’NSCDC Custodial Deaths: Recurring Impunity of Security Agencies Must End’’ noted that the owners of the illegal mining sites were culpable in the tragic end of the teenagers by engaging them for cheap labour rather than to be in school. There should be a broader inquiry into the ownership of the illegal mining sites where the teenagers were arrested. Section 131 of the Nigerian Minerals and Mining Act 2007 makes unlawful mining without a license punishable under the law. Nigerians deserve to know the owners of the illegal sites that allowed teenagers, who are supposed to be in school, to engage in cheap labour at illegal mining sites, in gross violation of the Child Rights Act 2003 and the Trafficking in Persons (Prohibition) Enforcement and Administration Act 2015. The owners of these illegal mining sites should be arrested and prosecuted, along with those found culpable in the deaths of the 37 teenagers.’’ Meribole, who insisted that the suspension of the NSCDC personnel is not justice, called for a departure from the past where government-instituted investigative panel reports are allowed to gather dust without punishment for indicted officials and compensation for victims. ‘’ The tragic death of the 37 teenagers in Minna should mark a turning point in the Nigerian government’s indifference to the implementation of investigative panel reports. The investigation of the Minna tragedy must not become another bureaucratic exercise whose findings gather dust. That cycle must end. The culture of recurring impunity must stop.’’ He also advocated for reforms in the detention policy of the NSCDC, stressing that arresting a suspect over allegations of a crime committed should not strip suspects of their dignity and right to life. ‘’More importantly, this tragedy must also compel an urgent review of detention practices across the NSCDC commands and other law-enforcement agencies. Overcrowding, medical screening, emergency response, detainee monitoring, separation of minors from adults, sanitation, ventilation, and access to necessities cannot be treated as administrative details. They are matters of life and death. A detention facility must never become a place where a person disappears from public view and loses the protection of the law. ‘’The Federal Government must immediately conduct an urgent audit of law enforcement and security agencies’ detention facilities nationwide, particularly with respect to overcrowding, ventilation, and emergency response.’’ The post Minna: NAS demands arrest of owners of illegal mining sites appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‘You won’t return to Senate’ – Wike again tells Ireti Kingibe
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Federal Capital Territory FCT Minister, Nyesom Wike, has told the FCT Senator, Ireti Kingibe, that she will not return to the National Assembly in 2027, describing her as illiterate and insisting that all loans taken by the FCT Administration followed due process and National Assembly approval. Wike made the remarks on Tuesday while responding to questions from journalists during an inspection of ongoing road projects in the FCT, after Senator Kingibe had accused him of taking loans without approval. “She is an illiterate, with all due respect, and that is why she is not going back to the Senate. She has nothing to offer to the people of the FCT. There is no way you can go and take a loan without the approval of the National Assembly. Anyone take a loan, you will include it in the budget that this aspect of this budget, the government is going to collect loan,” the minister said. Wike said he would rather not dignify the senator’s comments with further reaction, describing her as already on her way out of political relevance following the choice residents had made to back President Bola Tinubu and his preferred candidate for the FCT senatorial seat, Philip Aduda. “I don’t want to comment about her. When the time is right, let her pack her bags out, the people have made their choice by agreeing to support President Tinubu, and then will support Philip Aduda for Senate. So, let us not waste our time reacting to inferiors who failed in all ramifications. I don’t want to react to it, I am above that,” he said. The minister argued that the more relevant question the senator should have raised was whether the loans were being applied to development, rather than the fact that a loan was taken at all. “I thought she would criticise that I am doing nothing. So if her problem is that I took a loan, if I took a loan, I am using it to work. I thought her concern would have been: are we applying the loan to work for the interest of residents? She believes that we can’t run infrastructure without loans, and that we must have taken a loan, that is her problem,” he said. Wike also dismissed the timing of the criticism as politically motivated, linking it to the recent lifting of the ban on campaigns for the presidential and National Assembly elections, and pointed to his ongoing project inspections as proof of performance ahead of the polls. “When is the time to campaign? Look at what we are doing. That is the campaign. The ban on campaign has been lifted for the President and National Assembly, am I not right? As I finish now, then she know what we are doing, and they are seeing every road, and tell everyone that this is what President Tinubu is doing. Who will see what Mr President is doing and will say that he will vote for another person? That is not correct. So, I am doing my job. While we are doing an inspection of the project, we are also doing a campaign,” he said. On the state of the projects inspected, Wike said he was impressed with progress recorded across the sites visited, including the N1 road and stretches covering Tunga Madaki down to Zuba and Kagini. He said the projects, once completed, would have a direct economic impact on residents of the affected rural communities, adding that the happiness of the people remained the essence of governance. The post ‘You won’t return to Senate’ – Wike again tells Ireti Kingibe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Conférence One Health à Rome : le Cameroun plaide pour des normes au service du terrain
items.description: © DR Représentant le Cameroun à la Conférence Mondiale sur l'approche « Une seule santé » organisée par la FAO à Rome, le Ministre de l'Élevage, Dr Taïga, a délivré un message fort : les normes internationales n'ont de valeur que si elles sont appliquées concrètement. Il a présenté le modèle camerounais, entre architecture institutionnelle et capacités opérationnelles. Le Cameroun fait entendre sa voix à Rome.A l'occasion de la Conférence Mondiale sur l'Application de l'Approche « Une seule santé » dans les systèmes agroalimentaires, organisée par la FAO, le Ministre de l'Élevage, des Pêches et des Industries Animales, Dr Taïga, a plaidé pour des normes internationales au service du terrain. Devant les hauts responsables de la FAO, ministres et ambassadeurs, il a rappelé l'interdépendance entre santés humaine, animale, végétale et environnementale. « Le Codex Alimentarius, les normes de l'OMSA, les normes phytosanitaires et le Règlement Sanitaire International fournissent un langage commun pour gérer les risques », a-t-il souligné. Situé au cœur du bassin du Congo, le Cameroun est exposé aux risques zoonotiques. Les épisodes d'anthrax et la mortalité des grands singes dans la Réserve du Dja en 2005 ont conduit à la création d'une Stratégie nationale, devenue aujourd'hui le Programme National de Lutte contre les Zoonoses (PNPLZER), plateforme « One Health » placée sous la supervision des Services du Premier Ministre. Une dynamique soutenue par l'ANOR avec plus de 3 200 normes référencées, dont 113 homologuées en élevage en 2024 et 25 en technologie alimentaire en 2025, et sur le terrain par le LANAVET, le RESCAM et le Centre d'urgence en santé animale. Le Dr Taïga a dégagé trois leçons : adapter les normes sans perdre leur cohérence, exiger un portage politique au plus haut niveau, et bâtir des capacités opérationnelles concrètes. Cet article Conférence One Health à Rome : le Cameroun plaide pour des normes au service du terrain est apparu en premier sur Journalducameroun.com .

items.title: TPI de Dixinn : un jeune élève jugé pour tentative de vol d’un iPhone 13 Pro Max
items.description: Le procès de Mamadou Djabellou Sacko s’est ouvert ce mardi 22 septembre 2026 devant le tribunal correctionnel de Dixinn. Ce jeune élève est poursuivi pour « tentative de vol aggravé et coups et blessures volontaires » à l’égard de Sacé Fofana. Interrogé sur les faits qui lui sont reprochés, le prévenu les a reconnus. Il explique que tout est parti d’une bagarre qui a éclaté entre les deux autour d’un téléphone de marque iPhone 13 Pro Max appartenant à cette dernière. Le jeune aurait voulu dérober l’appareil en s’introduisant nuitamment dans sa boutique, située dans la commune de Lambanyi. Il explique qu’il a intimé à la dame de lui remettre le téléphone après avoir retiré le code d’accès, sous peine de châtiment extrême. Des menaces qui n’ont pas fait plier Sacé Fofana. C’est dans cette résistance qu’elle aurait subi des coups ayant entraîné des blessures. Mamadou Djabellou Sacko n’a pas pu emporter le téléphone. C’est à la suite de cela qu’il a été interpellé et mis à la disposition des services de sécurité. Pour exprimer ses regrets devant le tribunal, cet élève, en classe de 12ᵉ année, option sciences sociales, s’est même interrogé sur les raisons qui l’ont poussé à agir de la sorte vis-à-vis de dame Sacé Fofana, absente à l’audience ce mardi. En raison de cette absence, l’affaire a été renvoyée au 29 septembre 2026 pour sa comparution. Lébêré Baldé L’article TPI de Dixinn : un jeune élève jugé pour tentative de vol d’un iPhone 13 Pro Max est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Sophia Momodu recounts growing up as pastor’s daughter, facing pregnancy backlash
items.description: Entrepreneur, Sophia Momodu, has opened up about the ridicule and social stigma she faced after becoming pregnant by the singer outside marriage. Momodu spoke during a side panel at the 81st United Nations General Assembly in New York, in a video shared on her Instagram Story on Tuesday. Recalling the experience, Momodu said being the daughter of a pastor made the situation particularly difficult because of the stigma attached to having a child outside wedlock in Nigerian society. “This is my life story. I am a pastor’s daughter who got pregnant out of wedlock by a global superstar. And I was mocked. It was crazy. And I had to find my strength in the midst of all of that,” she said. “And for the longest time, I didn’t have a voice. I was famous, I was popular, but I didn’t have a voice. It kept getting drowned out by whatever negativity was around that story,” she said. She said the experience was especially stigmatising in Nigeria because of her background. “If you’re Nigerian and you’re here, you know that it’s almost a taboo to be a pastor’s daughter and have a child out of wedlock,” Momodu added. According to her, she later gained the confidence to speak publicly about her experience and discovered that many other women had gone through similar situations. Momodu said an aunt also once contacted her after someone allegedly asked her to remain silent about the matter. “And then, an aunt called me one day and said a friend of hers had called her to talk to me to please keep quiet, because this is not a topic that we are allowed to talk about as Black women,” she said. She said sharing her experience at different forums, including in South Africa, helped her realise that she was not alone. Momodu said several women subsequently approached her to share similar experiences, which encouraged her to continue speaking about her own story. “I’m just grateful for the platform, I’m grateful to be able to tell my story, and because of people like Stephanie and these amazing women on this panel, I don’t think I would ever stop telling my story,” she said. Momodu and Davido, whose real name is David Adeleke, welcomed their daughter, Imade Adeleke, on May 14, 2015. DNA testing later confirmed Davido’s paternity. The pair were intermittently involved before their relationship ended in 2022, and they never married. The post Sophia Momodu recounts growing up as pastor’s daughter, facing pregnancy backlash appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Protect the customer by changing who owns the loss
items.description: Between 2022 and 2025, fraud cases among Ghana’s payment service providers nearly doubled. At a recent COCLAB workshop, Matilda Asante Asiedu, the Second Deputy Governor of the Bank of Ghana, presented that figure and advocated for a shift in both strategy and perspective. She is right regarding the modification. Examine the same four years in the financial system as a whole. The number of fraud cases reported by banks decreased from 716 in 2024 to 472 in 2025, representing a 34% decrease. The number of specialised deposit-taking institutions decreased by half, from 344 to 182. Ghana did not experience an explosion of fraud. It shifted away from institutions that strengthened their defences and settled in areas where defences remained weak. The industry’s preferred rationale is rendered obsolete by that singular migration. The Bank of Ghana links the concentration in payment service providers partly to lower digital literacy among users. Nevertheless, the same Ghanaians are served by institutions that are exposed to the same scam contacts and use the same phones. There was no sudden increase in the sophistication of their clientele. The institutions merely filled in the voids, and the figures followed. Fraud has consistently been associated with inadequate design. The provider is only responsible for a complaint, while the consumer who incurs a loss is responsible for the loss under the current regulations. The concentration we are currently observing is precisely the result of that arrangement. By adjusting the location of the loss, the design problem begins to resolve itself. Britain responded in a straightforward manner to a comparable scenario. Providers are required to reimburse victims of authorised push-payment fraud up to £85,000 within five working days from October 2024. The cost is equally distributed between the transmitting and receiving firms. The second half is critical; the institution that established the account into which the funds disappeared now bears half of the liability. Suddenly, each provider in the chain has a specific cause to halt the mule account prior to its opening. Ghana has the ability to construct its own version, which will betailored to the local environment. The reimbursement cap can be set at GH¢20,000. That figure would still encompass the vast majority of cases; the average cost of each of the 24,778 incidents and GH¢101 million at risk is approximately GH¢4,000. Establish exceptions for customers who disregard explicit warnings. To allow fintechs to prepare, the rule will be phased in over a period of eighteen months. The fundamental action is to render a fraud case expensive for the provider. It is currently costing them almost nothing. Three practical fixes cease to await regulation and commence competing for budgetary resources upon the arrival of that cost. Prior to payment, the sender is required to verify the actual identity associated with the recipient’s account, which effectively eliminates the majority of impersonation schemes at the time of transfer. The 118% increase in fraudulent withdrawals (currently GH¢3.97 million) could be mitigated by an emergency block that secures a wallet within ninety seconds. Speed is the determining factor in these instances; document inspections can be implemented at a later time. Additionally, a shared mule-account registry, which would be visible to all providers within an hour, would prevent a single compromised number from travelling the entire ecosystem, thereby mitigating the very risk that Mrs. Asante Asiedu identified. None of these instruments is particularly uncommon. The playbook has already been demonstrated to be effective by Ghana’s banks. Ghana is at risk of sliding back into the FATF grey list; this is the costly version of the discussion. The less expensive version commences with a single principle: the institution that holds the funds is responsible for any losses. Give providers a bill, and the people who built the systems will fix them. ********* Writer: Dr. Genevieve Sedalo, Department of Marketing, University of Professional Studies. gdsedalo@gmail.com
