items.title: Why State Police Bill was transmitted quickly to state assemblies – NASS
items.description: By Henry Umoru The National Assembly has explained that it gave priority to the transmission of a bill for the establishment of State Police Service to the State Houses of Assembly in response to widespread public demands and the need to address concerns relating to security and policing in the country through an appropriate constitutional and legal framework. In a statement on Tuesday to clarify the transmission, the Clerk to the National Assembly, Kamoru Ogunlana, assured that other Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bills before the National Assembly will be transmitted to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 States of the Federation upon their passage in identical form by both chambers of the National Assembly, in accordance with the constitutional amendment process. Recall that the Senate, on the strength of the Executive Bill received from President Bola Tinubu on Tuesday, June 23, 2026, expeditiously considered and passed the State Police Establishment Bill for third reading on Wednesday, June 24, 2026, while the House of Representatives later considered the same executive bill and it was read and passed for third reading on July 23, 2026. The transmission marks the commencement of the next phase of the constitutional alteration process, just as it was carried out pursuant to Section 9 and a directive from the leadership of the National Assembly. The 2/3 concurrence means that at least 24 out of the 36 State Houses of Assembly must concur with the Constitution Alteration Bill before final transmission to President Tinubu for presidential assent. The statement read, “The National Assembly wishes to clarify recent reports and public perceptions regarding the transmission of one of the Constitution Alteration Bills to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 States of the Federation. “On Wednesday, 16 September 2026, the National Assembly issued a press release informing the general public that the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria 1999 (Sixth Alteration) Bill, 2026, titled: “A Bil for an Act to Alter the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 10 Provide for the Establishment of State Police Services; and for Related Matters,” had been transmitted to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 States of the Federation for their consideration and approval. “For the avoidance of doubt, it is only this particular Constitution Alteration Bill that has so far been transmitted to the State Houses of Assembly. It is therefore incorrect to suggest or create the impression that all the Constitution Alteration Bills before the National Assembly have been transmitted to the States. “The decision to accord priority to the Bill on the establishment of State Police Service is in response to widespread public demands and the need to address concerns relating to security and policing in the country through an appropriate constitutional and legal framework. “The other Constitution (Sixth Alteration) Bills before the National Assembly will be transmitted to the Houses of Assembly of the 36 States of the Federation upon their passage in identical form by both Chambers of the National Assembly, in accordance with the constitutional amendment process. “The National Assembly remains commited to ensuring that the ongoing Constitution Alteration process is conducted transparently, responsibly and in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria. “Members of the public and the media are therefore encouraged to rely on official communications of the National Assembly for accurate information regarding the status and transmission of the various Constitution Alteration Bills.” The post Why State Police Bill was transmitted quickly to state assemblies – NASS appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Président du CORED : Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye, un pionnier de la télévision nationale
items.description: Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye, ancien directeur de la télévision nationale et actuel président du Tribunal des pairs du Cored, incarne un demi-siècle de mémoire journalistique. Diplômé de la 7e promotion du Cesti, il appartient à une génération qui a écrit les premières grandes pages de la télévision sénégalaise. De Guinguinéo aux studios de la Rts, des routes du Sénégal à l’autorégulation des médias, retour sur le parcours d’un pionnier animé par « une conviction chevillée à l’âme » : celle d’un journalisme professionnel et responsable. Plus de 15 ans après avoir pris sa retraite, Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye ne s’attend plus forcément à être reconnu dans la rue. Pourtant, chaque soir, il s’invitait dans tous les foyers sénégalais en tant que présentateur vedette, reporter, ou réalisateur de documentaires marquants de la télévision nationale. Dans les années 80 où la petite lucarne était rare et précieuse, il ne passait pas inaperçu : les agents de la Radiodiffusion télévision nationale (Rts) devenant des figures publiques majeures, des « stars » respectées et reconnues dans la rue, portant sur leurs épaules une lourde responsabilité, celle d’informateurs du peuple, garants de la cohésion nationale et témoins privilégiés des premières transformations du Sénégal post-colonial. Aujourd’hui, le septuagénaire s’en souvient avec sa voix timbrée, marquée par des décennies de pratiques au micro. « Les temps ont beaucoup changé. Nous, nous avons vécu la belle époque, hein ! », sourit-il. Une époque où « il y avait une seule chaîne de télévision », avec seulement douze reporters pour couvrir le pays et sept ou huit présentateurs pour assurer les journaux. De Guinguinéo aux bancs du Cesti Mais il suffit parfois d’un regard appuyé pour que vienne la phrase qui ramène l’ancien directeur de la télévision nationale de 2007 à 2009, à ses années de gloire sur le petit écran : « Je vous connais. Je vous ai beaucoup regardé à la télévision et c’est en partie grâce à vous que je suis devenu ce que je suis, vous avez participé à ma formation », lui lance un jour, à bord d’un avion, un fonctionnaire international. Le fait est anecdotique, mais derrière cette scène de reconnaissance, il y a surtout une longue histoire avec le journalisme sénégalais. En effet, Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye de son vrai nom Ibrahima Ndiaye porte cette histoire comme une mémoire vivante. Pendant plus de trois décennies, de la fin des années 70 au début des années 2010, celui que l’on surnomme Ndiaye 2 pour le distinguer d’un autre Ibrahima Ndiaye à la Rts a traversé les grandes mutations sociopolitiques du Sénégal avec l’éthique professionnelle chevillée au corps. Né en 1954 à Guinguinéo dans la région de Kaolack, ce fils de cheminot a grandi au milieu des rails, dans un Sénégal en pleine transition. À une époque où Guinguinéo fut un véritable nœud ferroviaire, il y effectue toute sa scolarité primaire, brièvement à l’école de Guinguinéo 1, puis à l’école de Guinguinéo 2 situé au quartier Campement, construite pour éviter aux enfants la traversée des voies ferrées. « Ma maman me tenait par le bras. Elle me faisait traverser la gare, et quand elle finissait, elle me lâchait la main et je pouvais aller à l’école », se souvient-il. À l’époque, les journées se prolongent parfois par des parties de chasse avec les camarades. Lapins, lièvres et varans sont ramenés au village, puis viennent le thé, le pain tout chaud fraichement sorti de la boulangerie et les longues veillées. Des souvenirs d’enfance qu’il ressasse aujourd’hui avec une pointe de nostalgie. Alors comme un bon fils de cheminot, après son Cm2, sa mère souhaitait le voir intégrer l’école du chemin de fer de Thiès pour prendre la relève paternelle, mais son instituteur s’y oppose fermement. Dans la foulée, lui et six autres élèves de sa classe vont être directement orientés au lycée Charles de Gaulle de Saint-Louis, réservé à l’époque aux meilleurs élèves. Il y reste deux ans de 1967 à 1969 avant de rejoindre le lycée Malick Sy de Thiès où il obtient son Bepc puis son Baccalauréat et prend, « presque sur un coup de tête », le chemin du Cesti. À l’école de la Rts Mais en réalité, pour Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye, la vocation journalistique était déjà là. Selon lui, il remonte à un soir de 1970, lorsqu’adolescent, il écoute à la radio des reporters raconter la Coupe du Monde au Mexique remporté cette année-là par les Brésiliens. « Je me suis pris à rêver en me disant : mais attends. Ces reporters-là, ils sont partout dans le monde. Ils sont témoins de tout, ça doit être un très beau métier. Et j’ai dit : Ah ! Moi, je veux devenir journaliste. », raconte-t-il. Dieu faisant bien les choses, en 1975 après, son Baccalauréat, en vacances à Dakar, il aperçut le fameux bus du Cesti surnommé le « Dragon » et découvre qu’il s’agit de l’école de journalisme. C’est ainsi qu’il postule au concours d’entrée. En octobre 1976, il est retenu parmi la 7e promotion aux côtés de Babacar Touré, Mamadou Koumé, Fatoumata Sow, Martin Faye, Sidy Gaye, Ibrahima Fall avec d’autres camarades venus d’autres pays africains. À sa sortie du Cesti, en 1979, Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye est recruté à la télévision nationale après avoir traversé une période de chômage. « Le chômage dont vous vous plaignez ne date pas d’aujourd’hui », rappelle-t-il, malicieusement. Toutefois, dans ce tournant des années 1980-1981, période charnière marquée par l’émergence d’une génération de professionnels de l’audiovisuel, le jeune journaliste s’impose rapidement au sein de la rédaction de l’Office de Radiodiffusion Télévision du Sénégal (Orts) devenu la Rts en 1992. Aux côtés de pionniers comme Babacar Diagne, Mactar Sylla, Guila Thiam, Cheikhou Omar Seck et, notamment, Pathé Fall Dièye, puis de bien d’autres professionnels qui rejoindront la maison, il contribue à écrire quelques-unes des belles pages de l’information audiovisuelle sénégalaise. Sa trajectoire suscite encore le respect de ceux qui l’ont côtoyé. Abdoulaye Ndiaye, ancien collègue de la Rts et aujourd’hui formateur au Cesti, résume : « C’est un personnage qui a le journalisme chevillé à l’âme. » Le journaliste devenu passeur Il souligne sa « rigueur professionnelle », sa culture et son goût du reportage. « Il était également un bon reporter. On sentait la patte du professionnel », témoigne-t-il. De fait, son goût du terrain est d’ailleurs attesté par le genre grand reportage qu’il affectionnait tant et qu’il a contribué à vulgariser au sein de la rédaction de la télévision avec notamment son documentaire « Fruits et légumes du Sénégal ». Au-delà de son travail de reporter, Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye s’est illustré comme l’un des plus redoutables intervieweurs de sa génération. Son émission « Champ contre champ » demeure, à ce titre, un moment d’anthologie de la télévision sénégalaise. Le journaliste chevronné laissera aussi son empreinte à la Rts comme directeur de la télévision. À ce poste, il lance notamment « Ndef Leng », consacré à la culture sérère, et « Kenkeliba », émission matinale qui rencontre un large écho et dont le concept sera ensuite repris par plusieurs chaînes sénégalaises. « Je voulais imprimer ma marque », explique-t-il. Après son départ de la télévision publique en 2011, il continue de mettre son expertise au service du paysage audiovisuel. C’est ainsi qu’il fonde « Bluecom-Stratégies », un cabinet de conseil et d’expertise en communication avec l’ancien journaliste du quotidien Le Soleil Cheikh Tidiane Fall. Auparavant, le doyen Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye a eu une carrière internationale à l’Uemoa durant le magistère de Cheikh Hadjibou Soumaré à la Commission, après son passage à la Primature en tant Chef de la Cellule communication. Mais porté par la défense des principes éthiques, c’est finalement au Tribunal des pairs du Cored qu’Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye trouve une autre manière de servir le métier. Et au décès d’Eugénie Rokhaya Aw, il est élu à l’unanimité, en octobre 2022, à la présidence du Tribunal. Cette succession a pour lui une résonance particulière. Eugénie l’avait elle-même préparé à prendre le relais. Il parle d’un « passage de témoin post-mortem ». Aujourd’hui, son rôle dépasse la seule fonction institutionnelle. Analysant aujourd’hui, l’évolution du paysage médiatique, son diagnostic est sans concession. Pour le président du Cored, les défis de la presse sont colossaux allant de la confusion des genres sur les plateaux à la banalisation de la revue de presse par des animateurs en passant par la précarisation économique. Ainsi, en tant que « gardien du Temple », Ibrahima Souleymane Ndiaye plaide pour un journalisme fort, exigeant et respecté pour la bonne santé de la démocratie sénégalaise. Par Souleymane WANE

items.title: Renforcement de l’accès à l’eau potable : Korsimoro se dote d’un système innovant et futuriste capable de desservir 15 000 habitants
items.description: Dans le cadre du suivi de la campagne agropastorale 2026-2027, le Ministre d’État, Ministre de l’Agriculture, de l’Eau, des Ressources animales et halieutiques, le Camarade Commandant Ismaël SOMBIÉ, a effectué, ce lundi 21 septembre 2026, une visite du Système d’adduction d’eau potable (AEPS) de Korsimoro, dans la région des Koulsé. Cette infrastructure, réalisée dans le cadre du Programme d’Approvisionnement en Eau et d’Assainissement (PAEA), renforce durablement l’accès à l’eau potable dans la commune. Le dispositif repose sur deux forages d’un débit de 15 m³ par heure chacun, soit une capacité totale de 30 m³ par heure. Leur interconnexion permet d’alimenter un château d’eau désormais entièrement réalisé et opérationnel. Le réseau de distribution, qui s’étend sur 32 kilomètres, améliore ainsi la couverture en eau potable dans les différents secteurs de la commune. L’investissement comprend également 400 branchements particuliers réalisés gratuitement au profit des populations. Il prévoit en outre la réhabilitation de 18 bornes-fontaines et la construction de 15 nouvelles, rapprochant davantage le service d’eau potable des ménages. Avec une capacité de production pouvant répondre aux besoins de 15 000 habitants, contre un besoin actuel estimé à environ 5 000 habitants, le système offre une marge importante pour accompagner la croissance démographique de Korsimoro. Selon les projections présentées, cette capacité devrait permettre de couvrir les besoins de la commune jusqu’à l’horizon 2030. L’innovation du dispositif réside également dans son autonomie énergétique. Le système fonctionne grâce à un champ solaire couplé à des batteries au lithium, qui permettent de stocker l’énergie produite pendant les périodes d’ensoleillement. Cette énergie emmagasinée assure la continuité du fonctionnement lorsque la production solaire diminue ou s’interrompt. L’installation peut ainsi atteindre 15 heures d’autonomie, tandis que le surplus d’énergie produit est également stocké pour renforcer la régularité de l’alimentation. Le projet anticipe par ailleurs l’évolution future de la demande. Quatre forages ont été réalisés en réserve et les travaux préparatoires nécessaires à leur intégration au réseau sont déjà effectués. Leur mise en service pourra donc accompagner progressivement l’augmentation des besoins, sans nécessiter une reprise complète des infrastructures existantes. À l’issue de la visite, le Ministre d’État Ismaël SOMBIÉ a salué la réalisation de cette infrastructure, qui apporte une réponse concrète aux besoins des populations de Korsimoro. Il a rappelé que l’accès à l’eau potable est un droit et non un luxe. À ce titre, les investissements engagés doivent permettre de garantir aux populations un accès régulier, durable et équitable à cette ressource essentielle. À Korsimoro, l’accès à l’eau potable franchit ainsi une étape importante avec un dispositif qui combine augmentation de la capacité de production, extension du réseau, autonomie énergétique et possibilités d’extension. Une approche qui traduit l’engagement du Gouvernement de rapprocher durablement l’eau potable des populations et d’anticiper l’évolution de leurs besoins. DCRP/MAERAH

items.title: Los expertos alertan de que el creciente coste de las pensiones obliga a desatender la sanidad o la educación
items.description: La Comisión del Pacto de Toledo debe renovar sus recomendaciones próximamente y, para ello, está escuchando las comparecencias de economistas expertos en pensiones. En la jornada de este martes, han intervenido el director ejecutivo de la Fundación de Estudios de Economía Aplicada (FEDEA), Ángel de la Fuente, y el profesor de Teoría Económica de la Universidad de Alcalá Daniel Fuentes. Ambos han coincidido, con matices, en que el problema del creciente gasto en pensiones, y como parte del enfrentamiento generacional que podría subyacer de fondo, radica en lo que los economistas llaman “coste de oportunidad”. Este concepto implica que, dentro de un presupuesto público que no es ilimitado, todo el crecimiento de la nómina para pagar la renta de los jubilados es dinero que se detrae de otros destinos de los servicios públicos, como sanidad, educación o infraestructuras. items.title: Counterfeit currency syndicates used churches to hide printing operations – National Security Council Secretariat
items.description: Counterfeit currency syndicates deliberately exploited churches and administrative offices of some religious organisations to conceal their printing operations, the National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS) has revealed. The Secretariat said the use of religious premises was among the key operational patterns uncovered during intelligence-led raids conducted between June 12 and July 24, 2026. According to the NSCS, the syndicates used the premises to reduce suspicion around the noise and vibration generated by printing machines, as well as for storage of materials and finished counterfeit currency. The disclosure forms part of findings from a major security operation targeting transnational and domestic criminal networks involved in the alleged large-scale production, possession and distribution of counterfeit Ghanaian and foreign currencies. In a statement issued on Tuesday, September 22, the NSCS said tactical units carried out six coordinated raids across operational locations in the Greater Accra Region and surrounding districts. The operations resulted in the arrest of 16 principal suspects, comprising Ghanaian and foreign nationals, and the dismantling of four printing hubs. Security agencies seized four counterfeit currency printing machines, six vehicles and two motorcycles allegedly used to transport and distribute the counterfeit currency. They also recovered US$543,000, GH¢196,600 and CFA 60,000 in finished counterfeit notes. A further US$5,293,500, GH¢19,553,700 and CFA 623,550,000 in coupons yet to be processed and printed were also seized. One of the significant operations occurred on June 29 at Lashibi and Klagon. The NSCS said a raid on an office facility in Lashibi led to the arrest of five suspects and the seizure of printing equipment. Follow-up intelligence subsequently took security teams to the headquarters of a religious facility in Klagon. The Secretariat said searches there revealed that administrative offices and residential quarters were allegedly being used as a production and storage facility for the counterfeit currency operation. One printing machine and two operational vehicles were seized, along with large quantities of counterfeit currency coupons. Rev. Emmanuel Boakye-Danquah was identified by the NSCS as being at large in connection with the operation. The allegations against the named suspect remain subject to the ongoing legal process. The NSCS said its investigations revealed a structured system involving different levels of the alleged criminal networks. These included transnational facilitators responsible for cross-border distribution, technical operators handling the printing process, and commercial courier riders who allegedly used motorcycles to deliver counterfeit notes and coupons. The Secretariat said the seizure of millions of finished notes and unprocessed coupons, together with four printing machines capable of producing millions of notes, prevented potential disruption to the economy. It said the circulation of such volumes of counterfeit currency could contribute to artificial inflation, exchange-rate distortions and instability in the financial sector. The NSCS said all 16 arrested suspects have been formally remanded into state custody. Case dockets have been completed and submitted to the Office of the Attorney-General and Ministry of Justice, with prosecution proceedings ongoing at the Accra High Court, General Jurisdiction. Special intelligence teams are also continuing efforts to locate and arrest suspects who remain at large. The NSCS said state prosecutors have initiated processes for the court-ordered forfeiture of vehicles, printing equipment and mobile devices allegedly used in the operations. The Secretariat has urged members of the public, financial institutions, property owners and administrators of religious facilities to conduct due diligence on activities taking place on their premises. It is also asking the public to report suspicious high-volume printing activities, particularly late at night, as well as unusual foreign currency transactions, to the nearest security agency.

items.title: ONU : l’Afrique relance sa bataille pour des sièges permanents au Conseil de sécurité
items.description: L'Afrique entend profiter de la 81e session de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies pour renforcer sa demande d'une representation permanente au Conseil de securite. Le president de la Commission de l'Union africaine (UA), Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, conduit a New York une delegation de responsables africains avec pour objectif de faire entendre une position commune sur la reforme du systeme multilateral, notamment en matiere de paix et de securite. L'UA defend une reforme jugee necessaire pour rendre le Conseil de securite plus representatif de l'ordre international actuel. Selon sa position, fondee sur le consensus d'Ezulwini adopte en 2005 et la Declaration de Syrte, l'Afrique doit obtenir au moins deux sieges permanents dotes de l'ensemble des prerogatives, y compris le droit de veto tant que celui-ci existe, ainsi que cinq sieges non permanents. Le continent ne dispose actuellement d'aucun siege permanent au Conseil de securite. Celui-ci compte 15 membres, dont cinq permanents – Chine, etats-Unis, France, Royaume-Uni et Russie – et dix membres elus pour des mandats de deux ans. L'Afrique occupe regulierement des sieges elus, mais reste absente de la categorie permanente.. L'Afrique du Sud entend notamment utiliser les negociations intergouvernementales engagees aux Nations unies pour faire progresser cette revendication. Son ambassadeur aupres de l'ONU a New York, Mxolisi Sizo Nkosi, a indique que Pretoria souhaitait accelerer les discussions sur l'elargissement du Conseil et continuer a defendre le consensus d'Ezulwini. Pour Pretoria, l'absence de l'Afrique parmi les membres permanents ne correspond ni au poids demographique du continent, qui compte plus d'un milliard d'habitants, ni a son importance economique et geopolitique. L'ambassadeur sud-africain souligne egalement que de nombreux conflits auxquels le Conseil de securite doit repondre se deroulent sur le continent africain. Washington oppose son veto au droit de veto La question des pouvoirs associes a ces futurs sieges constitue toutefois l'un des principaux points de desaccord. Selon les elements presentes dans les textes, les etats-Unis se sont declares favorables a l'attribution de deux sieges permanents a l'Afrique, mais sans droit de veto. Une formule qui ne correspond pas a la position de l'UA, qui reclame des sieges disposant des memes prerogatives que les autres membres permanents. La reforme se heurte egalement a des divergences au sein meme du continent. Le consensus d'Ezulwini prevoit que l'Afrique designe elle-meme ses representants, mais les etats membres n'ont pas encore arrete de mecanisme contraignant pour departager les differentes candidatures. Plusieurs puissances regionales sont susceptibles de pretendre a ces sieges, notamment l'Afrique du Sud, le Nigeria et l'egypte. Les rivalites entre le Maroc et l'Algerie compliquent egalement l'emergence d'une position commune en Afrique du Nord, tandis que plusieurs pays d'Afrique de l'Est mettent en avant leur role diplomatique et securitaire. Deux pistes de compromis sont evoquees : une repartition geographique entre l'Afrique du Nord et l'Afrique subsaharienne, ou un systeme de rotation entre les cinq regions du continent. Cette derniere option souleve toutefois la question de la permanence institutionnelle attachee aux sieges concernes. Au-dela de la composition du Conseil, l'UA met en avant une contradiction entre son ambition de renforcer l'autonomie africaine et sa dependance financiere vis-a-vis de partenaires exterieurs. L'Union africaine tire en effet une part importante de son budget et de ses operations de paix et de securite de financements internationaux.

items.title: NPP press conference on drug busts should be treated with contempt – NDC
items.description: The Deputy Director of Elections and IT of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Rashid Tanko-Computer, has called for the New Patriotic Party’s (NPP) recent press conference on drug busts to be treated with contempt. Speaking on JoyNews’ The Pulse on Tuesday, September 22, he questioned the credibility of the NPP’s concerns, citing what he described as the party’s record on drug management while in government. “You should dismiss them completely. In fact, if this call was coming from CPP, PNC, or other political party, maybe one would have taken note of their concern. But NPP, look, the history of drug management in this country. In fact, it doesn’t support it,” he said. Mr Tanko-Computer, however, said the allegations raised by the NPP should not be ignored entirely, particularly claims that clandestine laboratories are operating in Ghana. He urged the NPP to provide the relevant information to the security agencies if it has evidence to support its claims. “I listened to the press conference, and I’m sure the National Security Secretariat and other allied security agencies listened to the press conference, because it appeared this group of people they have a lot of information about these drugs,” he stated. Read also: NPP links resurgence of drug trafficking cases to NDC’s return to power “If you have clear information about these dealings, we are open for information as a government. Come and give us more information,” he added. His comments follow a press conference by NPP National Organiser Henry Nana Boakye over the current drug busts linked to Ghana. At the event, Mr Boakye accused the NDC of having a history of association with illicit drug trafficking. Nana B, as he is popularly known as Nana B, claimed that the emergence of recent drug-related cases following the NDC’s return to power was evidence of a link between the party and the illicit drug trade. He cited the case of Nayele Ametefeh, who was arrested at Heathrow Airport in the United Kingdom in November 2014 for transporting cocaine from Ghana during President John Mahama’s first administration. Mr Ametefeh was found with about 12.5 kilogrammes of cocaine and was subsequently convicted and sentenced to eight years and eight months in prison by a British court. Mr Boakye argued on Tuesday, September 22, that recent narcotics-related incidents involving consignments reportedly traced to Ghana mirrored developments recorded under the previous Mahama administration. He described the situation as disturbing, claiming that illicit drug trafficking had resurfaced following the NDC’s return to government. “We have been here before, don’t forget. Ghanaians have not forgotten the Nayele Ametefe scandal under the first Mahama administration, where this drug trafficker was afforded the courtesy of the VVIP wing at the Kotoka International Airport before her arrest at Heathrow with cocaine in her bags, an episode that dragged our country’s name through international disgrace,” he said. “Today, under the second Mahama term, the same pattern has resurfaced, the same process has returned, and it has grown to be much worse,” he claimed.

items.title: PHC to take up plea seeking recovery of 'abducted' KP minister Fazal Shakoor
items.description: CHARSADDA/PESHAWAR: The Peshawar High Court (PHC) will take up a petition on Wednesday seeking the recovery of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Minister for Public Health Engineering Fazal Shakoor. The petition was filed on Tuesday, a day after the minister and two other men with him were allegedly abducted by unidentified armed men near Peshawar’s M-1 toll plaza. A case has also been filed at the Chamkani police station on kidnapping charges. Both the petition and the first information report (FIR) were filed on the complaint of the minister’s brother, retired Major Anwar Aziz. The FIR, dated Sept 21 and seen by Dawn , alleged that Fazal, his driver Qaiser Khan and Constable Mujahid were abducted by unidentified armed men near Peshawar’s M-1 toll plaza on Monday afternoon. The plea, filed through advocate Bashir Khan Wazir, requested the PHC to direct the police and other law enforcement agencies to recover the minister, whose whereabouts remain unknown to his family. It also sought directions to the KP inspector general (IG) and the capital city police officer (CCPO) to constitute a high-level inquiry committee to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take steps to recover Fazal. The KP IG, CCPO, the Peshawar senior superintendent of police (SSP) Operations, and other relevant authorities have been made respondents in the petition. It claimed that armed men in plain clothes intercepted his vehicle near the Peshawar Motorway Toll Plaza and fired at its tyres. It further alleged that the armed men then forced the provincial minister out of his vehicle and took him away. The plea described the alleged abduction of the provincial minister in broad daylight as a matter of serious concern and requested the PHC to order his recovery. The petitioner maintained that if the missing minister was in the custody of any state institution or other authority, he should be produced before the court and released if his detention was found to be unlawful. The petition is fixed for hearing on Sept 23 (Wednesday) before a division bench comprising Senior Puisne Judge Justice Ijaz Anwar and Justice Kamran Hayat Miankhel. The FIR invoked Section 365 (kidnapping or abduction) of the Pakistan Penal Code (PPC). According to the complaint, Fazal and the others were travelling from Charsadda to Peshawar to attend a KP Assembly session when they were intercepted by armed men in “black uniforms and plain clothes”. They were taken to an undisclosed location, while the official vehicle they were travelling in was left at the spot, the FIR added. A video shared by the PTI showed several masked armed men approaching the minister’s car. In the video, one of the masked men grabs the door of the car to open it while another is seen firing shots at the tyres of the moving vehicle. MNA picked up en route to protest: PTI PTI also claimed its MNA Fazal Muhammad Khan was abducted by unidentified men within the limits of Mardan’s Sheikh Maltoon police station. Waqar Khan, personal secretary to Khan, told Dawn that the MNA was travelling from Islamabad to Charsadda when unidentified men intercepted his vehicle near the Rashakai Interchange on the Mardan Bypass. He said the attackers fired at the tyres of the vehicle before taking the MNA away. According to him, the unidentified men were dressed in black clothes. Khan was travelling to Charsadda to attend a protest demonstration against the alleged abduction of Fazal. That protest was held later in the afternoon at Charsadda’s Farooq Azam Chowk, with PTI leaders and workers demanding the minister’s immediate recovery. The protesters also called for the release of political workers allegedly detained in connection with the party’s activities. Declaring their support for the PTI’s planned march to Islamabad on Sept 27, the workers said they would demand an end to “state oppression”, supremacy of the Constitution and law, and the establishment of a “genuine system” in the country. PTI leaders address a protest demonstration at Farooq Azam Chowk in Charsadda against the alleged abduction of Minister for Public Health Engineering Fazal Shakoor Khan on Sept 22, 2026. — photo via Faiz Muhammad Furthermore, the PTI leaders expressed concern over the alleged detention of Khan and condemned the registration of a case against KP Minister for Communication and Works Shakil Khan. They said the alleged incidents involving elected representatives were a matter of concern and demanded that Fazal and Khan be brought before the public immediately. If detained, they said, the two lawmakers should be produced before a court in accordance with the law. The speakers questioned the situation of ordinary citizens, contending that if elected representatives could allegedly face such treatment under their own provincial government, the plight of common people could only be worse. In a statement posted on X, KP Information Minister Shafi Jan termed the “picking up” of Fazal a “direct attack on the Constitution, law, democracy and public mandate”. “We will not be intimidated by such tactics. Snatching away the right to peaceful political struggle is the height of fascism, but we will continue to fight for our rights while remaining within the bounds of the Constitution and law,” he said.

items.title: Sénégal: 984 détenus bénéficient de la grâce présidentielle
items.description: Le président sénégalais Bassirou Diomaye Faye a accordé une grâce à 984 personnes définitivement condamnées. La mesure, annoncée, ce mardi 22 septembre 2026, par le ministère de la Justice, vise notamment à réduire la surpopulation carcérale et à favoriser la réinsertion des bénéficiaires. Le chef de l’État sénégalais, Bassirou Diomaye Faye, a accordé une nouvelle mesure de clémence à 984 personnes condamnées, à travers des décrets signés le 21 septembre 2026. La répartition des bénéficiaires se présente comme suit: 921 condamnés bénéficient d’une remise totale de peine. À ce groupe s’ajoutent 21 détenus gravement malades, 19 détenus mineurs et un détenu âgé de plus de 65 ans, qui bénéficient eux aussi d’une remise totale de peine. Au total, 962 personnes sont donc concernées par une remise totale de peine. Par ailleurs, 18 condamnés bénéficient d’une remise partielle de peine, tandis que quatre personnes condamnées à la réclusion criminelle à perpétuité voient leur peine commuée. L’ensemble de ces mesures porte ainsi à 984 le nombre total de bénéficiaires de la grâce présidentielle. Selon le ministère de la Justice, cette décision participe aux efforts engagés pour lutter contre la surpopulation carcérale, améliorer les conditions de détention et favoriser la réinsertion sociale des personnes ayant déjà exécuté une partie de leur peine. La grâce présidentielle relève des prérogatives constitutionnelles du chef de l’État. Elle peut être accordée aux personnes définitivement condamnées, conformément aux dispositions légales en vigueur. En avril 2025, le président sénégalais avait déjà accordé une grâce à 1 121 personnes condamnées pour diverses infractions. Avec ces nouvelles mesures, les autorités sénégalaises poursuivent leur démarche de désengorgement des établissements pénitentiaires, tout en ouvrant la voie à la réinsertion de centaines de condamnés. Par Valentin SOMANDE L’article Sénégal: 984 détenus bénéficient de la grâce présidentielle est apparu en premier sur Wakat Séra .

Simple lance une première au Maroc avec l’alimentation instantanée du compte par carte bancaire
items.description: Simple innove sur le marché bancaire marocain en proposant, pour la première fois au Maroc, la possibilité d’alimenter instantanément son compte dès son ouverture à partir de n’importe quelle carte bancaire, nationale ou internationale, quelle que soit la banque émettrice. Une solution inédite qui permet au client de disposer immédiatement de ses fonds et d’utiliser son compte sans attendre. Finis les délais d'attente liés aux virements classiques et les déplacements en agence. Avec Simple, la néobanque d'Attijariwafa bank, l'autonomie du client est placée au cœur de l'expérience bancaire. Dès l'ouverture de son compte via l'application, le client a désormais la liberté de l'alimenter instantanément. L'avantage majeur de cette nouvelle fonctionnalité réside dans son universalité, puisque l'opération peut s'effectuer au moyen de n'importe quelle carte bancaire, qu'elle soit nationale ou internationale, et quelle que soit la banque émettrice. Un parcours digitalisé en quelques clics Conçue pour garantir une expérience sans friction, l'alimentation du compte s'effectue en un parcours extrêmement court. Le client saisit le montant qu'il souhaite verser, renseigne les informations de la carte bancaire à débiter, puis valide l'opération en toute sécurité. Le résultat est immédiat. Les fonds sont rendus disponibles sur le compte Simple à la seconde même. items.title: Don’t abandon working policies because of politics – Asiedu Nketiah
items.description: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has called for greater policy continuity in Ghana, urging successive governments to improve programmes that are delivering results instead of abandoning them because they were initiated by their predecessors. He said although governments had a responsibility to discontinue policies that were failing, there was little justification for scrapping effective programmes simply because political administrations had changed. Mr Asiedu Nketiah was speaking at the 4th Bono Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards in Sunyani on Saturday, September 19, 2026. “There is another habit we have developed in our politics that we should correct. We abandon too much,” he said. According to him, a change of government could sometimes result in an existing programme being renamed or restructured, with additional public funds spent to achieve almost the same objective. He said such an approach deprived the country of the full benefit of investments already made. “Of course, a government must change policies that are failing, and nobody should continue a bad programme for the sake of continuity. But where something is working and public money has already been invested in it, the sensible thing is to improve it and allow the country to receive the benefit,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said Ghana needed to use the improving economic conditions as an opportunity to think beyond recovery and determine what should be built on the stability being achieved. The Ghana Statistical Service currently reports 6.0% annual GDP growth for the second quarter of 2026 and inflation of 5.0% for August 2026. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the significance of economic improvement would ultimately depend on whether it translated into better incomes, stronger businesses and improved living conditions. He said infrastructure investments should also be assessed according to the economic activity they were expected to generate. “If we borrow money to construct a road, our interest should continue after the road has been commissioned. We should know what economic activity the road is expected to support and whether that activity is actually developing,” he said. Using the Bono Region as an example, he said investment in roads should be complemented by measures to improve agricultural processing, storage, logistics and access to markets so that farmers could retain more value from their produce. He said the same principle should apply to other sectors, with government planning ahead for population growth, urbanisation, energy demand, housing, transport and the changing skills requirements of the labour market. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said Ghana had experienced situations where good policies were abandoned and bad policies were defended for too long because admitting mistakes was difficult in politics. He therefore urged political leaders to learn from previous experiences and make decisions based on what worked for the country rather than political ownership. “We should also have enough confidence as a country to preserve what works, regardless of who started it,” he said. He said continuity did not mean preserving every programme or policy indefinitely, but maintaining useful interventions while improving areas that required change. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said such an approach was particularly important because Ghana had already spent considerable public resources on development programmes and could not afford to repeatedly start from the beginning. He said journalists also had an important role to play by tracking government programmes over time and establishing whether commitments made by administrations translated into results. He urged the media to keep records that would allow citizens to assess development commitments years after their announcement. “Five years from now, it should be possible for somebody to go into the archives of the media in Bono and reconstruct what happened to the major development commitments being made today,” he said.

items.title: Céramique : le grand retour des Espagnols en Algérie
items.description: Le secteur de la céramique était l’un des plus affectés par la crise entre l’Algérie et l’Espagne. La suspension du commerce bilatéral à partir de juin 2022 a causé de grosses pertes notamment aux fabricants d'équipements et d'intrants qui faisaient une grande partie de leur chiffre d’affaires en Algérie. Les choses sont revenues à la normale entre Alger et Madrid à partir de novembre 2023 et le commerce a repris. Les fabricants de machinerie pour céramique espagnols ont pu reconquérir leurs parts de marché en Algérie , assure leur représentant. Céramique : les affaires reprennent entre l’Espagne et l’Algérie José Miquel est président de l'Asebec, l’association espagnole des fabricants d'équipements pour l’industrie de la céramique . Dans un entretien au journal El Periodico Mediterraneo, il a fait état d’une grave crise qui affecte la filière. “La production et les ventes de céramique stagnent, et aucun investissement dans de nouvelles machines n'est réalisé. De ce fait, la maintenance et les petits investissements indispensables sont les seuls éléments qui nous permettent de survivre”, dit-il. Pour se redéployer, l’organisation professionnelle axe ses efforts sur les zones où ses membres comptent leurs principaux clients internationaux, notamment l'Amérique centrale et du Sud et l’Afrique du Nord. José Miquel a été interrogé particulièrement sur le marché algérien, l’un des plus importants pour la filière espagnole des équipements de céramique. Selon lui, les affaires ont repris leur cours normal. “Dans de nombreux cas, nous avons réussi à reconquérir les clients avec lesquels nous travaillions”, a-t-il assuré, tout en déplorant que les Espagnols ont perdu en Algérie des projets sur le point d'être finalisés. Avant même la crise politique qui a aggravé les choses, les affaires avec l'Algérie étaient déjà affectées par la crise sanitaire. “L'Algérie était et reste l'un de nos plus gros clients” “Pendant le confinement, nous n'avons pas pu accéder aux nouveaux projets remportés par nos concurrents, ce qui nous a parfois même exclus du marché. Ces deux années d'impossibilité de collaborer avec nos clients nous ont fortement pénalisés à tous les niveaux d'une relation commerciale normale, d'autant plus que le confinement a été brutal”, a souligné José Miquel qui se félicite toutefois de la reconquête par les espagnols de leurs débouchés en Algérie. “L'Algérie était et reste l'un de nos plus gros clients, et heureusement, grâce à de nombreux efforts, nous avons réussi à le reconquérir”, assure-t-il. L’Asebec avait notamment organisé en mai dernier des rencontres à Sétif et Batna avec la participation de plusieurs entreprises espagnoles qui ont présenté leurs produits aux producteurs de céramique de l’est algérien. Avec une quarantaine d'entreprises et une production de 200 millions de mètres carrés par an, le marché algérien est très important pour l’industrie espagnole de machineries et d'intrants de céramique. L’article Céramique : le grand retour des Espagnols en Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: National Security arrests 16 and seizes millions in counterfeit currency and printing equipment
items.description: The National Security Council Secretariat (NSCS), working with security and intelligence agencies, says it has dismantled four major counterfeit currency printing hubs and arrested 16 suspects in a nationwide crackdown on criminal syndicates. The operations, conducted between June 12 and July 24, 2026, targeted networks allegedly involved in the large-scale printing, possession and distribution of counterfeit Ghanaian and foreign currencies. In a statement issued on Tuesday, September 22, the NSCS said six coordinated raids were conducted across the Greater Accra Region and surrounding districts following months of covert intelligence gathering. The operations resulted in the seizure of counterfeit currency printing equipment, vehicles, motorcycles and large quantities of finished counterfeit notes and unprocessed currency coupons. The NSCS said the operations yielded four counterfeit currency printing machines, six vehicles and two motorcycles allegedly used to transport and distribute the counterfeit currency. Security agencies also seized: US$543,000 , GH¢196,600 and CFA 60,000 in finished counterfeit notes. US$5,293,500 , GH¢19,553,700 and CFA 623,550,000 in unprocessed coupons allegedly intended for further printing. The 16 arrested suspects, together with physical and digital exhibits, have been transferred to the Bureau of National Intelligence (BNI) for forensic examination and further legal processes. The NSCS said case dockets had been completed and submitted to the Office of the Attorney-General and Ministry of Justice, with prosecution proceedings ongoing at the Accra High Court, General Jurisdiction. The first raid took place at Amuzu, a suburb of Kasoa, on June 12. According to the NSCS, operatives targeted a residential compound allegedly operating under the cover of a traditional spiritual centre. One suspect, Nana Nyarko Derrick Dapaah, was arrested, while security personnel seized a printing machine, fake gold bars, five mobile phones and assorted counterfeit notes and coupons. A second operation targeted what the NSCS described as a transnational criminal cell allegedly moving high-grade foreign counterfeit currency between commercial centres using unregistered vehicles. Seven suspects — three Ghanaians and four foreign nationals — were arrested. Three unregistered vehicles and US$65,900 in counterfeit notes were also seized. On June 29, security operatives raided an office facility at Lashibi and Klagon, arresting five people and recovering printing equipment. The NSCS said follow-up intelligence led investigators to the headquarters of a religious facility in Klagon, where administrative offices and residential quarters were allegedly being used as a production and storage facility. One printing machine and two operational vehicles were seized. The security agency also reported the seizure of US$5,287,900, CFA 623,530,000 and GH¢7,129,000 in counterfeit coupons. Rev. Emmanuel Boakye-Danquah was named by the NSCS as being at large in connection with the operation. On July 9, security operatives near the Lakeside Shell Filling Station intercepted a commercial dispatch rider allegedly transporting pre-packaged counterfeit currency to buyers. Issah Ibrahim was arrested, while Adamu Haruna was listed as being at large. Five boxes containing counterfeit GH¢200 notes, with an estimated face value of GH¢12,421,600, were seized together with two registered motorcycles. In another operation, Solomon Acheampong, 54, was arrested at what the NSCS described as a regional distribution point. Amankwah Bismark was identified as a suspected kingpin who remains at large. A white Toyota Corolla, three mobile phones, GH¢500 in genuine currency and assorted counterfeit coupons were seized. On July 24, operatives raided a hotel facility at Achimota Mile 7 and arrested Osman Iddrisu, 50, whom the NSCS described as a key technical operator. The agency said he was found with mobile printing equipment. A subsequent search of his residence at Amasaman uncovered what investigators described as a fully equipped secondary printing facility. Two printing machines and quantities of counterfeit notes and coupons were seized. The NSCS said intelligence analysis of the dismantled networks revealed that some of the syndicates deliberately exploited churches and administrative premises of religious organisations. According to the Secretariat, the premises allegedly provided a degree of cover by reducing suspicion around the presence of printing equipment and facilitating the storage of materials. The agency said the syndicates operated through structured networks involving alleged transnational facilitators, technical printing operators and commercial couriers who used motorcycles to distribute counterfeit currency. It said the seizure of millions of finished notes and unprocessed coupons, together with four printing machines capable of producing large volumes, prevented what it described as a potential threat to monetary stability. The NSCS said widespread circulation of counterfeit currency could contribute to artificial inflation, exchange-rate distortions and disruption to the financial sector. The NSCS said all 16 arrested suspects have been formally remanded into state custody. Special intelligence teams remain deployed to locate and arrest other suspects identified during the investigations. State prosecutors have also begun legal processes seeking the forfeiture of vehicles, printing equipment and mobile devices allegedly used in the operations. The NSCS urged financial institutions, property owners and administrators of religious facilities to exercise greater due diligence over activities conducted on their premises. It also called on the public to report suspicious high-volume printing activities, particularly at unusual hours, as well as unusual foreign currency transactions, to the nearest security agency.

items.title: Guerre en Iran : Trump peine à trouver le bon message avant les élections de mi-mandat
items.description: a six semaines des elections de mi-mandat, la guerre contre l'Iran devient un probleme interieur pour Donald Trump. Declenche en fevrier, le conflit devait initialement etre bref. Pres de sept mois plus tard, il se poursuit, perturbe les exportations energetiques du Moyen-Orient et alimente la hausse des prix des carburants aux etats-Unis. Le president americain cherche desormais a concilier deux messages difficiles a tenir ensemble. D'un cote, il continue de defendre les frappes en affirmant qu'elles etaient necessaires pour empecher l'Iran d'acquerir l'arme nucleaire. Lors de la convention republicaine de Dallas, il a encore justifie la guerre et assure qu'elle prendrait fin « tres peu de temps apres » les elections. De l'autre, il doit convaincre des electeurs davantage preoccupes par leur pouvoir d'achat que par la politique etrangere. Une guerre impopulaire Les sondages illustrent cette difficulte. Une enquete Reuters/Ipsos publiee le 21 septembre mesure l'approbation de Trump a 32 %, son plus bas niveau dans cette serie. Seulement 34 % des personnes interrogees approuvent les frappes contre l'Iran et 17 % sa gestion du coût de la vie. Surtout, 82 % pensent que le conflit pourrait se prolonger. Le sujet commence a provoquer des tensions chez les republicains. Deux candidats au Senat, Mike Rogers dans le Michigan et Ashley Hinson dans l'Iowa, ont appele le 21 septembre a mettre rapidement fin a la guerre, alors qu'ils avaient auparavant soutenu la strategie presidentielle. Ils mettent a present en avant le prix de l'essence et du diesel. Trump reste donc pris entre sa volonte de presenter la campagne contre Teheran comme necessaire a la securite americaine et la promesse qui avait contribue a son retour au pouvoir en 2024 : reduire les prix et eviter les guerres prolongees. a l'approche du scrutin du 3 novembre, l'Iran n'est plus seulement un dossier de politique etrangere : il devient un enjeu electoral directement lie au portefeuille des Americains.

items.title: NPP links resurgence of drug trafficking cases to NDC’s return to power
items.description: The National Organiser of the opposition New Patriotic Party (NPP), Henry Nana Boakye, has accused the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC) of having a history of association with illicit drug trafficking. Speaking at a press conference, Nana B, as he is popularly known, as Nana B, claimed that the emergence of recent drug-related cases following the NDC’s return to power was evidence of a link between the party and the illicit drug trade. He cited the case of Nayele Ametefeh, who was arrested at Heathrow Airport in the United Kingdom in November 2014 for transporting cocaine from Ghana during President John Mahama’s first administration. Mr Ametefeh was found with about 12.5 kilogrammes of cocaine and was subsequently convicted and sentenced to eight years and eight months in prison by a British court. Read also: NPP press conference on drug busts should be treated with contempt – NDC Mr Boakye argued on Tuesday, September 22, that recent narcotics-related incidents involving consignments reportedly traced to Ghana mirrored developments recorded under the previous Mahama administration. He described the situation as disturbing, claiming that illicit drug trafficking had resurfaced following the NDC’s return to government. “We have been here before, don’t forget. Ghanaians have not forgotten the Nayele Ametefe scandal under the first Mahama administration, where this drug trafficker was afforded the courtesy of the VVIP wing at the Kotoka International Airport before her arrest at Heathrow with cocaine in her bags, an episode that dragged our country’s name through international disgrace,” he said. “Today, under the second Mahama term, the same pattern has resurfaced, the same process has returned, and it has grown to be much worse,” he claimed. His comments follow the reported interception of nearly 3.9 tonnes of cocaine at the Port of Dunkirk in France in September 2026. The drugs, valued at an estimated €225 million, were reportedly concealed in a container carrying plastic waste shipped from Ghana. The Narcotics Control Commission later announced the arrest of three people in connection with the consignment and said investigations were continuing.

items.title: KGL Foundation and GNPC Foundation partner to expand educational scholarships for Ghanaian students
items.description: The KGL Foundation and the GNPC Foundation have entered into a strategic partnership to expand educational opportunities for Ghanaian students, bringing the public and private sector together to support the development of the country’s human capital. The partnership agreement signing held at the KGL House seeks to support an additional 1,000 students, building on the GNPC Foundation’s longstanding scholarship programme and the KGL Foundation’s commitment to expanding access to quality education, helping more Ghanaian students to pursue their educational dreams and future aspirations without financial circumstances standing in the way. Speaking at the partnership agreement signing, Alex Apau Dadey, Group Executive Chairman of KGL Group, welcomed the partnership and recounted the personal significance of education to him and how his late father, Dr Alex Dadey, was a distinguished educationist , further strengthening his longstanding appreciation of education as a key driver of opportunity and national development. “True success lies in our ability to create value and ensure that the value we create contributes meaningfully to the lives and communities from which we derive value .” Against this backdrop, Helga J. M. Boadi, Executive Director of the GNPC Foundation said the partnership demonstrates the value of public–private collaboration in addressing national development priorities. She noted that the GNPC Foundation has, to date, supported more than 9,700 students through its national and international scholarship programmes, with approximately 1,390 students currently enrolled under its national scholarship scheme. The collaboration with the KGL Foundation will enable the Foundation to bring an additional 1,000 students into the scholarship programme. Ms Boadi expressed her excitement about the partnership, emphasising that collaboration between public institutions and private enterprises should extend beyond conventional commercial relationships to include purposeful investments in people. She also highlighted the GNPC Foundation’s approach to educational development, noting that its interventions are undertaken in collaboration with institutions including the Ghana Education Service and the Ministry of Education to ensure that educational investments go beyond infrastructure and contribute to stronger learning environments and improved opportunities for students to thrive. Mr Dadey further noted that education remains a key thematic area of the KGL Foundation, which has supported over 300 students and continues to develop partnerships that expand access to educational opportunities. The KGL Foundation’s education initiatives include its partnership with Lancaster University Ghana to support scholarship opportunities for brilliant students with financial needs, refurbishment of the Gloria Boatemaa Dadey Nifa Basic School in Adukrom into a renowned center of learning, the Kwabotwe Centre for Sports Excellence, the UG alumni centre in its final phase and its US$1 million, five-year partnership with the Ghana Football Association to support juvenile football development. Representing the KGL Foundation, Nii Annorbaah Sarpei, Programmes Manager, described the partnership as a significant addition to the Foundation’s growing network of collaborations with public institutions, including GETFund, the Mental Health Authority, the Ghana Education Service and the Ghana Football Association. For both Foundations, the objective is clear: to turn educational opportunity into human potential, and human potential into lasting national progress.

items.title: Asiedu Nketiah urges journalists to report fairly at all times, and not based on politicians’ complaints
items.description: National Chairman of the National Democratic Congress (NDC), Johnson Asiedu Nketiah, has urged journalists to remain independent and resist allowing complaints from politicians to determine whether their reporting is fair. He said journalists must subject claims and allegations to proper scrutiny and report the facts, regardless of whether the outcome was favourable or unfavourable to a political party or government. Mr Asiedu Nketiah was speaking in Sunyani on Saturday, September 19, 2026, when he addressed the 4th Bono Regional Ghana Journalists Association (GJA) Awards, held on the theme: “Ethics, Integrity and Impactful Journalism – Essential Ingredients for Societal Transformation.” He said politicians would naturally have opinions about how the media reported on them, but such opinions should not become the yardstick for determining journalistic fairness. “Journalists should listen to all of us, but the complaint of a politician cannot become the measure of whether a story is fair,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said journalists should report completed projects as such, establish the facts when projects failed and avoid presenting unsubstantiated allegations as facts simply because they made attractive headlines. “If a project has been completed, say so. If it has failed, establish the facts and say so. If somebody makes an allegation and the evidence is not there, do not convert the allegation into a fact simply because it will make an interesting headline,” he said. He said the credibility of journalists was their most valuable professional asset and warned that once public trust was lost, it was difficult to regain. Mr Asiedu Nketiah said the changing information environment made professional journalism even more important, particularly as social media, political parties, governments, companies and individuals could now publish directly to large audiences. He noted that artificial intelligence had also made it possible to manufacture voices, images and other material that could be mistaken for authentic content. “Somebody still has to establish what actually happened, and that responsibility makes professional journalism more important,” he said. The NDC Chairman also called on journalists to maintain a permanent record of major public investments and follow up on them beyond the initial announcements. He encouraged journalists in the Bono Region to track public projects by establishing what had been awarded, who was executing the work, the contractual completion date and whether the public ultimately received what it had paid for. He said such journalism would help citizens assess the performance of governments and create an independent historical record of development projects. “Governments and political parties will naturally tell their own stories. A professional media should leave behind a record that does not depend on the version preferred by either side,” he said. Mr Asiedu Nketiah, who is also the National Chairman of the governing NDC, said the government should expect scrutiny from the media. He said ministers should answer legitimate questions, public expenditure should be examined and government promises should be checked against actual delivery. He also urged politicians to avoid treating difficult questions from journalists as hostility, saying uncomfortable questions could sometimes draw attention to issues that those close to political leaders might be reluctant to raise. He further called for better working conditions for journalists and sustainable media institutions, saying journalists should be able to build respectable careers without becoming financially dependent on politicians, businesses and institutions they are expected to cover. He congratulated journalists who received awards at the ceremony and urged them to protect the professional reputations they had built over the years. “People eventually know which reporter checks the facts, which interviewer understands the subject and which journalist can be trusted when an issue becomes politically difficult,” he said.

items.title: Quand Kiev reste la priorité absolue de l'Élysée : les entreprises liées à l’aide à l’Ukraine intégrées aux plans de crise
items.description: Emmanuel Macron et Volodymyr Zelensky se sont retrouves a New York le 21 septembre pour poursuivre les discussions sur l'aide francaise a l'Ukraine. L'hiver, la defense antiaerienne et la cooperation industrielle etaient au centre des echanges. Paris doit fournir de nouveaux radars et intercepteurs a Kiev. Macron a assure que « la France sera aux cotes de l'Ukraine pour affronter l'hiver ». Les echanges ont aussi porte sur des systemes SAMP/T (Sol-Air Moyenne Portee/Terrestre) supplementaires, leurs missiles, leur possible production en Ukraine et le programme antibalistique FREYJA Macron a egalement evoque avec Donald Trump une « treve energetique » et un « moratoire en mer Noire ». Paris cherche ainsi a maintenir l'implication americaine dans le dossier ukrainien tout en poursuivant ses propres engagements militaires et industriels aupres de Kiev. L'aide a Kiev jusque dans les plans de continuite en France L'importance accordee a l'Ukraine apparaît desormais jusque dans les dispositifs prepares en France face a une panne electrique de grande ampleur. Le scenario serait lourd : feux de circulation hors service, ecoles sans eclairage, metros, trains et ascenseurs a l'arret, telephonie mobile et Internet coupes. Les hopitaux devraient basculer sur leurs generateurs. L'etat doit alors determiner les installations a maintenir en fonctionnement. Centrales electriques, reseaux d'eau, infrastructures ferroviaires et aeroports sont concernes. Mais les usines d'armement et certaines entreprises francaises participant a l'aide a l'Ukraine sont elles aussi integrees aux dispositifs de continuite. Le contraste est notable : meme si une panne majeure devait perturber profondement la vie quotidienne des Francais, Paris prevoit aussi de preserver des capacites industrielles liees a son engagement militaire en Ukraine. Le dossier ukrainien depasse ainsi le seul cadre de la politique etrangere et s'inscrit dans l'organisation de la continuite du pays en situation de crise. Attal cherche a convaincre que l'aide a Kiev sert les interets francais Gabriel Attal s'emploie, de son cote, a donner une justification interieure a cette politique. Invite de BFMTV le 21 septembre 2026, l'ancien Premier ministre a affirme que « defendre l'Ukraine » relevait directement de « l'interet immediat des Francais ». Il s'attache ainsi a presenter la poursuite, voire l'augmentation, de l'aide a Kiev non comme un simple choix de politique etrangere, mais comme une necessite pour la France elle-meme. Pour etayer cette position, Attal multiplie les mises en garde. En cas de victoire russe, il estime que le poids de l'Ukraine sur les marches cerealiers pourrait entraîner une hausse des matieres premieres et de l'inflation, avec des repercussions sur le budget des menages francais. Il evoque egalement le depart possible de millions d'Ukrainiens vers les pays de l'Union europeenne, qui peserait, selon lui, sur les finances publiques et les systemes sociaux. L'ancien Premier ministre va jusqu'a avancer un scenario nucleaire. Il imagine une frappe contre une centrale ukrainienne et, invoquant le precedent de Tchernobyl, affirme qu'un eventuel nuage radioactif ne s'arreterait pas aux frontieres du pays. Autant d'hypotheses qu'Attal utilise pour repondre a ceux qui contestent l'ampleur du soutien francais a Kiev et pour defendre son renforcement. Une limite demeure toutefois dans son discours : l'engagement direct de la France contre la Russie. Interroge sur l'idee de « declarer la guerre a la Russie », Attal a repondu clairement « non ». Il defend donc une aide militaire accrue a Kiev, tout en rejetant officiellement l'entree de la France dans une confrontation directe avec Moscou.

items.title: 2027: I’ll transmit power to VP whenever I’m on vacation — Makinde
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike Presidential candidate of the Action Peoples Movement, APM, Governor Seyi Makinde of Oyo State, has vowed to transmit power to the Vice President whenever he is unavailable, promising to obey the Constitution ‘to the letter’ if elected president in 2027. He made the pledge on Tuesday in Katsina at the APM North-West town meeting, where he outlined his proposed Reset Agenda for the economy, education, security and Nigeria’s political system. Makinde said his pledge on presidential power transfer was consistent with Section 145 of the Constitution, which requires the President to transmit a written declaration to the Senate President and Speaker of the House of Representatives when proceeding on vacation or otherwise unable to discharge the functions of office. “I promise you that, as your President, I will follow the Constitution to the letter. If I am not going to be available, if I am on vacation, I will transmit power to the Vice President. Record this and hold me accountable,” he said. The governor questioned why the same constitutional procedure should not apply at the national level, noting that he transmits power to his deputy when travelling for more than 21 days for reasons other than official duties. He also promised an issue-based campaign, saying his proposed reset would target an economy that can sustain intensive production and operate around the clock. “We are determined to reset our economy. Yes, people will argue that Nigeria is rich in natural resources. But natural resources are not enough. You must have skills and knowledge, and you must also have intensive production. Our economy must work 24/7,” Makinde said. On education, he promised to establish reliable data on the number of out-of-school children and develop measures to return them to school. “We want to reset our education. We want to measure the data that we are being given. We want to know how many out-of-school children we have and how we get them back into school,” he said. Makinde also called for mining to be removed from the Exclusive Legislative List and devolved to the states, with the Federal Government retaining oversight. “Right now, the issue of mining is on the Exclusive Legislative List in our Constitution. Devolve that responsibility to the states and let there be oversight only at the federal level. They will do better,” he said. He said the proposed restructuring would extend to the broader question of which level of government should take decisions on issues affecting Nigerians. On security, Makinde cited the recent deaths of 37 young people in Niger State, questioning whether they should be blamed for being born in Nigeria or for seeking means of survival. “Is it their fault that they were born in Nigeria? Is it their fault that they were looking for means of surviving? No, sir. The answer is no,” he said. The APM candidate also faulted what he described as an excessive focus on the supply side of illegal mining, arguing that the demand side must equally be addressed. “People may not want to take responsibility, but from what has been done so far and the actions that have been taken, we can see that we are focusing on the supply side of things. For every 10,000 illegal miners, you have perhaps another 10,000 on the demand side, legitimising the operation,” Makinde said. On the 2027 election, he urged Nigerians to obtain their Permanent Voter Cards, PVCs, and participate in the poll. “For the election, I maintain and repeat it: it won’t be APC versus APM, or APM versus ADC, or ADC versus NDC. It will be APC versus Nigerians,” he said. Makinde said he would return to Katsina, Kaduna, Kano, Kebbi, Zamfara and Jigawa for state-by-state campaigns, acknowledging that the task ahead was challenging but achievable with public support. He said the ultimate objective was to build a Nigeria that works for everyone, irrespective of tribe, religion or geographical location. Earlier, APM Vice-Presidential Candidate, Lawal Daura, said the North-West was yearning for change, identifying insecurity and poverty as the region’s most pressing challenges. “The North-West, and indeed Nigeria at large, is yearning for resetting Nigeria. Here in the North-West, some of our most prominent and pressing problems include, first and foremost, insecurity, and, of course, the twin brother of insecurity, which is poverty,” Daura said. He said Makinde’s proposed reset aligned with his own belief that Nigeria needed fundamental change, urging supporters to exercise their civic rights and vote for the APM ticket. Daura said the details of the proposed agenda would be unveiled as the campaign progresses, but identified restoration of security and normalcy as immediate priorities. “It is real. It is sincere. It is honest, and it is going to deliver,” he said. Dantalle said the country could no longer afford a situation where insecurity prevents farmers from reaching their farms, children from attending school and Nigerians from conducting their businesses safely. “We must solve these problems together. Let our farmers return to their farms. Let our children go to school freely. Let Nigerians coexist peacefully and go about their normal businesses. We must put an end to insecurity and hunger, improve access to education, and eradicate poverty,” he said. Dantalle described Makinde as ‘young, active and pragmatic’, citing his record in Oyo State, while describing Daura as a security expert from Katsina capable of addressing security challenges in the North-West and the country. The post 2027: I’ll transmit power to VP whenever I’m on vacation — Makinde appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Madagascar : le dossier des îles Éparses maintenu à l’ordre du jour de l’ONU
items.description: La question des îles Glorieuses, Juan de Nova, Europa et Bassas da India figure de nouveau a l'ordre du jour de la 81e session de l'Assemblee generale des Nations unies, actuellement reunie a New York. Le dossier apparaît au point 57 sous l'intitule « Question of the Malagasy islands of Glorieuses, Juan de Nova, Europa and Bassas da India ». Cette sequence survient alors que le president malgache de la Refondation, le colonel Michael Randrianirina, participe pour la premiere fois a ce rendez-vous en qualite de chef de l'etat. Le debat general de la 81e session se deroule du 22 au 26 septembre, puis le 28 septembre 2026. Administrees par la France, les quatre îles sont revendiquees par Madagascar. Leur question est inscrite a l'agenda des Nations unies depuis 1979, lorsque l'Assemblee generale avait adopte la resolution 34/91, intitulee « Question des îles Glorieuses, Juan de Nova, Europa et Bassas da India ». Un an plus tard, l'Assemblee generale avait de nouveau examine le dossier et adopte, le 11 decembre 1980, la resolution 35/123 consacree aux « îles malgaches » de Glorieuses, Juan de Nova, Europa et Bassas da India. Le sujet a ensuite continue d'apparaître dans les travaux de l'Assemblee generale au fil des annees. Le differend a egalement fait l'objet d'un dialogue bilateral entre Paris et Antananarivo. Une commission mixte consacree aux quatre îles a ete mise en place en 2019. Sa deuxieme session s'est tenue le 30 juin 2025 au Quai d'Orsay, sous la copresidence des ministres francais et malgache des Affaires etrangeres. Les deux parties y ont rappele leurs positions respectives et reconnu l'existence d'un differend sur la souverainete. Lors de cette reunion, Madagascar a notamment demande la suspension de toute action unilaterale dans les zones concernees et propose l'elaboration d'une feuille de route comprenant un mecanisme permanent de concertation. La France a pris note de ces demandes tout en reaffirmant sa position sur la souverainete. Les deux pays sont convenus de poursuivre leurs discussions dans le respect de leurs positions. Le maintien du dossier a l'ordre du jour de l'Assemblee generale ne constitue donc pas l'ouverture d'une nouvelle procedure, mais prolonge une question diplomatique inscrite depuis plusieurs decennies dans le cadre des Nations unies. Pour Madagascar, cette presence permet de conserver le differend sur la scene multilaterale, parallelement au dialogue engage avec la France.
