items.title: Pakistan, 7 other Muslim nations call upon Israel to fulfil its commitment under Gaza plan
items.description: Pakistan joined other Muslim countries on Tuesday in calling for Israel to “immediately fulfill its outstanding commitments” under the first phase of a plan aimed at ending the conflict in Gaza. The demand was made in a joint statement attributed to the foreign ministers of Pakistan, Egypt, Turkiye, Indonesia, Jordan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates after they met on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. The statement said that as part of its commitments under the Gaza plan, Israel should ensure the immediate, safe and unhindered delivery of humanitarian assistance and early recovery supplies, as well as facilitate the rehabilitation of critical infrastructure. The ministers stressed the “imperative of preserving the ceasefire and ending all violations”. They emphasised that the road map for completing the implementation of the of the Gaza plan was an “integral part” of the plan and provided the framework for implementation to advance its second phase. This included “decommissioning alongside full Israeli withdrawal, the deployment of the International Stabilisation Force (ISF), the assumption by the National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) of its responsibilities throughout the Gaza Strip, and the launch of early recovery and reconstruction across Gaza”, the statement read. The ministers called on all parties to fulfill their respective commitments “in good faith and without delay” under the plan. They further reiterated their “categorical rejection of any measures aimed at the expulsion or the forced displacement of the Palestinian people from their homeland or attempts to alter the territorial or demographic character of the Occupied Palestinian Territory”. “They deplore in this context the illegal measures aimed at consolidating Israeli control and annexation, including the accelerating settlement expansion, land confiscation, demolition of Palestinian homes, settler violence and terrorism, and forced displacement, and called for their immediate reversal,” the statement said. The ministers additionally expressed grave concern over measures that undermined the historical and legal status quo of Muslim and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem. Moreover, they welcomed the recent measures taken by the United Kingdom in response to “illegal Israeli settlement activity, as well as broader national and European efforts, including measures to halt trade with illegal Israeli settlements”. The ministers called for further effective measures to end the expansion of settlements and ensure accountability for settler violence. They also emphasised that Gaza remained an integral part of the Palestinian territory. The ministers reaffirmed that the implementation of the Gaza plan must contribute to the reunification of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, and the Gaza Strip, and to a “credible and irreversible pathway towards the exercise of the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination and the realisation of a sovereign, viable, and independent Palestinian State with East Jerusalem as its capital” through the implementation of the two-state solution. They commended the leadership of US President Donald Trump and highlighted the role of the US in ensuring the implementation of the Comprehensive Plan. They called for “sustained and active” US engagement to ensure that all parties fulfilled their commitments, and to overcome obstacles to the implementation of the road map. “Tangible progress on the ground will strengthen the credibility of the Board of Peace and the authority of the plan and create deeply needed momentum,” the joint statement said. The eight ministers reaffirmed their readiness to continue working collectively with the US, the Board of Peace, the Palestinian Authority and all relevant parties to advance the full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan and its road map, alleviate the suffering of the Palestinian people, fulfill their right to self-determination and independent statehood, and “achieve just, lasting and comprehensive peace in the region”. Much of Gaza remains in ruins from two years ​of relentless Israeli bombing that began on Oct 7, 2023. After a ceasefire deal was struck in October 2025, Trump set ​out a 20-point peace plan for Gaza that provided for a the supply of humanitarian aid, civilian administration by Palestinian ⁠technocrats, Hamas laying down its arms and Israeli forces withdrawing. But the plan has stalled and the group of technocrats — known as the ​National Committee for the Administration of Gaza — has remained outside Gaza. Meanwhile, Israel rejected in August a plan — the latest stage in a US-led ceasefire announced in October — that said Hamas would surrender weapons to a nascent Palestinian governing body. The plan was endorsed by Hamas in July. After more than a week of gradually escalating criticism of the plan, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu explicitly opposed it as he faced pushback from his right-wing base ahead of elections. The Israeli military “will not carry out any withdrawal until Hamas is genuinely disarmed and will continue to thwart threats against our forces and our citizens”, Netanyahu said at a cabinet meeting. OIC meeting Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also attended a meeting of the Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) on Monday where he called for urgent global attention to Israeli settler violence and annexation policies in the occupied West Bank, as well as violations of the Gaza ceasefire, describing such acts as “flagrant violations of international law”. Speaking at the meeting of the OIC Committee of Six on Palestine in New York, Dar said the Palestinian cause remained “central to the OIC and the collective conscience of the Muslim Ummah”. “The Committee of Six has an important responsibility to mobilise political and diplomatic support for the Palestinian people and to ensure that the international community does not lose sight of their legitimate and inalienable rights,” he noted. He said the situation in the occupied Palestinian territory, both in Gaza and the West Bank, continued to demand “urgent and immediate attention”, with the humanitarian situation remaining dire and the security environment “extremely fragile”. “Our recent diplomatic efforts have created an opportunity to advance a critical process. Serious challenges still remain,” Dar said, adding that the Gaza ceasefire was being violated “on an almost daily basis”. He appreciated the efforts of mediating countries, including the United States, Egypt, Qatar and Turkiye, towards implementing the comprehensive plan to end the Gaza conflict, as endorsed by UN Security Council Resolution 2803. Dar said Israeli settlement activity, settler violence, annexation policies and other violations in the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, continued to threaten the “territorial integrity and contiguity” of the occupied Palestinian territory and undermine the viability of a future Palestinian state. Pakistan, he said, continued to “strongly condemn” Israeli violations at Al-Aqsa Mosque and Al-Haram Al-Sharif, including incursions by extremist settlers. “These acts are flagrant violations of international law, relevant UN resolutions, and the historical and legal status quo governing the Holy Sites,” he said. Dar said the ongoing situation required “renewed, coordinated diplomatic action” by the OIC and its member states, adding that the committee should continue to work on six points. The first was to safeguard the historical and legal status quo at Al-Aqsa Mosque, Al-Haram Al-Sharif and other Islamic and Christian holy sites in Jerusalem. Second, reject Israel’s illegal settlement expansion, annexation, settler violence and forced displacement in the occupied Palestinian territory, including East Jerusalem. Third, support the full and faithful implementation of the Gaza peace plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803. Fourth, ensure that reconstruction and governance arrangements in Gaza remain Palestinian-led, with a central role for the Palestinian Authority. Fifth, support accountability for violations of international law and international humanitarian law; further strengthen coordination among OIC member states in other international forums to protect the Palestinian people and uphold international law. Finally, maintain sustained international efforts towards a credible, irreversible and time-bound political process leading to the establishment of an independent, sovereign and contiguous State of Palestine based on the pre-1967 borders, with Al-Quds Al-Sharif as its capital, while also supporting Palestine’s full membership of the United Nations. “As members of the OIC Committee of Six, we have a particular responsibility to translate our collective solidarity into sustained and coordinated diplomatic efforts,” Dar stressed. “Pakistan’s solidarity with the Palestinian people remains steadfast and unwavering. We will continue to work with brotherly and partner countries to advance the Palestinian cause and contribute to a just and lasting resolution of the question of Palestine, in line with international legitimacy,” he affirmed. The Foreign Office (FO) later shared a statement outlining DPM Dar’s remarks at the meeting. The remarks come amid renewed Israeli settlement expansion and rising settler violence in the occupied West Bank. Israel has recently added 2,167 housing units to its E1 settlement plan, bringing the total planned units to 3,401, a move that Palestinians and several countries have criticised as threatening the territorial contiguity of a future Palestinian state. The UN has also reported a sharp rise in settler attacks. More than 1,600 incidents resulting in Palestinian casualties or property damage were recorded across 275 communities between January and September 14, while more than 2,600 Palestinians had been displaced in the context of settler violence and related access restrictions. R-4 meeting Dar also participated in the ministerial meeting of the Regional-4 (R-4) group in New York on Tuesday. He was joined by the foreign ministers of Turkiye, Saudi Arabia, and Egypt. The R-4 group has been focused on regional security and emerged in March amid efforts for mediation between the US and Iran. As the group met in New York, DPM Dar reaffirmed “Pakistan’s strong commitment to the R-4 framework and expressed the need for continued engagement for enhancing regional peace and prosperity”, the Foreign Office (FO) said in a statement. It added that the participants exchanged views on the latest situation in the region and expressed full support for efforts aimed at a peaceful resolution of the situation. “The ministers reiterated their support for the legitimate rights of the Palestinian people, including their inalienable right to self-determination and to establish an independent, sovereign, viable, and contiguous State of Palestine on the basis of 4 June 1967 lines, with East Jerusalem as its capital, in accordance with relevant United Nations Security Council resolutions,” it read. Dar meets with Libyan FM Separately, in a meeting with Libya’s acting foreign minister, Al-Taher Al-Baour, Dar discussed ways to further strengthen bilateral ties, particularly in trade, education and business-to-business exchanges, FO said in a statement. During the meeting, which took place on the sidelines of the 81st session of the UN General Assembly, the two sides exchanged views on “regional and international developments, including the evolving situation in the Middle East”, FO said. The Libyan foreign minister appreciated Pakistan’s “constructive diplomatic efforts” for regional peace and stability, according to the FO. DPM Dar underscored that “dialogue and diplomacy remained the only viable means of addressing regional challenges” and stressed the need for all parties to return to the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to advance regional stability, the statement added. Dar meets with Japanese FM Dar also held a meeting with Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi, during which the two discussed ways to further deepen bilateral cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, education, health, the automobile sector and digital IT cooperation, the FO said in a statement. They also exchanged views on “regional and international developments, including the situation in the Middle East”. Motegi appreciated Pakistan’s diplomatic and mediation efforts in support of regional peace and stability, the FO added. Both sides expressed hope that all parties would return to dialogue and pursue implementation of the Islamabad MoU. They also discussed the implications of the situation for energy supplies, supply chains and the global economy, according to the FO. The two ministers reaffirmed their commitment to sustaining the momentum of bilateral engagement and further expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest, the statement added.

items.title: L’ANCES-Togo dote la fédération de producteurs de soja de motos
items.description: Lomé, 22 sept. (ATOP) – La Fédération nationale des coopératives productrices de soja au Togo (FNCPS-Togo) a bénéficié, le mardi 22 septembre à Lomé, des motos tout-terrain de l’Association nationale des commerçants exportateurs de soja (ANCES-Togo). Elle a également reçu de bons de carburant (500 000F CFA) et un chèque d’un demi million. Ce matériel est destiné à faciliter le travail des techniciens chargés d’assurer un suivi de proximité auprès des producteurs dans les cinq régions du pays, notamment au niveau des unions communales mises en place par la FNCPS-Togo. Il va contribuer à améliorer l’accompagnement des producteurs, les rendements et, à terme, la production nationale de soja. Cet appui entend renforcer l’accompagnement des producteurs, considérés comme des acteurs essentiels de la filière soja. Les bénéficiaires et les dons Le président du conseil d’administration de l’ANCES-Togo, Tewou Kokou, a expliqué que cette initiative traduit la volonté de l’association de consolider les relations entre les différentes familles de l’interprofession du soja. Il a ajouté qu’il est question également de promouvoir une collaboration fondée sur la responsabilité, le dialogue et la complémentarité. M. Téwou a réaffirmé la disponibilité de l’ANCES-Togo à poursuivre les actions en faveur de la productivité, de la qualité, de la compétitivité et de l’amélioration des revenus des acteurs de la filière. Le président a invité les bénéficiaires à assurer une utilisation efficiente des équipements. La présidente du conseil d’administration de la FNCPS-Togo, Mme Daloli Mimbouab, a estimé que cet appui « dépasse largement le cadre matériel d’un simple moyen de transport : c’est un véritable levier de développement, un outil de travail stratégique pour accélérer notre présence sur le terrain ». Elle a souligné que les motos faciliteront le suivi des exigences liées à la certification du soja biologique et de sécuriser l’approvisionnement en graines de qualité au profit des commerçants contractualisés. La cérémonie s’est déroulée en présence des représentants des ministères chargés du Commerce et de l’Agriculture, du président du conseil d’administration du Conseil interprofessionnel de la filière soja (CIFS), du représentant de la GIZ et de plusieurs acteurs de la filière soja. ATOP/BA/AO

items.title: Eau potable en milieu rural : la SRM Casablanca-Settat accélère le déploiement des projets
items.description: La Société Régionale Multiservices (SRM) Casablanca-Settat contribue en partenariat avec la Région de Casablanca-Settat à la mise en œuvre d’un important programme visant à renforcer et à généraliser l’accès à l’eau potable dans les centres et douars de la Région, avec une attention particulière portée aux zones rurales. Inscrit dans le cadre du Programme National d’Approvisionnement en Eau Potable et d’Irrigation 2020-2027 (PNAEPI), ce programme représente une enveloppe globale estimée à 350,8 millions de DH, intégrant les études, l’assistance technique et l’acquisition de l’assiette foncière. Son financement est assuré à hauteur de 245,6 millions de DH par le ministère de l’Intérieur et de 105,2 millions de DH par la Direction Générale des Collectivités Territoriales. Les opérations concernent plusieurs provinces de la Région, notamment Settat, Berrechid, Benslimane, El Jadida et Sidi Bennour et portent sur : – l’alimentation en eau potable de 25 centres, pour un montant de 150 millions de DH ; – l’amélioration de la desserte des populations rurales à travers des interventions au niveau de 341 douars, pour 150,8 millions de DH, – l’aménagement de points d’eau au niveau de 80 douars , pour une enveloppe de 50 millions de DH. Ce programme répond à un enjeu essentiel : réduire les disparités territoriales en matière d’accès à l’eau potable et rapprocher ce service essentiel des populations rurales. Selon la nature des projets, les interventions comprennent notamment la réalisation et le renforcement des infrastructures nécessaires à l’alimentation en eau potable des centres et douars concernés. Dans ce cadre, la SRM Casablanca-Settat assure directement la prise en charge et le pilotage de projets représentant près de 44 millions de DH TTC dans les provinces de Sidi Bennour et d’El Jadida, depuis la préparation et la contractualisation des marchés jusqu’au suivi, au contrôle et à la réception des travaux. À Sidi Bennour, les projets portent sur six centres — Sebt Lamaarif, Ouled Amrane, M’Tal, Metrane, Ouled Si Bouhya et Bni Hilal — pour un montant global de 35 millions de DH TTC. Ils comprennent notamment la réalisation et le renforcement des réseaux d’eau potable, la construction de réservoirs surélevés et équipements associés, la réalisation de stations de surpression, ainsi que la réalisation de branchements individuels. Les travaux enregistrent aujourd’hui un taux d’avancement global de l’ordre de 90%. À El Jadida, le projet, d’un montant d’environ 8,6 millions de DH TTC, concerne l’équipement en eau potable du centre de Sidi Hssein Ben Abderrahmane et de six douars relevant de la commune d’Ouled Hcine. Il comprend notamment 19 km de conduites, neuf bornes-fontaines, un réservoir surélevé de 150 m³ et le renforcement de la station de pompage, au bénéfice d’environ 1.200 foyers, soit près de 6.000 habitants. Les travaux sont aujourd’hui achevés. À travers ces opérations, la SRM Casablanca-Settat assure un rôle opérationnel complet sur les projets qui lui sont confiés : réalisation ou actualisation des études techniques, préparation et lancement des appels d’offres, contractualisation des marchés, suivi et contrôle des travaux, réception des ouvrages, ainsi que suivi administratif et financier. The post Eau potable en milieu rural : la SRM Casablanca-Settat accélère le déploiement des projets appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Tchad : le ministère des Mines reprend la gestion du Guichet unique à la SONEMIC
items.description: © (DR) Dans une note circulaire du 21 septembre 2026, la ministre des Mines, du Pétrole et la Géologie, Fatima Haram Acyl annonce la reprise par son département, de la gestion exclusive du Guichet unique des pierres précieuses. Le gouvernement tchadien vient de procéder au changement de gestionnaire pour le Guichet unique des matières précieuses. Les usagers et l'ensemble des opérateurs miniers ont été informés ce jour de la reprise du Guichet unique autrefois placé sous la responsabilité de la Société Nationale d'Exploitation Minière et de Commercialisation (SONEMIC). Désormais, elle est intégralement transféré sous la responsabilité directe du ministère des Mines, du Pétrole et de la Géologie. A compter de la signature de la présente note circulaire, toutes les procédures et formalités administratives relative aux autorisations, aux activités d'achat, de vente, d'importation et d'exportation de l'or et autres pierres précieuses s'effectuent exclusivement auprès des services dédiés du ministère des Mines, du Pétrole et de la Géologie. Les usagers et opérateurs miniers sont désormais invités à se rapprocher des services du ministère des Mines, du Pétrole et de la Géologie pour bénéficier des prestations nécessaires, conformément aux dispositions réglementaires en vigueur. items.title: LHC hears Junaid Hafeez's appeal in blasphemy case, seeks prosecution's arguments on admissibility of digital evidence
items.description: LAHORE: The Lahore High Court (LHC) took up former university lecturer Junaid Hafeez’s appeal against his death sentence in a blasphemy case on Tuesday, seeking arguments from the prosecution on the admissibility of electronic evidence. Hafeez was sentenced to death in 2019 and his appeal against his conviction has been pending since 2020. A two-judge bench, comprising Justices Sadiq Mahmud Khurram and Muhammad Jawad Zafar, took up the appeal on Tuesday as complainant’s lawyer, Advocate Athar Shah Bokhari, and Hafeez’s lawyer, Advocate Asad Jamal, appeared before the court. The hearing began with the bench observing that formal notices had not been issued to the parties since the transfer of Hafeez’s appeal from the Multan bench to the principal seat. The case was transferred on the request of Hafeez’s lawyer in December 2021. During the hearing on Tuesday, the LHC issued notices on the appeal, which the lawyers for the prosecution and the complainant received in the court. The court further stated that it would like to hear the prosecution on the admissibility of electronic evidence involved in the case and the Facebook page attributed to Hafeez. It then decided to adjourn the hearing till Oct 7, but the complainant’s counsel sought a longer adjournment to prepare his arguments. The bench then said it would announce the date of the next hearing later. Hafeez — a former visiting lecturer at the Department of English Literature of the Bahauddin Zakariya University (BZU) — was arrested by police on March 13, 2013 and his trial in the blasphemy case, linked to Facebook uploads, began in 2014. He was sentenced to death by a Multan district and sessions court on December 21, 2019 on blasphemy charges and subsequently appealed his conviction in 2020. At least seven judges were transferred through the course of Hafeez’s case. As many as 15 prosecution witnesses recorded their statements against Hafeez while 11 others were not called after being declared irrelevant. The trial was shifted to the Multan Central Jail in April 2014 by the Punjab home department due to security concerns. One of Hafeez’s previous lawyer, Rashid Rehman , was shot dead in May 2014 in his office. The month prior to it, the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan had expressed serious concerns when death threats were extended to Rehman, also the special task force coordinator of the commission. In December 2014, another lawyer representing Hafeez also received a threat letter from the militant Islamic State group, warning him to withdraw from the case. The hearing of the appeal has also been deferred multiple times.

items.title: CDF reaffirms Pakistan's commitment to bolster defence, security cooperation with France
items.description: Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff (COAS) Field Marshal Asim Munir on Tuesday reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to boosting defence ties with France, Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said. The development came as a top French defence official, accompanied by France’s Ambassador to Pakistan Jean-Noël Poirier, called on CDF Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, according to an ISPR statement. During the meeting with Nicolas Roche, secretary general for France’s General Secretariat for Defence and National Security (SGDSN), “matters of mutual interest, including regional security, [and] bilateral cooperation in defence and security domains were discussed”. Field Marshal Munir reaffirmed Pakistan’s commitment to strengthening “bilateral ties and further enhancing defence and security cooperation”, the statement said. On his part, Roche acknowledged Pakistan’s efforts to promote regional peace and stability and expressed France’s “interest in expanding cooperation in areas of mutual interest”, ISPR said. According to its website , the SGDSN has a “central positioning in the executive power organisation” and assists the French prime minister in exercising their responsibilities in the field of defence and national security. It provides the secretariat for the national defence and security councils chaired by the French president. Strategic defence and security issues, military programming, deterrence policy, economic and energy security, cybersecurity, the fight against terrorism, and the fight against foreign digital interference are among the key areas that SGDSN covers. On Monday, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met France’s FM Jean-Noël Barrot on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly in New York. According to the Office (FO), they had stressed the need to ensure the “safety and free flow” of maritime traffic and uninterrupted energy supplies as the Middle East conflict disrupts oil shipments. “Both sides exchanged views on the importance of continued diplomatic engagement and regional efforts to address the crisis,” the statement said.

items.title: Rabat et Madrid renforcent leur coordination face aux appels à un passage vers Sebta le jour du scrutin
items.description: À la veille des élections législatives marocaines, la coordination entre Rabat et Madrid se renforce autour de la surveillance de la frontière avec Sebta occupée. Le ministre espagnol des Affaires étrangères, de l’Union européenne et de la Coopération, José Manuel Albares, a assuré mardi que le Maroc avait garanti la mise en place des moyens nécessaires pour empêcher une nouvelle tentative de passage collectif vers la ville le 23 septembre. Les déclarations du chef de la diplomatie espagnole, rapportées par El País depuis New York, interviennent alors que des appels circulent sur les réseaux sociaux pour inciter à une tentative d’entrée collective à Sebta occupée le jour du vote aux Législatives. Madrid dit suivre ces messages avec attention et avoir renforcé son dispositif préventif au niveau de la frontière. Albares a surtout insisté sur le niveau de coordination avec son homologue marocain, Nasser Bourita. Selon le ministre espagnol, les deux responsables sont en contact de manière quasi quotidienne et travaillent avec leurs administrations respectives afin d’empêcher une nouvelle tentative de passage collectif. Rabat assure Madrid de la mobilisation des moyens nécessaires D’après les déclarations rapportées par El País, les autorités marocaines ont assuré à Madrid qu’elles mettraient en place « tous les moyens » nécessaires pour éviter qu’une nouvelle tentative ne se produise le 23 septembre. Cette assurance intervient après plusieurs épisodes de tension enregistrés au niveau de la frontière de Sebta occupée. Les autorités espagnoles avaient déjà fait état, ces dernières semaines, d’appels diffusés en ligne encourageant des migrants à tenter de rejoindre la ville par voie terrestre ou maritime. Madrid cherche depuis lors à agir sur plusieurs fronts : renforcer la surveillance de la frontière, prévenir les tentatives de passage et lutter contre les informations présentées comme trompeuses sur les conséquences d’une entrée irrégulière en Espagne. Albares a ainsi indiqué que les autorités espagnoles coopéraient avec leurs homologues marocaines, mais également avec des médias au Maroc, afin de démentir certaines informations circulant sur les réseaux sociaux. Parmi les messages ciblés figurent ceux laissant entendre qu’une entrée irrégulière à Sebta permettrait aux personnes concernées de rester durablement en Espagne. Le gouvernement espagnol avait déjà indiqué que les messages relatifs au 23 septembre ne semblaient pas, au 21 septembre, susciter le même niveau de mobilisation que les appels diffusés avant les événements de la fin du mois de juillet. Une rencontre Bourita-Albares attendue à New York La question de Sebta et celle des migrants présents dans la ville doivent également être abordées directement par les chefs de la diplomatie marocaine et espagnole. Nasser Bourita et José Manuel Albares sont attendus pour une rencontre à New York, en marge des réunions de l’Assemblée générale des Nations unies. Selon Cadena SER, la situation à Sebta ainsi que le retour des migrants encore présents dans la ville figurent parmi les principaux dossiers qui doivent être examinés lors de cette réunion. Le dossier des retours occupe une place particulière dans les discussions entre Rabat et Madrid. Les deux pays travaillent à la mise en œuvre des procédures permettant le retour des personnes entrées irrégulièrement sur le territoire espagnol, une fois leurs dossiers établis et les conditions administratives réunies. Cette question avait déjà été évoquée par Albares lors de ses précédentes déclarations. Le ministre espagnol avait alors souligné la continuité des échanges avec Rabat sur les retours et la prévention de nouvelles tentatives de passage. Trois axes pour contenir les tentatives de passage La stratégie espagnole repose ainsi sur trois volets que le ministère des Affaires étrangères avait déjà mis en avant : faciliter le retour des personnes entrées irrégulièrement, lutter contre la désinformation en ligne et soutenir le renforcement du contrôle des frontières. Le volet relatif à l’information occupe une place croissante dans le dispositif. Madrid considère que certaines publications diffusées sur les réseaux sociaux entretiennent des attentes erronées sur les possibilités d’installation en Espagne après une entrée irrégulière. Les représentations diplomatiques espagnoles au Maroc participent également à cette campagne d’information. Sur le terrain, la coopération avec les autorités marocaines reste cependant le principal levier mis en avant par Madrid. Le gouvernement espagnol souligne régulièrement le rôle du Maroc dans la prévention des départs et des tentatives de passage vers Sebta et Melilla, ainsi que dans la lutte contre les réseaux de trafic de migrants. À quelques heures du scrutin du 23 septembre, les deux capitales cherchent donc à éviter qu’un nouvel appel relayé sur les réseaux sociaux ne se traduise par une tentative de passage collectif. Pour Madrid, la réponse repose à la fois sur le renforcement du contrôle frontalier et sur la coordination avec Rabat. Pour les autorités marocaines, la mobilisation annoncée des moyens nécessaires intervient dans le cadre plus large de la coopération migratoire entre les deux pays. La rencontre annoncée entre Bourita et Albares à New York devrait permettre de poursuivre ces échanges, avec Sebta, la prévention des passages irréguliers et le retour des migrants présents dans la ville parmi les dossiers évoqués. The post Rabat et Madrid renforcent leur coordination face aux appels à un passage vers Sebta le jour du scrutin appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: The Trump-Xi Summit
items.description: Sign up for our newsletter about national security here . Subscribe here: Apple Podcasts | Spotify | YouTube | Overcast | Pocket Casts It’s a big week on the global stage. More than 100 world leaders and their senior representatives will meet in New York City for the United Nations General Assembly. And on Thursday, eyes will turn south, to Washington, where President Trump will meet with Chinese President Xi Jinping for the second time in the past six months. Warnings from Silicon Valley executives about the potential dangers of artificial intelligence hang over the proceedings. Tech leaders have called for a slowdown in development and regulation, but Trump is wary of their caution. The president believes that slowing down on AI will help China, though recent reporting suggests that he may be just as, if not more, worried that a slowdown will throw the American economy—already hurting from the war in Iran, which has sent gas prices soaring—into a recession. What will come of the meetings in New York? Will Xi and Trump find common ground on AI? On this episode of Radio Atlantic , I spoke with my colleagues Vivian Salama, a longtime foreign-policy reporter, and Rogé Karma, an economics reporter, to make sense of it all. The following is a transcript of the episode: Rogé Karma: If Donald Trump’s main way to negotiate is by threatening economic coercion, China now knows he doesn’t have much to use. [ Music ] Adam Harris: This is Radio Atlantic . I’m Adam Harris, and it’s a big week in international politics. World leaders are meeting in New York for the United Nations General Assembly, and Chinese President Xi Jinping is coming to Washington for the first time in over a decade, at a moment when China is central to the global conversation around AI. President Trump continues to favor speed over caution to ensure the U.S. can remain ahead on artificial intelligence. But not everyone, including the CEOs leading AI companies, are so sure. The U.S. and China’s relationship has been cold to lukewarm since the president returned to office. The nations reached a shaky trade truce last year following Trump’s tariff rollout, and other countries have turned to China for trade deals amid the turmoil inflicted by his administration’s policies. Meanwhile, in the U.S., Americans are feeling the pain of Trump’s economic plans and a war that is driving up the price of everyday items, from gas to groceries. What will all of these meetings lead to—if anything? With me to discuss are my colleagues Atlantic staff writers Vivan Salama and Rogé Karma. Let’s get to questions. Vivian, Rogé, thank you so much for joining me today. Vivian Salama: Good to be here. Rogé Karma: Great to be here, Adam. Harris: Vivian, I want to start with you to sort of frame this a little bit for us. What is at stake during this week’s meetings between Xi and Trump? Salama: I mean, the two countries have so much at stake because they basically thrive in this ecosystem in which they are codependent and yet trying to cooperate with each other at the same time—codependent economically on each other, trying to compete with each other, and trying to kind of maintain their status as these two global superpowers. And a lot of these interests face headwinds. And so, they’re coming in a very strange moment geopolitically, both for President Trump and for President Xi. Apart from the fact that they’ve had this up-and-down dispute rolling for the last year and a half over trade and tariffs and, in particular, competition about advanced semiconductors and artificial intelligence and this race for rare-earth minerals, they’re both also squeezed economically at home. President Trump obviously has the Iran war very heavy on his mind these days, and he has been frustrated with countries like China and Russia, who are believed to still be propping up the Iranian regime and helping them to sustain the attacks that the U.S. has launched with Israel. But also the economic impact that has come from this war, where it’s basically sent shock waves across the world, and particularly for oil markets that have struggled. You know, that’s something that also impacts China as well. Inflationary pressures in both countries have been really problematic. And so they’re coming to the table with this understanding and this sense that they both really need to do something to help them domestically, first of all, while also sustaining their ability to do the things that they do around the world, and do so in a way where they’re competing with each other. It’s a very strange dynamic, but one that President Trump has consistently said is a priority for him. And he wants that relationship to thrive. Harris: How has the president’s posture changed, even from that first Trump term, right? It seemed that coming into this term, there was the outright kind of hostility with the tariffs, and it’s sort of changed into a Well , we can work together and We have this sort of working relationship. How has the president’s position on China changed since that first term? Salama: Yeah, well, I mean, he recognizes that picking a fight with China is not advantageous to the United States, although he has insisted that tariffs, for example, help American businesses, help American producers. He has said that farmers are sort of insulated. He’s denied the economic impact of those tariffs that so many economists around the world say are the cause for driving inflationary pressures up and prices up here in the United States. And so he has completely dismissed that. It is one of the core elements of his economic agenda. But what we’ve seen is that—on top of the Iran war and the pressures that are happening because oil prices have gone up and inflation is going up, and on top of some of the other economic conditions that we see here—the president is really in a bind, and he recognizes that picking a fight with China would only probably exacerbate that. His advisers continuously tell him that Picking a fight with China just does not present the ultimate advantages that you’re seeking. And especially—remind our listeners and viewers’we’re in an election period right now where Republicans, especially those running for the House, for House seats, are up against a wall right now because of a lot of these issues. And so politically, it’s not advantageous to pick a fight with China right now, and instead to try to find ways where, Yes, we can compete, but ultimately we need each other in order to survive and thrive in this day and age. And so they are trying to approach the relationship with China now with a very open-eyed, a wide-eyed recognition of that—that they just can’t shut the door to China. It’s not even realistic. Harris: You know, Rogé, one of the things I think we’ve learned over the last decade or so is that the president doesn’t always listen to his advisers when they’re telling him not to pick fights. And thinking about the news over the last several weeks—the panic about AI that’s been coming out from the tech CEOs themselves, who are talking about slowing down the pace of development to align and to allow for regulation to land in that time—The president, for his part, isn’t necessarily buying it, right? He’s said to reporters recently: Donald Trump: We’re leading China in AI. We’re the most sophisticated country in the world. And frankly, I want to keep it that way because whoever wins AI, wins. Harris: Rogé, do you buy this argument from the president that this push to disregard the tech CEOs’ warnings is about China? Karma: I don’t fully buy it. So, I think it’s important to place this meeting in context. I do think the AI race is going to be the central issue in this meeting. You already are seeing reports of Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent meeting with his Chinese counterpart and discussing the idea of, for example, an AI warning system. I think this issue is going to be central. And as you alluded to, Adam, I think there are really two stories that are colliding here. So the first story is the one that you mentioned, which is the AI freak-out that is happening in the U.S., where you have this series of incidents in which AIs are—and people are probably pretty familiar with them by now—but are displaying some, let’s just call it very scary behavior that has got essentially every tech CEO, from Elon Musk to Sam Altman at OpenAI to Dario Amodei at Anthropic, really, really worried. These companies that were bristling at the idea of regulation just six months ago are now basically begging the government to regulate them. You have lawmakers from both sides of the aisle scrambling to try to write regulations, and the whole view in the U.S. is like, Okay, this is going way too fast; we need to slow it down. But there’s also a second story that has been happening this year, and that is the acceleration of Chinese AI. And this is what’s happening in the background, is that heading into this year, Claude Code was taking the world by storm; there was a view that the U.S. and its labs were leading the AI race definitively. And over the last few months, there has been a series of Chinese models released that have basically, on the benchmarks that we know of, have shown to be pretty neck and neck with the U.S. models and have often been trained at a fraction of the price. And this, I think, has really complicated the story around the U.S. slowdown. Because I think there is a good-faith argument to be made that if the U.S. unilaterally imposes really strict regulations, if the U.S. unilaterally slows down, then it’s only a matter of time before China catches up with and then surpasses the U.S. And then we have the worst of both worlds, right? Because in that case, we have rapidly advancing AI systems that are dangerous, and the technology is controlled by our biggest geopolitical rival—an authoritarian government. And so I think these two stories coming together in this meeting is what’s really important. There is, I think, a view among AI experts that the only real, sustainable way in order to have an AI slowdown to address some of these possibilities is for the U.S. and China to work together. Now, when it comes to Donald Trump’s comments of saying, Okay, we can’t do any regulation because of China, I find that a little bit disingenuous and a little bit puzzling, because Donald Trump and his policies are some of the biggest reasons why China is so close to the U.S. in the AI race. Harris: How exactly has he advanced China’s capabilities? Karma: So the biggest advantage that the United States has when it comes to the AI race is our quasi-monopoly on what are called advanced semiconductors—the very advanced computer chips that are needed to run the trillions of calculations per second in order to train these very advanced AI systems. There’s basically one company in the world that can create, design, these at scale, and it’s the U.S.-based Nvidia, the most valuable company in the world. Under Joe Biden, there was a policy where the Biden administration announced what are called export controls on these semiconductors, basically saying, Look, we recognize this is an important technology. We recognize that it has a lot of military applications. We don’t want China to be able to advance as quickly as us in this technology. So we’re going to restrict the chip sales of our most advanced chips to China. We’re gonna tell Nvidia it’s not allowed to sell its best chips to China. Most experts believe that is a key reason why China has remained behind in the AI race, even though they have pretty equal AI-engineering talent. They have a huge amount of research scientists; they have incredible energy use and ability to build data centers. But the one thing they don’t have is the chips. But when Donald Trump comes into office, he has systematically rolled back those export controls. Right now, China has access to import the H200, which is the second-best Nvidia chip available, which is far more advanced than anything any Chinese company could make at the moment. And so I wrote a piece about this where I basically said, This is the equivalent of saying we’re in a race with Russia when it comes to nuclear weapons, while also selling the Kremlin uranium. That’s basically what Donald Trump’s policy is. And I think it makes very little sense. Harris: Vivian, we talk about the ways that the president’s policies have driven other nations into the arms of competitors, driven them into the arms of China—thinking about Mark Carney and his talk about the realignment of the international order. I’ve been thinking about the continuing war with Iran in this context. It’s a war that’s really unpopular with the majority of U.S. voters, but China recently hosted an Iranian diplomat in a show of Beijing’s leverage over Iran. What does that tell us about China’s relationship with Iran, as this war with the U.S. continues to unfold? Salama: So there’s so much to unpack in your question, and it happens to be something I’m writing quite a bit about these days. The relationship between China and Iran in particular is advantageous to Russia and to China for different reasons. At this point, Iran is looking for any friends that it can get. There’s increasingly, because of the Trump administration’s sanctions and blockades on Iran right now, there’s very little that can be done by countries around the world, even if their own bilateral relations are pretty solid with Tehran. They would face heavy sanctions on their own, especially as the Trump administration talks about what’s called secondary sanctions, which is sanctioning countries and companies elsewhere in the world for doing business with Iran. And China has heeded those warnings to a certain extent, where a lot of the aboveboard cooperation and relations with Iran have subdued because they would also be subject to those sanctions. But behind the scenes and, in particular, on the military side, China sees a customer in Iran. Iran right now—some of its stockpiles, its military stockpiles, have been depleted because of this war, in particular, drone technology, which has been a driving force of its ability to sustain U.S. attacks in the last eight months or so of this war. It will turn to China increasingly as it tries to rebuild those stockpiles. And China, of course, has excellent technology when it comes to military, but also especially with drone technology; it’s some of the most advanced in the world. Iran had pretty good technology too, but it needs more. And so China’s happy to do that. It ultimately wants to do that business, and it’s not concerned with the politics or the geopolitics involved in it. Obviously China also—it’s a double-edged sword for China because, again, economically this war has not been favorable to them. They have felt the pressures that many countries around the world have felt, and so it has been problematic for them. But both countries also have the advantage of also doing business with Russia, and Russia can fill in the gaps of some of those, especially when it comes to getting cheaper oil. They’ve lifted, temporarily, any blockades on Russian oil being exported during this war to alleviate some of the pressures globally to get some of that oil in the market. And so they have sort of a trio that benefits from each other in terms of being able to sustain the current challenges that are being felt economically around the world. To your broader question about the alliances, though, I really want to point out—and it’s something that I’ve been writing about quite a bit—is that one of the fears and Mark Carney, the prime minister of Canada, sort of being embraced by the European Union as an associate member, and all of these things that we’re seeing under the second Trump administration. One of the things I’ve been writing about is that this is not really isolated to the second Trump administration. If anything, I’ve been talking to senior officials around the world in recent months, and they say we have to plan for a world in which the United States is no longer the leader of the free world. And this is something that they believe is not isolated to Trump. You look at some of the winds of change here in the United States; you even hear progressives in some ways talking about less wars overseas and defunding the Department of Defense and things like that. That is troubling to a lot of countries around the world who say, yes, Donald Trump has made clear that he does not view the traditional alliances of the post–World War II era with the same sanctity as some of his predecessors. But the fact of the matter is, the American people voted him in twice. And if the American people voted him in twice—albeit with a break in between—it shows that there is an appetite for what he’s selling. And if there’s an appetite for what he’s selling, then increasingly—and especially with younger generations turning more isolationist—a Democrat would have to embrace some of those policies too. And so, instead of treating Donald Trump as a phenomenon, they’re now treating him as the norm. And who benefits from all that, at the end? It is China. And it’s not because China is a favorable benefactor for these countries. Most countries around the world do not trust China. But even just the slightest decoupling, whether it be militarily, economically, on industries—the slightest decoupling from the United States opens a window for China. It’s a little window of opportunity for China. And China is seizing that. And the Iran case is something very unique to the current situation, the current war. But China is also benefiting from the policies of the Trump administration, of whatever will come after it. And so it’s something to watch. Karma: And Adam, could I actually just add something in real quick? One thing I’ve been covering a lot with this war is oil markets. And I think one very underappreciated element of the meeting that’s going to be happening this week is the role that China has played in keeping global oil prices down. Almost every expert I talked to who, at the beginning of this war, believed that oil prices were going to spike to $150 or $200 a barrel, and then proceeded to not spike—we’re now well into this war. It’s been months and months and months, and oil prices are high, but they’re not nearly as high as the sort of doomsday predictions that everyone thought. And the single biggest reason is China. Because China, for reasons that no one fully understands—and no one even really knows exactly how they did it—they basically slashed their imports of oil by around half earlier this year. They are the single biggest importer of oil in the world, and so this is a huge deal. It was almost single-handedly enough to help keep oil prices down. But that kind of behavior can’t last forever. And so I think Donald Trump has a very vested interest in China continuing to consume a lot less oil. And to Vivian’s point, this fact that China has helped keep oil prices down not only buys it international goodwill, but I think does provide it some leverage in these talks. Because heading into the midterms, if China were to suddenly start buying a lot of oil again, that would suddenly send the price of oil much, much higher. It’s just one possible thing to think about as these meetings proceed. Harris: When we come back, Vivan and Rogé talk about what the government is doing about inflation and the UN General Assembly in New York. [ BREAK ] Harris: The U.S. economy is in this perpetual position of tumult. Last week, the Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, raised interest rates for the first time in three years. What does that rate hike, Rogé, tell us about the U.S. economy at this moment? Karma: I think the most important thing it signals about the U.S. economy is the extent to which we have committed a series of own goals that have taken an otherwise very strong economy and weakened it. Listeners might remember that, heading into the fall of 2024, so about two years ago, the Federal Reserve was beginning to lower interest rates. Inflation was coming down, right? The labor market was strong. And the Fed basically declared victory. And then Donald Trump came into office, he instituted these global tariffs, and the Fed had to pause and said, Wait a minute, maybe we can’t be lowering interest rates, because inflation might come back. Then we had a period of stagnation. And then the Iran war came, and it has driven global energy prices, but also lots of other prices, up so much that now the Fed feels like we may be in a position where inflation gets out of control again. And so we have to raise interest rates. So I think the most important thing it tells us about the economy is that all of a sudden, the U.S. is facing—and really the world, because of this war—is facing an inflation crisis again. The Fed feels like it has to take pretty drastic action to address that crisis—that this crisis is almost entirely one that the United States, and Donald Trump specifically, created by launching this war. And in terms of what it means for this meeting, I think what it means is that the U.S. has a lot less leverage than it might have. You, Adam, at the beginning, you asked, What has changed about Trump between the first and second term? And one answer is that the economic context has changed. Salama: Totally. Karma: In Trump’s first term, inflation was low; the employment was strong. Now inflation is getting scarily high. Interest rates are much higher than they were back then. Consumers are much angrier than they were back then. If Donald Trump’s main way to negotiate is by threatening economic coercion, China now knows he doesn’t have much to use. They’re looking at these polls going into the midterms; they’re looking at the price of gas; they’re looking at how frustrated consumers are. And I think they’re probably saying to themselves, We have the upper hand going into this. Salama: But at the same time, the same is true in China, right? I mean there are inflationary pressures in China, and economically, Xi is up against a wall as well. I think they have a different kind of government and a different kind of society and so it may not threaten his regime in the same way that the administration would politically face consequences for something like that. But it is definitely something that weighs heavily on his mind as he comes to Washington. Harris: We’re talking a lot about Trump and China, but there are gonna be a lot of world leaders who are here in New York City. As they’re meeting this week, what are some of the things that you’re going to be paying attention to in this split-screen week of meetings? Salama: There’s so much. The UN General Assembly for a long time has not been as relevant as it once was. But there is this sense, on the theme that we’re talking about, about this departure of alliances, or the fracturing of traditional alliances from the post–World War II era, and whether or not the United States can be depended upon. Other things to watch out for—obviously the Iranians coming to town are going to lay out their case for the United Nations on the world stage to hear from them, and to hear where they stand on this war, is probably going to be interesting, and so we’ll watch out for that. The Iranians have traditionally set off fireworks at the United Nations, and this year certainly will be no different. The Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu, is scheduled to speak later this week, and he is in an election season right now. He’s up for reelection next month. And with the Iran war and just the sentiment toward the Israeli government that has been souring it, not just in the United States but around the world—I think his comments are going to be interesting to watch. I do just want to also note, the Trump administration has been down on the UN in particular as an international body. Ambassador Mike Waltz, who used to be a Florida congressman and was very aligned with Trump, has really set out to lay out the case that the Trump administration makes that the UN is basically irrelevant and is not operating in the way it should be. And there are a lot of countries around the world who agree with him that the UN was in need of desperate reform, and so that’s also going to be an interesting sidebar to watch about the relevance of the United Nations in the current era and whether or not it actually serves the purposes that it once did, to unite and basically uphold international law and humanitarian issues. So we’ll watch out for that as well. Harris: And Rogé, same question to you. What are some of the things that you’re going to be thinking about and reporting on as the week moves ahead? Karma: I think the single biggest thing that I’m going to be watching is the language around AI. This is the issue that I think has been front of mind for a lot of legislators in the U.S. And as I was saying earlier, there is only one real way to engineer a global AI slowdown if that is really what people are worried about, and it is a U.S.-China deal. And I think the general view going into this is that neither Donald Trump or Xi Jinping are very amenable to this kind of deal. But already, the fact that I was reading this morning that Secretary Bessent and his counterpart were talking about an AI warning system, I think that is a signal that members of both governments are taking this more seriously. And I’ll just be very interested in what comes out of this, in part because on so many of these issues we’re talking about—whether tariffs are one; economic relations are another—there has been so much conversation for so long that it’s hard to imagine anything very substantive happening. Like, for example, the U.S. and China came to their trade truce that involved China purchasing a bunch of U.S. soybeans—China hasn’t been purchasing the amount of soybeans. There has been in a lot of these meetings this economic dance that goes back and forth, where Trump tries to pin down China with commitments; China sort of skirts them. That’s more, for me, more predictable, and I could see it happening again. With AI, this is a much more open space. It’s much more amenable and in flux. And so I am actually going to be interested in what both sides say, what positions they stake, and what, if anything, they can agree to—even if it’s just some rhetoric around what even the nature of the problem is. Harris: Well, Vivian, Rogé, there will be a lot to watch out for this week, and we will be reading your reporting as it goes along. Thank you so much for joining us. Salama: Thanks, Adam. Karma: Appreciate you having us. [ Music ] Harris: That’s all for today’s show. This episode of Radio Atlantic was produced by Mike Pesoli and edited by Hadley Robinson. It was engineered by Miguel Carrascal and has original music by Rob Smierciak. Claudine Ebeid is the executive producer of Atlantic Audio, and Andrea Valdez is our managing editor. If you like what you saw here, new episodes of Radio Atlantic drop every Monday and Thursday. You can subscribe on The Atlantic ’s YouTube page, on Apple or Spotify, or wherever it is you get your podcasts. And if you want to support this work and the work of my colleagues, you can subscribe to the publication at TheAtlantic.com/Listener. Until next time, I’m Adam Harris.

items.title: "Viser juste" d’Adèle Haenel : écrire pour se reconstruire
items.description: Elle a quitté le cinéma pour retrouver sa liberté. Aujourd’hui, Adèle Haenel revient avec "Viser juste", son premier livre, un texte hybride dans lequel elle explore les violences sexistes et sexuelles qu’elle a subies, mais aussi les mécanismes du silence, du déni et de la reconstruction. De son enfance à ses années d’actrice, de ses rôles marquants à son engagement contre les violences faites aux femmes, elle interroge ce qui l’a longtemps éloignée d’elle-même. Une "enquête sur sa propre disparition", comme elle la décrit.

items.title: Taux directeur inchangé : Bank Al-Maghrib mise sur la résilience marocaine
items.description: Bank Al-Maghrib a décidé de maintenir son taux directeur à 2,25 %, à l’issue de la troisième réunion trimestrielle de son Conseil au titre de 2026, tenue ce mardi 22 septembre. La Banque centrale justifie cette décision par des perspectives d’inflation qui demeurent modérées et par la consolidation attendue de l’activité économique non agricole, tout en soulignant le niveau « très élevé » des incertitudes entourant les perspectives économiques. Le Conseil de Bank Al-Maghrib a consacré sa réunion à l’examen de l’évolution de la conjoncture économique, des développements récents sur les plans externe et interne ainsi que de ses projections macroéconomiques à moyen terme. Dans son diagnostic, l’institution relève un environnement international marqué par la recrudescence des hostilités au Moyen-Orient et l’enlisement du conflit russo-ukrainien. Ces tensions continuent de perturber les chaînes de production et d’approvisionnement, notamment pour les produits énergétiques et alimentaires ainsi que pour certains intrants essentiels. Cette situation s’accompagne d’une remontée volatile des cours des matières premières et d’une accélération de l’inflation au niveau mondial. La croissance internationale demeure toutefois relativement résiliente, soutenue notamment par les investissements liés à l’intelligence artificielle et par la progression des dépenses publiques, en particulier dans la défense. Une inflation encore contenue au Maroc Au Maroc, les effets de cet environnement extérieur défavorable se manifestent principalement à travers la hausse des importations de produits énergétiques et le rythme d’activité de certaines industries dépendantes d’intrants importés. L’impact de la flambée des prix de l’énergie sur les prix domestiques reste toutefois limité, notamment grâce aux subventions accordées aux professionnels du transport routier et au maintien des prix du gaz butane et de l’électricité. Dans ce contexte, l’inflation est restée faible, à 0,3 % en moyenne au cours des huit premiers mois de 2026, en partie sous l’effet de la baisse des prix de certains produits alimentaires. Bank Al-Maghrib prévoit une inflation moyenne de 0,7 % sur l’ensemble de 2026, avant une remontée à 1,5 % en 2027. Cette progression serait principalement portée par l’inflation sous-jacente, qui passerait de -0,2 % en 2026 à 2,2 % en 2027. La Banque centrale explique cette évolution par la dissipation de l’effet de la contraction de la composante alimentaire, notamment celle liée aux prix de l’huile d’olive, ainsi que par la persistance de l’inflation importée à un niveau relativement élevé. Les anticipations d’inflation restent, pour leur part, bien ancrées : les experts du secteur financier tablent sur une moyenne de 2,1 % à l’horizon de huit trimestres et de 2,2 % à celui de douze trimestres. Une croissance attendue à 4,4 % en 2026 Sur le front de l’activité, Bank Al-Maghrib anticipe une progression de 4,4 % de l’économie nationale en 2026, après 4,9 % en 2025, avant un ralentissement à 2,9 % en 2027. Cette évolution recouvre des trajectoires différentes entre les secteurs. La valeur ajoutée agricole devrait rebondir de 16 % cette année, portée notamment par une récolte céréalière estimée à 93 millions de quintaux, selon le Département de l’Agriculture. Elle reculerait ensuite de 7,6 % en 2027, sous l’hypothèse d’un retour à une production céréalière moyenne de 50 millions de quintaux. Du côté des activités non agricoles, la croissance devrait ralentir de 4,5 % en 2025 à 3,1 % en 2026, notamment en raison d’une évolution moins favorable que prévu dans certaines branches, parmi lesquelles les industries extractives et manufacturières. Elle remonterait toutefois à 4 % en 2027. Le marché du travail conserve parallèlement une dynamique positive. Les données du HCP relatives au deuxième trimestre 2026 font état de 406.000 créations nettes d’emplois sur un an, tandis que le taux de chômage au sens strict est revenu à 9,5 %, avec 11,9 % dans les villes et 5,4 % en milieu rural. La facture énergétique repart fortement à la hausse Les comptes extérieurs devraient en revanche subir davantage la hausse des prix des hydrocarbures et de certains intrants, ainsi que le maintien à un niveau élevé des importations de biens d’équipement, dans un contexte de poursuite de l’investissement. La facture énergétique devrait ainsi augmenter de 28,4 % en 2026, à 138,1 milliards de dirhams, avant de revenir à 116 milliards en 2027. Les achats de produits bruts progresseraient de 53,4 % cette année, tandis que les acquisitions de biens d’équipement augmenteraient de 15,6 %, pour atteindre 250,7 milliards de dirhams. Les exportations devraient néanmoins bénéficier de plusieurs relais. Les ventes de phosphate et de ses dérivés progresseraient de 9,7 % en 2026, soutenues notamment par la hausse des cours des engrais, avant une progression de 12,1 % en 2027, à 122,6 milliards de dirhams. Les exportations automobiles devraient, quant à elles, reprendre progressivement pour atteindre 202,2 milliards de dirhams en 2027. Les recettes de voyages poursuivraient également leur progression, à 160 milliards de dirhams en 2027, tandis que les transferts des Marocains résidant à l’étranger atteindraient 136,3 milliards la même année. Malgré ces évolutions, le déficit du compte courant devrait se creuser de 2,4 % du PIB en 2025 à 4,6 % en 2026, avant de revenir à 3 % en 2027. Les réserves dépasseraient 500 MMDH Les avoirs officiels de réserve continueraient toutefois de se renforcer. Bank Al-Maghrib les projette à 502,8 milliards de dirhams à fin 2026, puis à 515,3 milliards à fin 2027, soit l’équivalent de cinq mois et demi d’importations de biens et services. Les recettes d’IDE sont, pour leur part, projetées à un niveau annuel équivalent à 3,5 % du PIB. Sur le plan monétaire, le besoin de liquidité des banques devrait continuer à augmenter sous l’effet notamment de la hausse prévue de la circulation fiduciaire, pour atteindre 168,2 milliards de dirhams en 2027. Le crédit bancaire au secteur non financier devrait, lui, accélérer nettement en 2026, avec une croissance projetée à 8,1 %, contre 4,8 % en 2025, avant de revenir à 6,1 % en 2027. Un environnement international plus inflationniste Les projections de BAM intègrent également une hausse sensible des prix du pétrole. Le Brent passerait d’une moyenne de 68,2 dollars le baril en 2025 à 87,2 dollars en 2026, avant de revenir à 73,5 dollars en 2027. Les cours des engrais phosphatés devraient également rester élevés cette année, sous l’effet notamment du renchérissement des principaux intrants et du maintien des restrictions chinoises sur les exportations d’engrais phosphatés. Pour les produits d’origine marocaine, le prix du DAP est projeté à 860 dollars la tonne en moyenne en 2026, contre 713 dollars en 2025, avant un recul à 803 dollars en 2027. Dans le même temps, la croissance mondiale devrait ralentir, passant de 3,2 % en 2025 à 3 % en 2026, puis 2,9 % en 2027. L’inflation mondiale progresserait de 2,9 % à 3,4 % entre 2025 et 2026, avant de revenir à 3,2 % en 2027. Cette toile de fond explique aussi la prudence de Bank Al-Maghrib. La Banque centrale identifie parmi les principaux facteurs d’incertitude la persistance des conflits et des tensions géoéconomiques, les risques pesant sur l’approvisionnement en énergie, en produits alimentaires et en intrants essentiels, mais également la remontée des rendements souverains et les manifestations plus prononcées du changement climatique. Au niveau interne, les conditions climatiques et l’orientation future de la politique économique constituent également des sources d’incertitude. Sur cette base, le Conseil a donc jugé approprié de maintenir le taux directeur à 2,25 %, tout en indiquant qu’il continuera à suivre étroitement l’évolution de la conjoncture externe et interne et à fonder ses décisions, réunion par réunion, sur les données les plus actualisées. Enfin, sur les finances publiques, l’exécution budgétaire des huit premiers mois de l’année fait ressortir une hausse de 9,6 % des recettes ordinaires et de 10,5 % des dépenses globales, ces dernières étant notamment tirées par les dépenses de biens et services et les intérêts de la dette. Bank Al-Maghrib projette le déficit budgétaire, hors produits de cession des participations de l’État, à 3,4 % du PIB en 2026, puis à 3,5 % en 2027. The post Taux directeur inchangé : Bank Al-Maghrib mise sur la résilience marocaine appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Kankan : une moto volée depuis quatre mois retrouvée grâce à son numéro de châssis
items.description: Volée en pleine nuit dans une cour familiale à Kankan, une moto a été retrouvée quatre mois plus tard grâce à son numéro de châssis. Signalé après le vol puis bloqué dans le système d’immatriculation, l’engin a été identifié lors d’un contrôle avant d’être restitué à son propriétaire. Une affaire qui souligne l’importance de l’immatriculation et de la vérification des motos d’occasion. Quatre mois après la disparition de sa moto, Thierno Lao Baldé a finalement récupéré son engin. La moto avait été volée de nuit dans la cour familiale du propriétaire, dans le quartier Mobile, à Kankan. Après le signalement du vol, son numéro de châssis a été enregistré et bloqué dans le système d’immatriculation. C’est ce dispositif qui a permis son identification plusieurs mois plus tard. « Je suis très content. Cela fait quatre mois que la moto a été volée. Ils l’ont volée la nuit dans notre cour. Je l’avais laissée dans la cour, en oubliant de la faire rentrer », témoigne Thierno Lao Baldé. Pour lui, cette expérience montre l’importance de faire immatriculer son engin. « Tout le monde doit prendre la plaque d’immatriculation. Même si ta moto est volée, on peut la retrouver. Si je n’avais pas immatriculé ma moto, je n’allais pas la retrouver », ajoute-t-il. Le numéro de châssis au cœur du dispositif Selon Mme Kaba Fatoumata baloka, coordonnatrice régionale du DSD de Kankan, le numéro de châssis constitue un élément essentiel dans le suivi des engins signalés volés. Après une déclaration auprès de la police ou de la gendarmerie, le propriétaire doit se présenter au centre d’immatriculation avec le document attestant le vol. Le numéro de châssis est alors enregistré et bloqué dans le système. « En bloquant le numéro de châssis, la moto ne peut plus être immatriculée sur toute l’étendue du territoire guinéen », explique la responsable. Dans le cas de la moto de Thierno Lao Baldé, cette procédure avait été appliquée après la déclaration du vol. Quelques mois plus tard, l’engin a été intercepté lors d’un contrôle. Les vérifications effectuées sur le numéro de châssis ont permis de constater qu’il correspondait à la moto déclarée volée. Après les enquêtes et les vérifications nécessaires, l’engin a été restitué à son propriétaire, quatre mois après sa disparition. Plus de dix motos retrouvées, selon la coordination Mme Kaba Fatoumata baloka affirme que le dispositif a déjà permis de retrouver plusieurs motos depuis sa prise de fonction à la tête de la coordination régionale. « À Kankan, depuis que je suis là, on a retrouvé au minimum plus de dix motos. Et toutes les motos retrouvées sont remises à leurs propriétaires », affirme-t-elle. La responsable précise que le rôle du service est notamment de contribuer à la sécurisation des engins et à la protection de leurs propriétaires. « Nous ne sommes pas là contre la population. Nous sommes là pour la population, pour la sécurisation de leurs biens », insiste-t-elle. Prudence lors de l’achat d’une moto d’occasion Au-delà du vol, la responsable attire l’attention des acheteurs sur les motos d’occasion dont les numéros de châssis pourraient avoir été modifiés ou falsifiés. Elle recommande aux personnes souhaitant acheter un engin d’occasion de procéder aux vérifications nécessaires avant toute transaction. « Avant d’acheter une moto, regardez si le châssis est bien. Si le châssis n’est pas bien, n’achetez pas la moto », conseille-t-elle. Elle invite notamment les acheteurs à se rapprocher du centre d’immatriculation pour vérifier l’engin et sa situation administrative avant de conclure la vente. Une moto dont le numéro de châssis présente des anomalies peut en effet poser des difficultés à son acquéreur, notamment si elle est liée à un vol. L’immatriculation comme moyen de suivi Dans le cas de la moto retrouvée à Kankan, les démarches administratives liées à l’immatriculation ont donc permis de faire le lien entre l’engin intercepté et son propriétaire. Après les vérifications nécessaires, la plaque d’immatriculation et les documents pourront être rétablis, selon la procédure administrative applicable. Pour Thierno Lao Baldé, quatre mois après le vol, le dénouement de cette affaire constitue surtout un rappel pour les propriétaires de motos : immatriculer son engin, conserver ses documents et signaler rapidement tout vol peuvent faciliter les recherches. Du côté des acheteurs, la vérification du numéro de châssis et de la situation administrative d’une moto d’occasion reste également une précaution importante avant toute transaction. items.title: Belgique : un chat risque l’expulsion vers l’Algérie
items.description: L’histoire peut paraître invraisemblable, mais elle est réelle. Un chat ramené d'Algérie par son propriétaire est sous la menace d’une expulsion du territoire belge pour défaut de vaccination. Une affaire qui illustre les excès de la réglementation européenne, non pas dans le domaine d’immigration évidemment, mais en matière de normes sanitaires. Un chat « Algérien » indésirable en Belgique L’histoire démontre aussi le poids des préjugés en Europe vis-à-vis des pays du Sud. Le litige est porté jusque devant le Conseil d'Etat. Selon le média local L’Avenir, Le chat, un siamois de 9 mois dénommé Robert, avait été ramené d’Algérie et mis en vente sur une plateforme en ligne spécialisée. En mai dernier, une femme de la ville de Mons, en Wallonie, a repéré l’annonce et acquis l’animal pour 600 euros. Les choses se sont déroulées normalement jusqu’à ce qu'un vétérinaire se rende compte que le chat n’est ni vacciné ni pucé, ce qui contrevient aux règles de l’Union européenne. L’administration belge propose 3 solutions dont le renvoi du chat en Algérie Il alerte aussitôt l’AFSCA, l’organisme belge de sécurité de la chaîne alimentaire. Vu que l’animal n’a pas été vacciné à temps, l’organisme a proposé trois solutions : le confiner pendant 4 mois, l'euthanasier ou le renvoyer en Algérie, indique pour sa part la RTBF. L’administration a fondé sa décision sur un préjugé totalement faux : selon elle, il y aurait “un grand nombre de foyers de rage sur le sol algérien”. La propriétaire ne souhaite pas se séparer de son chat, rejetant catégoriquement les options de l'euthanasie et de l’expulsion qu'elle juge “radicales pour un chaton de 9 mois”. Il lui reste le confinement, mais cela coûte cher, 50 euros la journée. Sur quatre mois, cela fait une petite fortune. Même l'idée d’un confinement à domicile est refusée par l’administration qui estime que cela est “irresponsable pour la vie animale et humaine”. Selon la RTBF, la dame a tenté de casser la décision devant le Conseil d'Etat, mais sans succès. L’article Belgique : un chat risque l’expulsion vers l’Algérie est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Netanyahu says will 'tell the truth' on Israel's actions at United Nations
items.description: JERUSALEM, Sept 22 (Reuters) - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Tuesday he would use his speech at the United Nations this week to defend Israel's military actions against the Palestinians, while accusing New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani of supporting Hamas. Netanyahu's comments were in response to remarks by the New York mayor, who told CNN on Monday that Netanyahu was a "war criminal and an architect of a horrific genocide of the Palestinian people". items.title: Labé : le respect du protocole d’accord sur l’engagement des enseignants contractuels préoccupe un syndicaliste
items.description: À quelques jours de l’ouverture des classes, la question de l’engagement des enseignants contractuels à la fonction publique continue de susciter des interrogations. À Labé, un responsable syndical estime que l’État doit respecter les engagements pris dans le protocole d’accord signé le 3 janvier 2026. Rencontré le 21 septembre à Labé, Mamoudou Keita, secrétaire général de la Coordination régionale des enseignants contractuels de Labé, s’est dit préoccupé par la situation. Selon lui, plusieurs étapes prévues dans le cadre du protocole d’accord ont déjà été franchies, mais l’engagement des enseignants concernés à la fonction publique reste encore en attente. « Après la signature du protocole d’accord le 3 janvier 2026, on avait demandé qu’il y ait des commissions qui doivent œuvrer pour le respect des points du protocole d’accord. Ces commissions ont été mises en place en avril, après plusieurs grognes des syndicats pour menacer la tenue des examens afin que ces commissions soient mises en place », explique-t-il. Parmi les commissions mises en place figure celle chargée de la vérification et de l’élaboration de la liste des enseignants contractuels ayant fait la biométrie, la pratique de classe et obtenu une moyenne d’au moins 10 sur 20. « Cette commission a travaillé et cela nous laisse croire que le travail est déjà fini. Tout ce qui reste, c’est au ministère de la Fonction publique de faire son devoir par rapport aux engagements déjà pris, chose qui n’est pas encore faite », regrette le syndicaliste. 4 573 enseignants concernés Selon Mamoudou Keita, 4 573 enseignants contractuels sont concernés par cette attente d’engagement à la fonction publique. Des enseignants qui, selon lui, disposent d’une expérience de terrain acquise au cours de plusieurs années d’exercice. Le responsable syndical plaide ainsi pour leur prise en charge par l’État et appelle les autorités à respecter les engagements pris. « Actuellement, nous sommes en conclave, on tient des réunions pour voir ce qu’il y a lieu de faire par rapport à la mise en œuvre du protocole d’accord. Il y a une menace qui surgit du côté du ministère de la Fonction publique, mais on se prépare pour contrecarrer cette menace qui empêcherait le respect du protocole d’accord. Chose qui sera dévoilée au moment venu », annonce-t-il. Face à cette situation, Mamoudou Keita appelle également les enseignants contractuels à rester unis et patients. « Je lance un appel aux enseignants contractuels à l’union, à l’écoute et à la patience pour atteindre l’objectif qu’on s’est fixé, c’est-à-dire l’intégration à la fonction publique. Au gouvernement, je demande de respecter ses engagements qui ont été pris pour éviter des grognes sociales », conclut-il. À quelques jours de la rentrée scolaire, les enseignants contractuels attendent donc la concrétisation des engagements pris par l’État. Le syndicaliste appelle les autorités à agir afin d’éviter de nouvelles tensions sociales. Alpha Moussa Dieng, correspondant régional à Labé L’article Labé : le respect du protocole d’accord sur l’engagement des enseignants contractuels préoccupe un syndicaliste est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
